summary: Write, from the code, how a tester reaches each Web item, using the cheap model
logs: paths: 1702 items returned for 1698 asked; 0 areas returned nothing

items.where: Site address / (signed out, private window)
steps: Open the site root address in a private browser window, signed out.
Look at the first screen for the 'Try chat' button and the Desktop call to action beside it.
Compare with Expected: sign-in, try and download calls to action are visible on the homepage.
items.needs: none for the signed-out check; a Free account for the signed-in check
items.note: An earlier run recorded that a signed-in visit to / showed Something Went Wrong (E085); the signed-out homepage was not tested earlier.

items.where: Products > Chat
steps: Click the Products menu in the header.
Click Chat.
Read the page headline and the paragraph about chatting with eligible models.
Compare with Expected: the page explains the chat assistant and has a 'Try chat' button to start.
items.needs: none

items.where: Footer > Capabilities > Deep research
steps: Scroll to the footer and find the Capabilities column.
Click Deep research.
Look for the section 'Review and edit before you start' and the cited-report explanation.
Compare with Expected: the page explains deep research with cited reports and how to use it.
items.needs: none
items.note: Deep research is not in the header menu; it is reached from the footer or the sitemap.

items.where: Products > Work
steps: Click the Products menu in the header.
Click Work.
Read the menu description 'A goal in, a plan first, approvals on sensitive steps' and the page that opens.
Compare with Expected: the page presents agentic work and has a way to start.
items.needs: none

items.where: Products > Code
steps: Click the Products menu in the header.
Click Code.
Read the menu description 'One coding agent across the CLI and VS Code' and the page that opens.
Compare with Expected: the page presents the coding agent and how to get it.
items.needs: none

items.where: Products > Desktop
steps: Click the Products menu in the header.
Click Desktop.
Read the page on what the desktop app does and which platforms it covers.
Compare with Expected: the page describes the desktop app truthfully, including availability and download.
items.needs: none
items.note: The download page reports Windows and Linux installers as not published (apps/web/app/download/DesktopDownloadAvailability.tsx); compare the Desktop page wording with that.

items.where: Products > Mobile
steps: Click the Products menu in the header.
Click Mobile.
Read the page on the mobile app and its availability.
Compare with Expected: the page describes the mobile app and its availability.
items.needs: none

items.where: Products > CLI
steps: Click the Products menu in the header.
Click CLI.
Find the install section and the install command, if the page shows one.
Compare with Expected: the page tells a visitor how to install the CLI and offers a working install.
items.needs: none
items.note: The install command is shown only when a release is published; otherwise the page says 'No signed release is published yet, so there is no install command to run.' (apps/web/app/cli/CliInstallCommand.tsx), which differs from a working-install expectation if no release exists.

items.where: Products > Code for VS Code
steps: Click the Products menu in the header.
Click Code for VS Code.
Read the page describing the extension and its availability.
Compare with Expected: the page describes the IDE extension and where it is available.
items.needs: none
items.note: The menu text is built in nav.ts from the product name plus ' for VS Code', so the exact visible text is composed, not stored as one string.

items.where: Products > Extension
steps: Click the Products menu in the header.
Click Extension.
Read the page describing the browser extension and its availability.
Compare with Expected: the page describes the browser extension and its availability.
items.needs: none
items.note: The footer names the same page 'Chrome' under Surfaces (apps/web/features/marketing/components/system/nav.ts).

items.where: Resources > MCP directory
steps: Click the Resources menu in the header.
Click MCP directory.
Type a server name in the search box and read the results.
Open one listing and read its publisher and listed tools.
Compare with Expected: the logged-out visitor can browse and search the integration directory.
items.needs: none
items.note: Connecting a server asks for sign-in; browsing and searching do not, per the page copy in apps/web/app/connectors/mcp-directory/page.tsx.

items.where: Sitemap > Product > Plugins
steps: Scroll to the bottom of the page and click Sitemap.
Under Product, click Plugins.
Browse the plugin catalogue and click one plugin name.
Compare with Expected: a logged-out visitor can browse the catalogue with a path to install.
items.needs: none
items.note: The catalogue is read from the live registry (apps/web/features/plugins/server/registry-source.ts); what the page shows when the registry is empty or fails was not read.

items.where: Resources > Skills
steps: Click the Resources menu in the header or scroll to the footer Resources column.
Click Skills.
Look for the heading 'Skills live in your workspace' and the skill list.
Compare with Expected: a logged-out visitor sees a public skill directory.
items.needs: none
items.note: An earlier run recorded that /skills opened Settings > Skills for a signed-in user; the signed-out directory in apps/web/app/skills/SignedOutSkills.tsx was not tested earlier.

items.where: Sitemap > Product > Gallery
steps: Scroll to the bottom of the page and click Sitemap.
Under Product, click Gallery.
Look at the template cards and the 'Start from scratch' option.
Compare with Expected: the gallery offers curated templates that can be previewed and launched into chat.
items.needs: none
items.note: The launch path is in apps/web/app/gallery/GalleryClient.tsx; some line references in the audit moved, so the launch behaviour was not checked against a live page.

items.where: Sitemap > Product > Plugins, then click a plugin name
steps: Scroll to the bottom of the page and click Sitemap.
Under Product, click Plugins, then click any plugin name.
On its page read the Version line, the Install section and the Releases section.
Compare with Expected: description, install info and release history are shown.
items.needs: none
items.note: The detail page has no 'Permissions' heading in the code; it has Skills and Capabilities sections instead.

items.where: Sitemap > Product > Gallery, then click a template
steps: Scroll to the bottom of the page and click Sitemap.
Under Product, click Gallery, then click any template card.
Check that the page address shows /gallery/ followed by the template name.
Compare with Expected: each template has its own previewable page at its own address.
items.needs: none
items.note: The template address is built in apps/web/app/gallery/inspiration.ts as /gallery/<id>.

items.where: Footer > Product > Pricing
steps: Scroll to the footer and find the Product column.
Click Pricing.
Read the individual plan cards, their prices and the plan names.
Click a paid plan's button and stop at the checkout or sign-in step. Do not complete a purchase.
Compare with Expected: individual plans and prices are listed, and a plan can be chosen.
items.needs: none to view; a Free account to reach the checkout step
items.note: Paid plan buttons open checkout; the tester must stop before payment.

items.where: Solutions > Teams
steps: Click the Solutions menu in the header.
Click Teams.
Click the button that starts at the minimum seat count, which opens the Team pricing section.
Choose a seat count and read the per-seat price.
Compare with Expected: per-seat pricing is shown, and the buyer can choose seats. Stop before paying.
items.needs: none to view; a Free account to reach the checkout step
items.note: The Teams page button text is built from a seat constant, so its exact words are composed; 'Get Team' is the pricing page's button key.

items.where: Solutions > Enterprise
steps: Click the Solutions menu in the header.
Click Enterprise.
Look for the 'Start the evaluation' section and its contact or sales button.
Compare with Expected: the Enterprise offering is presented with a sales path. Do not submit the form.
items.needs: none

items.where: Footer > Product > Pricing, then scroll to Compare plans
steps: Scroll to the footer and click Pricing under Product.
Scroll to the 'Compare plans' section.
Read the rows and the plan columns.
Compare each cell with Expected: the cell should match what the plan allows.
items.needs: none
items.note: The audit's line references for the comparison data moved; the table cells were not traced to enforcement code here.

items.where: Footer > Resources > Help, then open 'Usage limits, credits and top-ups'
steps: Scroll to the footer and click Help under Resources.
Open the article 'Usage limits, credits and top-ups'.
Read how usage is measured and what happens when an allowance runs out.
Also open Pricing and read the sentence 'Weekly and monthly usage allowances apply.'
Compare with Expected: public pages explain managed usage, allowances and credits.
items.needs: none

items.where: Products > Downloads
steps: Click the Products menu in the header.
Click Downloads.
Read the Mac download buttons and the platform notes.
Compare with Expected: installers are offered per platform and architecture, and only what is published is shown.
items.needs: none
items.note: The page states that Windows and Linux installers are not published (apps/web/app/download/DesktopDownloadAvailability.tsx).

items.where: Resources > Release notes
steps: Click the Resources menu in the header.
Click Release notes.
Look for the heading 'Releases, newest first.' and the dated release rows.
Compare with Expected: a public changelog lists dated releases.
items.needs: none
items.note: The same page is also served at /changelog (apps/web/app/changelog/page.tsx) without a menu link.

items.where: Resources > Release notes, then click a release
steps: Click the Resources menu in the header, then Release notes.
Click the title of any release.
Check that the page shows that release and a button named 'All release notes'.
Compare with Expected: each announcement has its own public page.
items.needs: none

items.where: Resources > Documentation
steps: Click the Resources menu in the header.
Click Documentation.
Read the guide index and look for the API docs link.
Compare with Expected: the documentation portal indexes guides and API docs.
items.needs: none

items.where: Footer > Resources > Help, then type in "Search help articles"
steps: Scroll to the footer and click "Help" under Resources (logged out or signed in).
Click the box labelled "Search help articles" and type a word such as "temporary".
Wait for the results list and click one result.
Check that the article opens at its own address and shows readable article text, compared with Expected (searchable articles).
items.needs: none
items.note: The help page heading reads "Get unstuck, fast." and the search is a client component that calls /api/help/search.

items.where: Resources > Status (header menu) or Footer > Resources > Status
steps: Open the "Resources" menu in the header, or scroll to the footer.
Click "Status".
Read the status heading and the list of checks, with the time each check ran.
Compare with Expected (current health from live checks). The page says model inference and a chat turn are not tested.
items.needs: none
items.note: Health labels such as "Checks passing" and "Some checks failing" are in apps/web/app/status/page.tsx; the page is force-dynamic.

items.where: Resources > Trust centre (header menu) or Footer > Legal > Trust centre
steps: Open the "Resources" menu in the header and click "Trust centre".
Read the page heading "Claims with dates, and the ones we cannot make."
Scroll to the rows and the "Check the live health signal" item, which links to /status.
Compare with Expected (security posture and data handling are explained).
items.needs: none
items.note: The heading text is in apps/web/app/trust/page.tsx.

items.where: Resources > About (header menu) or Footer > Company > About
steps: Open the "Resources" menu in the header and click "About".
Read the heading "Multi-provider, by design."
Scroll to the company description that starts "AGI is built by".
Compare with Expected (product and company information is shown).
items.needs: none

items.where: Resources > Contact (header menu) or Footer > Company > Contact
steps: Open the "Resources" menu in the header and click "Contact".
Read the heading "One inbox, one human." and the email address shown on the page.
Scroll to "Draft it here, send it from your mail app." and check the composer fields are present.
Compare with Expected (a visitor can reach the company). Do not press the send button: it opens the mail app.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Draft it here, send it from your mail app.

items.note: The contact page composer opens a pre-filled mail draft; it does not store the message.

items.where: Products > Desktop (footer Surfaces > Desktop) > "Discuss Enterprise access"
steps: Open the Desktop page from the footer under Surfaces, labelled "Desktop".
Click the button labelled "Discuss Enterprise access".
In the dialog titled "Discuss Enterprise access", check the email field and the wording about contract-scoped Enterprise access.
Compare with Expected (a prospect can request an Enterprise conversation). Do not submit unless testing storage is allowed; the success text is "You're on the list."
items.needs: none
items.note: The form dialog is apps/web/features/marketing/components/WaitlistDialog.tsx. The Enterprise page's own button "Contact sales" goes to an email page, not this form, and the /waitlist route exists in apps/web/app but its link was not traced. I did not confirm the desktop button renders the trigger.

items.where: Footer > bottom legal row: "Privacy", "Terms", "Cookies", "Accessibility"
steps: Scroll to the bottom of any public page to the legal row of the footer.
Click "Terms", then go back and click "Privacy", then "Cookies", then "Accessibility".
Check each page opens with a heading and readable body text.
Compare with Expected (all four pages exist and are linked site-wide).
items.needs: none
items.note: The footer legal nav has aria-label "Legal" in apps/web/features/marketing/components/system/MarketingFooter.tsx.

items.where: Signed-in chat > open a conversation > conversation title menu > "Share…" > "Share conversation"; then open the link in a signed-out private window
steps: Sign in, open a conversation in chat, and open its title menu.
Click "Share…", then choose a public link and create it (the dialog title reads "Share conversation" until a link exists).
Copy the link, then open it in a private window while signed out.
Check that the shared conversation appears read-only with its messages, compared with Expected (a logged-out visitor sees shared content).
items.needs: a signed-in account with a conversation, and a private browser window
items.note: The exact button that opens the title menu was not traced. Expired or non-live links return not found (apps/web/app/share/[token]/page.tsx).

items.where: Signed out: "Log in or sign up" screen > "Email address" > "Continue"
steps: Sign out, or open the app while signed out.
Type your account email in "Email address".
Click "Continue".
Enter your password (or the emailed code) and click "Continue".
Look for the signed-in chat page, which means the session was issued.
items.needs: an existing account with a password or email code
items.note: The same screen serves /login and /signup. Provider and passkey buttons appear above the email field when configured.

items.where: Signed out: "Log in or sign up" screen > "Email address" > "Continue" (use an address with no account)
steps: Open the sign-up address (/signup) or sign out.
Type an email address that has no account in "Email address".
Click "Continue".
Follow the next step, which can be "Create a password".
Look for the account being created and the next step (email confirmation).
items.needs: an email address that has no account yet
items.note: There is no separate "Create account" button in the code. /signup renders the same screen as sign-in.

items.where: Signed out: "Log in or sign up" > new "Email address" > "Continue" > "Check your inbox" screen
steps: Sign up with an email address that has no account.
Look for the "Check your inbox" screen and the "We sent a code to" line with your address.
Open your email and find the code.
Enter it in "Code" and click "Continue".
Check that the account is usable after the code is accepted.
items.needs: a new email address you can read
items.note: The order of sign-up steps is set by the server response, so the exact screen order is not fixed in the code.

items.where: "Check your inbox" screen > "Code" field (reach it with "Try another way to sign in" > "Email me a code" when a password is offered)
steps: Reach the "Check your inbox" screen.
Type a wrong code in "Code" and click "Continue"; look for the error.
Click "Resend code" and look for the "Resend code in" countdown.
Enter the newest emailed code (autofill from the email app is offered by the field) and click "Continue".
Look for the signed-in result.
items.needs: an email account you can read
items.note: This screen takes emailed codes. Authenticator codes are entered on the "Confirm it is you" screen (S3.14).

items.where: "Log in or sign up" > "Email address" > "Continue" > "Enter your password" > "Forgot password?"
steps: Type the email of an account that has a password and click "Continue".
On "Enter your password" click "Forgot password?".
Look for the "Check your inbox" screen with the "We sent a code to" line.
Open the email inbox and look for the reset code.
items.needs: an account with a password and access to its email

items.where: "Forgot password?" > "Check your inbox" > "Code" > "Continue" > "Set a new password"
steps: Enter the reset code from the email in "Code" and click "Continue".
On "Set a new password" type a new password in "New password".
Read the rule line about minimum length and breach checks.
Click "Continue".
Look for being signed in after the new password is set.
items.needs: the reset code from the email

items.where: Signed out: "Log in or sign up" screen > "Continue with Google" or "Continue with GitHub" (buttons above the email field)
steps: Sign out and open the sign-in screen.
Look for the provider buttons above "Email address".
Click "Continue with Google" (or GitHub).
Finish the provider sign-in in the provider window.
Look for the signed-in chat page.
items.needs: a Google or GitHub account
items.note: The provider list comes from AGI_AUTH_PROVIDERS and defaults to Google and GitHub. Microsoft and Apple are also defined.

items.where: Signed out: "Log in or sign up" > "Email address" (an organization address) > "Continue"
steps: Type an email address of an SSO-enabled organization in "Email address".
Click "Continue".
Look for the message "This address belongs to an organization. Taking you to its sign-in".
Finish the organization sign-in in the browser when asked, then look for the signed-in result.
items.needs: an account in an SSO-enabled organization

labels.text: This address belongs to an organization. Taking you to its sign-in

items.note: No separate SSO button exists in the code. The SSO start is triggered by the email step.

items.where: "Log in or sign up" > "Email address" (a work email) > "Continue"; the effect shows as the organization message
steps: Type a work email whose domain belongs to a verified organization.
Click "Continue".
Look for the message "This address belongs to an organization. Taking you to its sign-in" and the redirect to the organization sign-in.
items.needs: a work email on a verified organization domain

labels.text: This address belongs to an organization. Taking you to its sign-in

items.note: The domain check runs on the server (apps/web/lib/services/organization-verified-domains.ts); the screen only shows its result.

items.where: Settings > Security > "Passkeys" > "Add a passkey"
steps: Sign in, then open Settings.
Click "Security" in the Settings list.
Find the "Passkeys" heading and click "Add a passkey".
Complete the device or browser passkey prompt.
Look for the new passkey listed; click "Rename" or "Remove" on it to check those controls.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a browser or device that supports passkeys
items.note: The menu entry that opens Settings was not found under this exact wording; the Settings title is in packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/common.json.

items.where: "Log in or sign up" > "Sign in with a passkey or security key" (above the email field); or "Try another way to sign in" > "Use a passkey or security key"
steps: Sign out and open the sign-in screen.
Click "Sign in with a passkey or security key".
Complete the passkey prompt on the device.
Look for the signed-in result without a password or code.
items.needs: a registered passkey on the account and a device that holds it

labels.text: Sign in with a passkey or security key
Use a passkey or security key

items.note: The button appears only when the server provider list includes passkey and the browser supports passkeys.

items.where: Settings > Security > "Authenticator app" > "Set up authenticator app"
steps: Open Settings, click "Security", find "Authenticator app".
Click "Set up authenticator app" (or "Enable two-factor" in the confirm step).
Scan the QR code with an authenticator app, or use "Copy key".
Type the 6-digit code in "Enter the 6-digit code from the app" and click "Verify and enable".
Look for "Two-factor authentication is now enabled on your account." Then sign out and check that sign-in asks for a code.
items.needs: an authenticator app on a phone
items.note: The confirm dialog says the change may also sign out sessions and revoke linked access.

items.where: Signed out: "Log in or sign up" > "Email address" > "Continue" > password > "Confirm it is you" screen
steps: Sign in with password on an account that has two-factor on.
Look for the "Confirm it is you" screen.
Enter the code from the authenticator app and click "Continue".
Look for the alternatives such as "Use a backup code" or "Text me a code instead".
Look for "Lost the device with your codes?" as the recovery path.
items.needs: an account with authenticator two-factor on, and its device

labels.text: Lost the device with your codes?

items.where: Settings > Security > "Authenticator app" > "Generate new backup codes" (also shown during "Set up authenticator app")
steps: Open Settings, click "Security", find "Authenticator app".
Click "Generate new backup codes" and confirm in "Replace your backup codes?".
Look for the "Save your backup codes" section with the codes.
Click "Copy codes", "Download codes" and "Print codes" one at a time and check each result.
Look that the codes are shown only once in this view.
items.needs: a signed-in account with two-factor on, or the setup flow
items.note: Print uses the browser print path; the code shows a fallback message if printing fails.

items.where: "Log in or sign up" > "Email address" > "Continue" > "Enter your password" > "Can’t reach this email?" (or "Confirm it is you" > "Lost the device with your codes?") > "Request recovery"
steps: Reach "Can’t reach this email?" from the password screen.
Look for the "Recover your account" page and pick the reason shown.
Fill in every field and an email address we can reach you at.
Click "Request recovery".
Look for the request-sent confirmation, or the error if a field is missing.
items.needs: an email address you can be reached at
items.note: The page says a person verifies the account, so the restore is handled after the request. Recovery tickets are in apps/web/lib/support/tickets/recovery.ts.

items.where: Settings > Security > "Sign-in methods" > "Connect" next to Google or GitHub
steps: Sign in, open Settings, click "Security".
Find the "Sign-in methods" heading.
Click "Connect" next to Google (or GitHub) and finish the provider sign-in.
Look for the row to say "Connected as" with your provider email.
Click "Disconnect" to see the removal step; do not confirm unless the test needs it.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a Google or GitHub account not yet linked

items.where: "Log in or sign up" > "Email address" > "Continue" (error message appears on the screen)
steps: Enter an email address that already has an account and click "Continue".
Look for the message "This email already has an account" and the action "Log in instead".
Enter an email address with no account and click "Continue".
Look for "No account uses this email" and the action "Create an account".
items.needs: one account email and one unused email

labels.text: This email already has an account

items.note: The copy exists. The combined screen may route an existing address straight to sign-in, so the conflict message may be hard to trigger by hand.

items.where: Finish signing in screen after sign-in or sign-up: "Finish signing in" > checkbox "I agree to the Terms of Service and acknowledge the Privacy Policy." > "Continue"
steps: Sign in with an account that has not accepted the current Terms, or create a new account.
Look for the "Finish signing in" screen and the line "Review the details below to continue."
Tick the terms checkbox.
Click "Continue".
Look for the sign-in finishing into the app.
items.needs: an account that has not accepted the current Terms
items.note: The re-prompt after a Terms change is applied on the server (apps/web/lib/server/terms.ts); the tester cannot trigger a new version.

items.where: After sign-in with an account that has not finished setup: "What should we call you?" > "Preferred name" > "Continue"
steps: Sign in with a new account.
On "What should we call you?" clear "Preferred name" and type a name.
Click "Continue", then click "Finish" on the next step.
Look for the name being used by the chat (or check the name in Settings > General).
items.needs: a new account that has not finished onboarding
items.note: The page is /welcome. The name field's label inside Settings > General was not checked.

items.where: /welcome after sign-in: step 1 "What best describes your work?" (pick from the list); step 2 "What do you want to do first?" (radio options such as "Write and debug code")
steps: On step 1 open "What best describes your work?" and pick an option (default says "Select one").
Click "Continue".
On step 2 pick "Write and debug code" or another option.
Read "This picks the suggestions below and nothing else".
Look at the starter prompts that change with the choice.
items.needs: a new account that has not finished onboarding

labels.text: What do you want to do first?

items.note: Copy conflict: the disclosure says the choice is not saved and only picks suggestions, while the "How this works" list says the work described shapes replies, and Expected says it tailors replies.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > "Response style" (onboarding asks only for name and work, not style)
steps: Open Settings and click "Personalization".
Change a value under "Response style" or "Response length".
Open a chat and send a short question.
Compare the reply style with the setting you chose.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Onboarding has no personalization style step, so only the Settings page is reachable for it.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > "Memory" > "Import memory from other AI providers" > "Start import"
steps: Open Settings, click "Personalization", scroll to "Memory".
Click "Start import".
Pick a source (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot or Other), then "Paste memories" or "Upload file".
Click "Preview" and select the memories to keep.
Click "Import" with the count and look for "Imported N memories from".
items.needs: text or a file exported from another assistant, and a Cloud account with memory available
items.note: The Start import button is disabled when no memory controller is available.

items.where: Settings > "Connectors" > "Suggested for" row (appears only when a work role is saved)
steps: Open Settings and click "Connectors".
Look for the "Suggested for" heading with connector buttons.
Click one suggested connector.
Click its connect action and follow the guided flow.
Look for the connector shown as connected.
items.needs: a saved work role and an outside account for the connector
items.note: Suggestions are not shown during onboarding itself; they show in Settings > Connectors and only when a work role is set.

items.where: Chat page during a long reply: banner "Get notified when the response is ready." with "Enable" and a close control; later change in Settings > Notifications > "Reply ready"
steps: Send a message that takes a while to answer.
Wait for the banner "Get notified when the response is ready.".
Click "Enable" and look for the browser permission prompt; or click the close control labelled "Dismiss notification prompt".
Open Settings, click "Notifications", and look at "Reply ready" to change it later.
items.needs: a browser where notification permission is still undecided, and a reply that runs long

labels.text: Get notified when the response is ready.

items.note: The banner appears only while browser permission is the default and a reply is still running. Whether the Notifications page has a browser permission control was not checked.

items.where: /welcome step 2: "What do you want to do first?" > "How this works" > a starter prompt, or "Finish"
steps: As a new account on step 2, click "How this works" and read the points.
Click one starter prompt (or pick a use case and click "Finish").
Look for the chat page opening with the chosen prompt in the message box.
Check that the prompt is not sent until you press send.
items.needs: a new account that has not finished onboarding

labels.text: What do you want to do first?

items.note: The prompt is passed as a starterPrompt query value and filled into the composer by apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx.

items.where: Sidebar > New chat
steps: Sign in and look at the first screen, which opens on the new-chat home.
If you are in a conversation, click the "New chat" button at the top of the sidebar.
Check for an empty transcript, a ready composer and the default model; the greeting and composer should be visible.
items.needs: none

items.where: Sidebar > conversation title in the chat history list
steps: In the sidebar, click a past conversation title.
Check that its transcript loads in the main area.
Type a follow-up in the composer and send it; the reply should continue the same conversation.
items.needs: a conversation that already has messages
items.note: The visible label of a conversation row is the conversation title, which is user data, so no fixed label exists in code.

items.where: Sidebar > Search
steps: Click the "Search" item in the sidebar rail or the Search button.
Type a word that appears in one of your conversations.
Check that matching conversations are listed and that clicking one opens it.
Optionally tick "Include archived conversations" and compare the results.
items.needs: at least one conversation containing a known word

items.needs: a browser window that can be resized to tablet widths
items.note: This is a layout rule in apps/web/shared/components/layout/app-shell-layout.ts (resolveShellLayout) and WebAppShell.tsx, with no control of its own; the window must be at least 768 px wide to be classed as tablet.

items.where: Sidebar > a conversation title (opens it); the conversation's own page address is its stable link. Open a product link at /open/<target>/<id> by typing it in the address bar.
steps: Sign in and click a conversation title in the sidebar.
Read the address in the browser address bar and copy it.
Open a new browser window, paste the address and press Return.
Compare with Expected: the same conversation opens directly. A product link at /open/chat/<id> either redirects to the conversation or shows an unavailable screen.
items.needs: a conversation in the account (the sidebar must show at least one)
items.note: The sidebar row is a link (SessionItem renders an anchor with the row's href). The product-link route is apps/web/app/open/[target]/[id]/page.tsx, which needs a signed-in session; the exact href format for a conversation row was not confirmed.

items.where: Address bar: go to /open/chat/<id> with an id that does not exist > "This chat isn’t available" with a "Back to chats" button. The loading state shows "Loading chat" while /chat resolves.
steps: Sign in, then type the address of a non-existent chat link in the address bar: /open/chat/does-not-exist-1.
Compare with Expected: an unavailable screen appears with the title "This chat isn’t available" and a "Back to chats" button.
Reload /chat and watch for a brief "Loading chat" line while the route resolves.
Click "Back to chats" and check that it returns to the chat list.
items.needs: a signed-in account (any Free account works)
items.note: The title is built from a template ("This ${noun} isn’t available") in ProductLinkUnavailable.tsx, so it reads as "This chat isn’t available". The static 'Conversation not found' screen in apps/web/app/chat/not-found.tsx had no notFound() caller under apps/web/app or apps/web/features, so it may not appear in the app; the id format is letters, digits, dot, colon, underscore or hyphen (up to 128 characters).

items.where: Settings > Appearance > Theme (effect seen on page and panel backgrounds)
steps: Click Account menu at the bottom of the sidebar, then Settings.
Click Appearance in the Settings list, then Light under Theme.
Look at the page background, sidebar and panels.
Click Dark under Theme and compare the backgrounds again with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The per-token naming is inner code; only the Theme switch is a visible control.

items.where: Account menu > Settings (raised surface is seen on the account menu and dialogs)
steps: Click the Account menu button at the bottom of the sidebar.
Compare the menu panel with the page behind it.
Click Settings to open the Settings dialog and compare its surface with the page.
Switch Theme between Light and Dark and check the raised surfaces still stand out from the page.
items.needs: none
items.note: Surface token names are inner; the visible check is the contrast between menu/dialog and page.

items.where: Effect seen on any text, for example the sidebar conversation titles and the chat replies
steps: Open the sidebar and read the conversation titles.
Compare primary text with muted text such as hints in Settings > Appearance.
Switch Theme between Light and Dark and check both stay readable.
items.needs: none
items.note: Text tokens are defined in CSS; I did not open a specific screen that shows only muted text.

items.where: Settings > Appearance (borders around the Theme buttons and the Motion buttons)
steps: Click Settings from the Account menu, then Appearance.
Look at the borders around the Theme buttons.
Switch between Light and Dark and compare the border strength.
Compare with the border on the selected Theme button.
items.needs: none
items.note: Subtle and strong rule tokens are inner CSS names; the check is visual.

items.where: Settings > Appearance > Accent colour
steps: Click Account menu, then Settings, then Appearance.
Click each colour swatch under Accent colour.
Check the selected swatch shows a ring and a check mark.
Look at buttons and selected controls: their fill changes with the accent, and text on them stays readable.
items.needs: none
items.note: Contrast on each accent is not verified by this step; only the visible change is.

items.where: Effect seen on success, warning, error and info messages in the app
steps: Trigger a status message in the app, for example a failed or completed action.
Read its text and compare the contrast with the background in Light and in Dark theme.
items.needs: none
items.note: I did not locate one specific screen that shows all four status colours.

items.where: Settings > Appearance > Chat font
steps: Click Account menu, then Settings, then Appearance.
Choose Serif under Chat font (options are Default, Sans, Serif, Dyslexic friendly).
Send a message and read the reply text.
Compare the reply text with the font before the change, and check code in the reply stays monospace.
items.needs: none
items.note: Only message text changes font; the sans UI font is not switchable by this control.

items.where: Headings on the Settings and chat pages (effect seen on the Appearance page title and section titles)
steps: Open Settings, then Appearance.
Compare the size and weight of the page title and section titles.
Open another Settings section and check its headings use the same sizes.
items.needs: none
items.note: The Appearance page h1 is hidden on wide screens (md:hidden), so the title may be seen only at phone width.

items.where: Settings > Appearance > Chat text size
steps: Click Account menu, then Settings, then Appearance.
Choose Large under Chat text size.
Open or send a chat and read a reply.
Choose Small, read the reply again, and compare the size with Default and Large.
items.needs: none
items.note: Whether the OS large-text setting is also respected is not verified here.

items.where: Settings > Appearance (small hint text under rows such as Contrast and Motion)
steps: Open Settings, then Appearance.
Read the hint text under Contrast, for example System follows your device setting.
Compare the hint text size and contrast with the row labels above it.
items.needs: none
items.note: The 12px floor and AA contrast are inner rules; the visible check is the hint text.

items.where: Settings > Appearance > Code theme (code is shown in a chat reply)
steps: Click Account menu, then Settings, then Appearance.
Look at Code theme and pick a different theme if you want to compare.
Ask the chat for a short code snippet and read the code block.
Compare the code font with the reply text font, and change Chat font to Serif to check code stays monospace.
items.needs: none
items.note: The monospace family and size are inner CSS values; the visible check is code against body text.

items.where: Effect seen in multi-line chat replies and headings
steps: Ask the chat for a reply with a heading and three or four lines of text.
Compare the spacing between the lines of one paragraph.
Compare the line spacing of the heading with the text under it.
items.needs: none
items.note: Line-height rules are inner CSS; the check is visual.

items.where: Effect seen in chat replies with several paragraphs
steps: Ask the chat for an answer with three separate paragraphs.
Measure the gap between paragraphs and compare the gaps.
items.needs: none
items.note: The paragraph gap rule is inner CSS.

items.where: Effect seen in chat replies with bulleted or numbered lists
steps: Ask the chat for a list with nested sub-items.
Compare the indent of the first level with the indent of the nested level.
items.needs: none
items.note: List indentation is an inner CSS rule.

items.where: Effect seen inside code blocks in chat replies, and Settings > Appearance > Wrap long code lines
steps: Ask the chat for a code snippet and look at the space inside the code block edges.
Open Settings, then Appearance, and turn Wrap long code lines on.
Ask for a code line that is long and compare how it wraps inside the block padding.
items.needs: none
items.note: The padding value is inner CSS; the visible check is the space around code text.

items.where: Effect seen in tables in chat replies
steps: Ask the chat for a table with three columns and three rows.
Compare the space around the text in each cell.
Check cells in every row use the same padding.
items.needs: none
items.note: Table padding is an inner CSS rule; I did not confirm a data table outside chat.

items.where: Effect seen between two chat turns in one conversation
steps: Send two messages in one chat.
Measure the gap between the first reply and the next user message.
Compare that gap with the gap between the next user message and its reply.
items.needs: none
items.note: The turn spacing value is inner CSS.

items.where: Chat reply > hover the reply (action toolbar with Copy message, Good response, Bad response, Regenerate response)
steps: Send a message and wait for the reply.
Move the pointer over the reply, or tap it on a phone.
Look at the gap between the reply text and the toolbar below it.
Compare that gap with the spacing used by other replies.
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: Whether the toolbar always shows or only on hover at phone width was not verified.

items.where: Effect seen in the message box at the bottom of a new chat
steps: Click New chat.
Look at the space between the box edge and the text, and between the box edge and its buttons.
Type a long line and compare the padding with the empty box.
items.needs: none
items.note: Composer padding is an inner CSS rule; I did not confirm exact visible label text for the composer.

items.where: Effect seen at the left and right edges of chat and Settings pages when the window width changes
steps: Open Settings, then Appearance.
Resize the browser window to a wide width and note the left and right margin.
Narrow the window to phone width and check the margin gets smaller in steps, not jumps.
items.needs: none
items.note: Gutter values are inner CSS; the check is the visible margin.

items.where: Effect seen in the sidebar conversation list
steps: Open the sidebar with several conversations listed.
Measure the height of each row.
Compare the rows: each should be the same height.
items.needs: a few conversations in the account
items.note: The row height is inner CSS; I did not verify the exact row height.

items.where: Account menu > Settings (menu items are in the Account menu list)
steps: Click the Account menu button at the bottom of the sidebar.
Read the menu items, such as Settings.
Measure or compare the row height and padding of each item.
Open another dropdown menu in the app and compare item heights.
items.needs: none
items.note: I did not identify the second menu to compare; only the Account menu was checked.

items.where: Account menu > Settings (the Settings dialog) and any confirmation dialog
steps: Click the Account menu button, then Settings.
Measure the inner padding around the title and the content.
Open a confirmation or sheet dialog from another place in the app and compare its padding.
items.needs: none
items.note: I did not locate a second dialog to compare against.

items.where: Settings > General (label-to-input spacing and field-to-field spacing)
steps: Click Account menu, then Settings, then General.
Measure the gap between a field label and its control.
Measure the gap between two fields.
Compare the gaps across rows.
items.needs: none
items.note: The form-field spacing rule is inner CSS; the General section was the form I located.

items.where: Effect seen on icons in the sidebar and the Account menu
steps: Open the Account menu.
Compare the icon size and stroke weight of Settings with other menu icons.
Open the sidebar and compare its icons with the menu icons.
items.needs: none
items.note: The icon grid and stroke are inner code values.

items.where: No control; button sizes are set in code and seen on any button
items.needs: none
items.note: Button sizes (default, xs, sm, lg, icon) are defined in packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/Button.tsx and there is no in-app density setting. Nothing for the tester to switch.

items.where: No control; corner radii show on buttons, cards and menus
steps: Open any menu or dialog in the app.
Compare the corner rounding of its panel and buttons with the page around it, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: Radius values come from the design tokens and Button.tsx; there is no setting for them.

items.where: No control; shadows show on open menus and dialogs
steps: Open any menu or dialog in the app.
Look at the edge and shadow of the raised panel against the page, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: Shadow scale is set in design tokens and primitives such as Dialog.tsx; no in-app control.

items.where: No control; stacking order shows when a dialog opens over other layers
steps: Open a menu, then open a dialog from the app.
Check the dialog sits above the menu and the page, and that the menu does not show through, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The z-index ladder is in the design tokens and Dialog.tsx; a tester can only see its effect in stacking.

items.where: No control; durations and easing show when menus, dialogs and sheets open and close
steps: Open a menu or dialog, then close it.
Watch the timing and easing of the open and close, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: Durations are set in the design tokens and Sheet.tsx; there is no in-app setting for them.

items.where: Settings > Appearance > Motion > Reduced
steps: Open Settings from the account menu and choose Appearance.
Under Motion, click Reduced.
Open a chat and send a message, then watch the reply and any loading animation.
Compare what moves with Expected: looping or travelling animation should stop or become gentle. Set Motion back to System afterwards.
items.needs: none
items.note: The in-app Reduced option sets a page attribute; the OS reduce-motion setting is changed outside the app and the 'System' choice follows it. The 'Settings' menu entry was not confirmed in the account footer file.

items.where: Settings > Appearance > Theme > Light, Dark or System
steps: Open Settings and choose Appearance.
Under Theme, click Light and look at the whole page, including a code block in a reply.
Click Dark and look again, then click System.
Compare with Expected: each choice should change the whole surface, including code.
items.needs: none
items.note: Code blocks also have their own 'Code theme' setting in the same section, so the tester should check code blocks against that setting as well.

items.where: Settings > Appearance > Contrast > High
steps: Open Settings and choose Appearance.
Set Contrast to High.
Look at text, borders and dividers on the chat page and in a menu.
Press Tab to move focus across buttons and compare the focus ring with Expected. Set Contrast back to System afterwards.
items.needs: none
items.note: System follows the device's own contrast setting, which lives outside the app and was not tested from the code.

items.where: No control; hover, focus, press and disabled looks show on any button
steps: Open Settings and choose Appearance.
Move the pointer over a Theme button, then press Tab to focus one.
Click and hold a button to see its pressed look, then compare the states with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: States are styled in packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/Button.tsx; there is no separate control for them.

items.where: Sidebar top row (brand mark) and the browser tab or installed app icon
steps: After signing in, look at the top of the sidebar for the brand mark.
Compare the mark and the app icon with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: Icons are set in apps/web/app/manifest.ts and the sidebar wordmark in apps/web/shared/components/agi/SidebarWordmark.tsx; the visible wording of the wordmark was not read.

items.where: Sidebar or command palette > New chat, then look at the empty start screen
steps: Sign in and select New chat from the sidebar, or open the command palette and choose New chat.
Look at the empty chat before typing anything.
Check that the greeting and the composer sit in the middle of the area, with no empty transcript above them.
Widen and narrow the window and check the start view stays centred.
items.needs: none
items.note: The sidebar button itself was not traced; the label is taken from the command palette entry. The centring rule is in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx around line 7637.

items.where: Inner layout rule; visible in any conversation with long replies
steps: Open a conversation that has long assistant replies.
Make the window very wide.
Check that the message text stays in a centred column of limited width rather than running edge to edge.
items.needs: a conversation with long messages
items.note: Width rule is in apps/web/app/globals.css and apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx; the exact max width value was not read.

items.needs: a conversation with a wide table
items.note: Found the table components in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownTable.tsx and MarkdownContent.tsx, but found no control that switches to a full-width data layout. Searched for full-width and data-view toggles in the chat folders.

items.needs: a conversation that produces an artifact
items.note: The artifact panel code exists (ArtifactsPanel.tsx), but the control that opens an artifact beside the conversation was not traced to a visible label.

items.needs: a conversation with sources
items.note: ResearchPanel.tsx has a Sources heading and empty state, but the control that opens the inspector beside the conversation was not found.

items.needs: a Free or paid account with a code session
items.note: The code workspace panels (CodeChangesPanel and the draft terminal or side panel) exist in apps/web/features/code/CloudCodePage.tsx, but the entry path from the chat screen was not confirmed.

items.where: Code session list: Cmd-click (Ctrl-click) a second session, then use the pane button Place panes side by side
steps: Open the code page with at least two sessions in the session list.
Click one session, then Cmd-click (or Ctrl-click) a second session to open it in a second pane.
Click the button labelled Place panes side by side if the panes are stacked.
Use each pane: type in one, then the other, and check both stay live and usable.
items.needs: two code sessions
items.note: The code page's entry path from the sidebar was not confirmed; the Cmd/Ctrl-click split is in apps/web/features/code/components/CodeRail.tsx.

items.where: Code session list: Cmd-click (Ctrl-click) several sessions, then use the pane button Stack panes
steps: Open the code page with at least two sessions in the session list.
Cmd-click (or Ctrl-click) a second and a third session to open them as panes.
Click the button labelled Stack panes to place them one above another.
Check each stacked session is live and usable on its own.
items.needs: two or more code sessions
items.note: The stacked layout styles are in apps/web/features/code/CloudCodePage.module.css; the code page's entry path was not confirmed.

items.where: Open the artifacts panel or the research panel, then drag its left edge labelled Resize artifacts panel or Resize research panel
steps: Open an artifact or a research panel beside the conversation.
Drag the thin handle on the panel edge labelled Resize artifacts panel (or Resize research panel).
Release, then check the conversation column gets narrower or wider.
Click the handle, press the Left or Right arrow key, and check the panel width changes.
items.needs: an artifact or research panel open
items.note: Keyboard resizing is implemented in apps/web/features/chat/components/SidePanelResizeHandle.tsx. The work-session panel label was not confirmed.

items.where: Sidebar > Collapse sidebar (or Toggle sidebar); on narrow screens, Open navigation
steps: Sign in and look at the left sidebar.
Use the control labelled Collapse sidebar to hide it.
Check the conversation area widens and the sidebar is gone.
Use the control labelled Toggle sidebar or Open navigation to bring it back.
items.needs: none
items.note: The collapse state lives in apps/web/shared/stores/layout-store.ts; the text of the sidebar button itself was taken from the translation keys.

items.where: Chat composer > Expand message input
steps: Type a long prompt in the message box.
Click the button labelled Expand message input.
Check the editor gets taller so you can edit more text at once.
Click the same button again (its label changes when expanded) and check the editor returns to its normal height.
items.needs: none
items.note: Expected says the editor takes the whole screen, but the code only grows the composer to min(60dvh, 40rem) (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerInput.tsx); it does not go full screen.

items.where: Research report > Full screen (exit with Exit full screen)
steps: Open a research report in the chat.
Click the button titled Full screen.
Read the report in the full-screen view and check it fills the window.
Click Exit full screen to return to the chat.
items.needs: a research report
items.note: The path to open a research report from the chat was not traced; the desktop copy is apps/desktop/src/features/research/DeepResearchPage.tsx.

items.where: Chat > click an image in a message to open it in the viewer; close it from the chat
steps: Ask for an image, or open a conversation that already has one.
Click the image in the message.
Check the image opens in a full-screen viewer over the chat, with a Download image button.
Close the viewer and check you are back at the same place in the chat.
items.needs: a conversation with an image
items.note: The close and zoom controls were not read by label; they are in the same file.

items.where: Layout rule; visible when a conversation is long enough to scroll
steps: Open a long conversation.
Scroll the transcript up and down.
Check the composer stays fixed at the bottom while the messages scroll above it.
items.needs: a long conversation
items.note: Layout is in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx and ChatComposerNew.tsx.

items.where: Chat composer > type a long prompt > Expand message input
steps: Click the message box and type a long prompt over several lines.
Check the box grows taller as you type, up to a maximum height.
Click Expand message input to make the editor taller still.
Check the text stays readable and the send button stays usable.
items.needs: none
items.note: Resting maximum height is 240px and expanded maximum is min(60dvh, 40rem), per apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerInput.tsx.

items.where: Layout rule; visible when a side panel is open and the transcript is long
steps: Open a long conversation and open a side panel such as the artifacts panel.
Scroll only the transcript and check the header, side panel and composer stay where they are.
Scroll the side panel and check the transcript does not move.
items.needs: a long conversation and an open side panel
items.note: Scroll regions are set in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx and apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx.

items.where: Open an artifact > the viewer toolbar with Close artifact viewer; scroll the artifact body
steps: Open an artifact so its viewer shows.
Scroll the artifact content down.
Check the toolbar (download, view and close controls) stays visible at the top.
Click Close artifact viewer to close it.
items.needs: an artifact
items.note: The sticky rule itself was not read in the code, only the toolbar controls.

items.where: Table header rule; visible when a long table is in a message
steps: Open a message with a long table, such as a table in a report.
Scroll the page or the table down.
Check the table header row stays pinned at the top.
items.needs: a conversation with a long table
items.note: The sticky header class is in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownContent.tsx.

items.where: Layout rule; visible when the window is narrowed with a panel open
steps: Open the artifacts panel beside the conversation.
Make the window narrow, about a phone width.
Check the panel appears over the conversation as an overlay or sheet.
Widen the window and check the panel returns beside the conversation.
items.needs: an open side panel and a window that can be resized
items.note: The overlay switch is in ArtifactsPanel.tsx and WorkSessionPanel.tsx; the exact width breakpoint was not read.

items.where: Composer footer model picker at phone width (a menu or picker opens as a bottom drawer)
steps: Open the app on a phone-sized window or a phone.
Tap the model picker in the chat composer footer.
Check it opens as a bottom sheet that slides up, not a small desktop popover.
Close it by swiping down or tapping outside, and check it returns to the chat.
items.needs: phone width
items.note: Drawer use is in apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFooter.tsx; the picker's visible title text was not read.

items.where: Layout rule; visible at tablet width
steps: Open the app in a window about tablet width (around 768 to 1024 px).
Check navigation and content show as two columns side by side.
Compare with a phone-width window, which shows a single column.
items.needs: a tablet-width window or an iPad
items.note: Breakpoint is in apps/web/shared/components/layout/app-shell-layout.ts and apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx.

items.where: Layout rule; visible on a phone with a notch or home indicator and the on-screen keyboard
steps: On a phone, open a chat and check the composer is not under the home indicator.
Tap the message box so the on-screen keyboard opens.
Check the composer moves up above the keyboard and the transcript stays usable.
items.needs: a phone with a notch or home indicator
items.note: Safe-area rules are in apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx, apps/web/app/globals.css and apps/web/app/layout.tsx.

items.where: Resize limit rule; visible when dragging a side panel edge to the far limits
steps: Open the artifacts panel or research panel.
Drag its edge as far left as it goes, then check the panel stops at its minimum width.
Drag it as far right as it goes, then check the panel stops at its maximum width and the conversation keeps some width.
items.needs: an open side panel
items.note: The limits are 280 and 900 in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/stores/uiStore.ts.

items.where: Saved layout choice; visible after collapsing the sidebar and reloading the page
steps: Collapse the sidebar using Collapse sidebar.
Resize a side panel and open another one.
Reload the page or close and reopen the browser tab.
Check the sidebar is still collapsed and the panel width and open panels are as you left them.
items.needs: none
items.note: Only the sidebar state is persisted under the agi-ui-store key in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/stores/uiStore.ts; panel widths and open panels were not confirmed as persisted.

items.where: Conversation title menu > Print
steps: Open a conversation with a few messages.
Open the conversation's title menu and choose Print.
In the print preview, check there is no sidebar or header, the whole transcript is included, and the colours suit paper.
Check the page breaks fall between messages.
items.needs: a conversation with messages
items.note: The title menu's trigger control was not identified by a visible label; print flow is in apps/web/features/chat/lib/print-conversation.ts.

items.where: Chat > hover one of your sent messages > Edit message (pencil icon) > Save & Retry
steps: Sign in and open a conversation that has a message you sent.
Hover your sent message and click the pencil icon (Edit message).
Change the text in the edit box.
Look at the Save & Retry button: it should look like the emphasised main action, with readable label text, compared with Cancel.
items.needs: a conversation with a message you sent
items.note: The Save & Retry button uses variant default (packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/Button.tsx:13). Label contrast was not measured.

items.where: Chat > conversation title menu > Share… > Copy (next to the Conversation link box)
steps: Open a conversation and open its title menu.
Click Share….
Create a link if the dialog asks, then look at the Copy button beside the Conversation link box.
Compare: Copy should look like a lighter outline button, not the filled primary style.
items.needs: a conversation you can share
items.note: Copy is an outline button (ShareConversationDialog.tsx:304). The code does not show a filled primary button beside it in this dialog, so the pairing is not confirmed.

items.where: Chat > conversation title menu > Share… > Revoke every link (red button, shown only when the link list is incomplete and no link is active)
steps: Open a conversation title menu and click Share….
Look for the Revoke every link button in the dialog footer.
If it is missing, the link list is complete, so the button is not shown; note that.
If it appears, hover and compare its red danger colour with the other buttons.
items.needs: a shared conversation whose link list is incomplete (hard to create by hand)
items.note: The button shows only when inventoryIncomplete is true and no link is active (ShareConversationDialog.tsx:414-417). Do not click it to test; it revokes links.

items.where: Chat > hover one of your sent messages > the icon-only Retry and Edit buttons (tooltips Retry and Edit)
steps: Sign in and open a conversation with a message you sent.
Hover the sent message so the action icons appear.
Hover the icon buttons to see the tooltips Retry and Edit.
Check that each icon button has a name for screen readers (aria-label Retry this message and Edit message) using a screen reader or accessibility inspector.
items.needs: a conversation with a message you sent
items.note: The accessible names Retry this message and Edit message are not visible words; they are aria-labels.

items.where: Chat > the + button at the left of the message box (Add attachments and tools)
steps: Open a chat and find the + button beside the message box.
Click it and see whether a menu opens.
If a tool or attachment is active, check that the + button shows a count badge.
Look at the button's pressed state in an accessibility inspector: it should expose aria-pressed and aria-expanded.
items.needs: none
items.note: The + button uses aria-pressed and aria-expanded (ChatComposerNew.tsx:5977-5978). The label is an aria-label, not visible text.

items.where: Chat > composer > start voice dictation > the Voice dictation strip with its Discard recording button
steps: Open a chat and start voice dictation from the composer.
Look at the strip that appears above the message box.
Hover or focus the round X button to see its name Discard recording.
Compare the grouped controls with the group name Voice dictation in an accessibility inspector.
items.needs: a microphone and microphone permission
items.note: The start-dictation control's visible text was not found in the code; the grouping labels are aria-labels.

items.where: Chat > any assistant reply that contains a web link
steps: Send a message that asks for a reply with a web link, such as a website address.
Find a link in the reply.
Check it is styled as a link (coloured, underlined or otherwise marked).
