items.where: Settings > Connectors > select a connector > "Permissions requested" panel
steps: Open Settings and click "Connectors".
Click a connector that shows a permission list.
Read the "Permissions requested" list: each scope has a sentence and a "Read" or "Write" badge.
Read the "Before you connect" notice and the "Tool permissions" button for the allowed tools.
Compare with Expected: plain-language view of what the connector may do.
items.needs: a Free account or paid account; a connector that uses OAuth scopes (otherwise a short "This provider does not use OAuth scopes" message shows)
items.note: The "Before you connect" notice and the scope list show in different states (not connected versus connected); the code does not confirm which connector state shows which panel on one screen. Autonomy and allowed sites were not confirmed as shown in this view.

items.where: Chat > a message where the assistant wants to run a tool > approval card text "This tool requires approval before execution."
steps: Use a chat where the assistant asks to run a tool that needs approval (for example a connected app action).
Read the inline card: it names the tool and shows "This tool requires approval before execution."
Use the card's allow button (label from TOOL_APPROVAL_ACTION_LABELS, not read as visible text) or the deny control if shown.
Watch whether the run continues or stops after the choice.
Compare with Expected: an inline card with approve and deny that resumes or stops the run.
items.needs: a paid account or a connected app that triggers approval; a prompt that makes the assistant use a tool

labels.text: This tool requires approval before execution.

items.note: The approve and deny button wording was not read; the allow label comes from packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/tool-approval-presentation.ts. Whether a tester can trigger this depends on the account's tool setup.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > each connector card (status shown as "Connected", "Not connected" or "Reconnect")
steps: Open Settings and click "Connectors".
Use the tabs "All", "Connected" and "Not connected" to filter the list.
Open a connector; the header button shows "Connected" when linked, or "Reconnect" when the grant needs reconnecting.
For a connected connector, check the "Disconnect" action; for a not-connected one, check the connect action.
Compare with Expected: state shown on each card, and the connect or disconnect action.
items.needs: a paid account or a Free account; an outside account for a real connection (Google, GitHub or similar); an expired connection to see "Reconnect"
items.note: No visible word "Expired" was found for connector cards; the expired state is shown as a "Connection issue" warning with a Reconnect button (SettingsModal.tsx).

items.where: Chat composer > model picker (below the message box) > choose a model that lacks a feature > notice "Model compatibility" above the message box
steps: In the chat composer, open the model picker and choose a free model.
Attach an image or a file, or keep tools turned on.
Read the notice above the message box (role status, labelled "Model compatibility"): it says, for example, "Turn off tools to use this free model."
Remove the attachment or turn tools off, and check that the notice goes away.
Compare with Expected: a visible warning before sending when the model cannot handle the request.
items.needs: a Free account (free models) or a paid account with a model that has limits; an image or file to upload

labels.text: Turn off tools to use this free model.

items.note: The notice shows only when the model catalogue is closed (ComposerFooter.tsx). The model picker's own visible label was not read.

items.where: Chat > side panel "Chat details" (work-session panel) during a running task
steps: Start a task in chat that runs steps (for example a coding or agent task).
Open the side panel for work from the chat toolbar; the panel is labelled "Chat details" (or the work-session dock label on agent-work conversations).
Watch the card: it shows the current state, steps done and latest action, and updates while the run is going.
Compare with Expected: state and progress that update while the task runs.
items.needs: a paid account or a Free account that can start a task; a task that runs several steps
items.note: The toolbar button that opens the work-session panel was not located by its visible label; only the toggle code in WebChatPage.tsx was found. The Pluralised work-session dock label comes from TASK_DOCK_PANEL_LABEL in the same file.

items.needs: a question that makes the assistant send an interactive card (choices or app card)
items.note: InteractiveCardBlock.tsx renders the widget, and WebChatPage.tsx wires the resume handler, but no visible control label was found. The MessageBubble.tsx:2020 reference is not in the file now. The trigger for an interactive card in a normal chat is not confirmed from code.

items.where: Sidebar > bell icon beside the AGI wordmark (labelled "Notifications") > list > "Mark all as read"
steps: Sign in and look at the sidebar top row, next to the wordmark.
Click the bell; the panel titled "Notifications" opens, newest first.
Look for unread items: they show in a bolder weight, with a count badge on the bell and ", unread" for screen readers.
Click an item that has a link; it opens its page and is marked read. Or click "Mark all as read".
Compare with Expected: list newest first, unread marked, open or mark read.
items.needs: a signed-in account that has notifications (unread ones give a count on the bell)
items.note: Newest-first ordering comes from the feed hook, not checked in detail. The bell sits in SidebarBrandRow.tsx.

items.where: Press Cmd+K (Ctrl+K on Windows or Linux) on any page > command palette
steps: On any page after signing in, press Command+K (Mac).
Read the search box with the placeholder "Search chats and actions".
Type part of a command, for example "settings", and watch the list narrow.
Use the arrow keys to pick "Go to Settings" and press Enter.
Compare with Expected: list filters as you type and Enter runs the choice.
items.needs: none
items.note: The Cmd+K binding is in apps/web/shared/components/CommandPalette/CommandPaletteProvider.tsx (capture phase); the palette itself is mounted in apps/web/app/AppRuntimeMounts.tsx.

items.where: Sidebar > New project (icon button), or Projects > New project
steps: Sign in and look at the left sidebar.
Click the New project button (icon only, no visible text in the sidebar).
In the Create project dialog, type a name in the Project name field.
Click Create project.
Look for the new project in the sidebar Projects list and on the Projects page.
items.needs: none
items.note: The sidebar button has only an aria-label of New project, so it shows as an icon.

items.where: Chat header > Conversation options > Rename (also sidebar row > More options > Rename)
steps: Open any chat.
Click the Conversation options control in the chat title area.
Click Rename.
Type a new title and press Enter.
Check that the header and the sidebar row show the new title.
items.needs: none

items.where: Chat header > Conversation options > Move to project (also sidebar row > More options > Move to project)
steps: Make sure at least one project exists.
Open a chat and click Conversation options.
Click Move to project and pick a project name.
Check that the chat now appears inside that project.
items.needs: at least one project
items.note: The item only appears when at least one project exists. The menu item, not a dialog, is the picker.

items.where: Chat header > Conversation options > Duplicate as branch
steps: Open a chat with some messages.
Click Conversation options.
Click Duplicate as branch.
Look for the new copy and for any message that says where it is.
items.needs: none
items.note: The visible label says branch, not duplicate. I did not confirm that the result is an independent copy or what message names its location (WebChatPage.tsx:7422 not checked).

items.where: Sidebar > chat row > More options > Archive (also chat header > Conversation options > Archive)
steps: Click More options on a chat row in the sidebar.
Click Archive.
No confirm question is expected. Look for the notice with Undo and View archived.
Click View archived and check that the chat is there.
Click Undo on a second chat and check that it returns to the list.
items.needs: none
items.note: Archive does not ask first. It offers Undo and View archived in a notice instead, as the code shows.

items.where: Chat header > Conversation options > Delete (also sidebar row > More options > Delete)
steps: Open a chat or use the sidebar row menu.
Click Delete.
Read the dialog title, which names the chat.
Click Cancel first and check that nothing is removed.
Repeat and confirm only if you are willing to delete a test chat.
items.needs: a test chat you can delete

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Recently deleted > pick an item > Delete permanently
steps: Click Library in the sidebar.
Click Recently deleted.
Click the three-dot or action control on an item and click Delete permanently.
Read the dialog title and text, which say it cannot be undone and asks for a second confirmation.
Cancel first and check the item is still in Recently deleted.
items.needs: an item already in Recently deleted (delete one in Library first)
items.note: The chat delete dialog says it cannot be undone but is one step; the permanent path with Delete permanently is in Library. Two LibraryView files exist; I read the unified-chat one.

items.where: Chat header > Conversation options > Share…  (also sidebar row > More options > Share)
steps: Open a chat and click Conversation options, then Share….
Read the dialog text: read-only snapshot, who can open it, and the expiry choices.
Check the Link expires after choices (1, 7 or 30 days).
Click Create public link only if you accept that a real public link is created, then copy it.
Check the dialog states that anyone with the link can read the snapshot.
items.needs: a chat with messages; creating a link makes a real public link
items.note: The earlier app check of this item created no link. Creating one is a real public action.

items.where: Chat > open an artifact in the artifact panel > Publish
steps: Open an artifact (a document or page) in the artifact preview.
Click Publish.
Read the confirm dialog: Share with workspace or the public text about anyone holding the link.
Confirm only on a test artifact, then copy the link from the bar or the toast.
Check that the published link opens.
items.needs: a test artifact; publishing makes a live link
items.note: No take-down or unpublish label was found in ArtifactPreview.tsx, so the 'can take it down' part of Expected is unconfirmed.

items.where: Chat > open a generated app or page artifact > Publish
steps: Open a generated app or page in the artifact preview.
Click Publish.
Confirm when the dialog asks.
Read the toast and the link bar, which give the live URL.
Open the URL in a new tab.
items.needs: a generated app or page; publishing makes a live link
items.note: Same publish path as S10.10.

items.where: Settings > Shared links > Revoke (also chat > Conversation options > Share… > Revoke share)
steps: Open Settings and go to Shared links.
Read each link's title and access.
Click Revoke on a test link.
Read the confirm dialog Revoke this public link? and click cancel first.
Confirm and check the link is gone from the list.
items.needs: a shared link you made
items.note: The settings nav label for this section was not found in settings-nav.ts or SettingsModal.tsx, so the path name is from the section heading.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Invite teammate
steps: Open Settings and click Workspace.
In Invite teammate, type an email in Invitee email and pick a role.
Click Create invitation.
Check the Pending invitations list shows the email.
Click Renew invitation or Revoke on a test invite.
items.needs: a workspace owner or admin account with a free seat
items.note: The Members page at Workspace console > People > Members also exists (apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceConsoleNav.tsx).

items.where: Settings > Workspace > change a member's role (role on the member row)
steps: Open Settings > Workspace as an owner or admin.
Find another member and open the role choice on their row.
Pick a different role.
Read the dialog Change member role? and click Change role.
Check that the role label on the row changed.
items.needs: an admin account and a second test member
items.note: Server enforcement was not checked here. The Members page has a separate role editor in WorkspaceRoles.tsx.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Transfer ownership
steps: Open Settings > Workspace as the owner.
Find the card with the text Hand the owner role to another member while keeping your own seat.
Pick another member and click Transfer ownership.
Read the dialog Transfer ownership? and confirm only with a test member.
Check that the owner label moved to that member.
items.needs: an owner account and a second test member

items.where: Chat > a research run > Sources for this run > Add a source
steps: Start a research run in chat.
Read the text above the list: Searching the whole web. Add a source to narrow it. or Sources for this run.
Click Add a source and pick a source.
Click the remove control on a source to take it out.
Check the list changes and the run uses the chosen sources.
items.needs: a research run
items.note: I found the source controls but not the exact trigger that opens the research plan, and the picker is not a dialog in the code I read.

items.where: Composer + button > Add photos & files
steps: In a chat, click the + button at the left of the message box.
Click Add photos & files.
Pick a file in the device file chooser.
Check that the file chip appears in the message box before you send.
Send and check the file is attached to the message.
items.needs: a file to upload
items.note: The shortcut for this action is defined in the same file as findShortcut('composer-add-files').

items.where: Settings > Connectors > pick a service > Connect
steps: Open Settings and click Connectors.
Click a service that is not connected yet.
Click Connect.
Complete the sign-in page of the service in the browser.
Return to the app and check the service shows as connected.
items.needs: an outside account (for example Google) to sign in with
items.note: The Connect label constant was found; I did not confirm which element renders it on the connector card.

items.needs: a connection with a revoked or expired grant (for example Google Drive)
items.note: Searched ConnectorDetailView.tsx for Reconnect: the only hits were a copy function (connectorReconnectCopy in packages/ui/ui/src/directory/constants.ts) and no button label. The message reads Name needs reconnecting. Its tools stop until you do; its settings are kept. The code is partial per the ledger.

items.needs: two or more connected accounts for one service
items.note: ConnectorAccountSummary.tsx lists accounts, but I found no default or account-switch label in packages/ui or apps/web/features/connectors.

items.where: Settings > Plugins > pick a plugin > Install
steps: Open Settings and click Plugins.
Open a plugin from the list.
Click Install.
Read the confirm dialog titled Install <plugin name>? and click Cancel first.
Install a test plugin and check it shows as Installed.
items.needs: none

items.where: Settings > Plugins > pick a plugin > Permissions (before Install)
steps: Open Settings > Plugins and open a plugin.
Scroll to the Permissions heading.
Read the copy: What this plugin says it needs. Installing it agrees to these; you can remove it at any time.
Click Install and read the confirm dialog.
Check the dialog lists the permissions, then cancel if you do not agree.
items.needs: a plugin that lists permissions
items.note: The install confirm uses a notice field (entry.installNotice); I did not confirm it lists the permissions itself.

items.where: Settings > Plugins > an installed plugin > Switch version
steps: Open Settings > Plugins and open an installed plugin.
Click Switch version and pick a different version.
Read the confirm dialog Switch to version <version>? and any It also asks for: or What changed text.
Cancel first, then confirm on a test plugin.
Check the installed version label changed.
items.needs: an installed plugin with another version
items.note: The code uses the version picker for updates; I did not locate the exact control that holds Switch version on the page.

items.where: Settings > Skills > New skill > Import a SKILL.md
steps: Open Settings and click Skills.
Click New skill.
Click Import a SKILL.md and choose a SKILL.md file.
Check that Name, Description and Instructions fill in.
Click Create skill and check the skill is in the list.
items.needs: a SKILL.md file

items.where: Settings > Skills > pick a skill > Edit
steps: Open Settings and click Skills.
Click Edit on a skill you made.
In the Edit skill dialog, change Name, Description or Instructions.
Click Save changes.
Reopen the skill and check the new values stay.
items.needs: a skill you created
items.note: The Edit control was found in SettingsModal.tsx; the dialog title Edit skill is in SkillEditorDialog.tsx.

items.where: Chat > composer model picker > pick a model that cannot take the chat content
steps: Attach an image or turn on a feature the chosen model cannot handle.
Open the model picker at the bottom of the message box.
Pick a model that does not support it.
Read the dialog that starts Switch to <model>? and its findings.
Click Keep to stay, or Switch anyway to switch, and check which model is selected.
items.needs: a model that lacks a capability in use (for example images), which depends on the model catalog
items.note: The switch dialog appears only when the compatibility check finds a blocking issue. Which model is incompatible depends on the live catalog.

items.where: Message box > model picker (open the model name under the message box) > look at the bottom of the open list
steps: Sign in and open a conversation that is long (near the model's context limit), or paste a very long message into a new chat
Open the model picker under the message box
Read the warning at the bottom of the open picker
Compare the warning with Expected: it should say the conversation is near or over the limit and what to do (trim, compact, new chat)
items.needs: a long conversation near the model's context limit

labels.text: Older messages will be left out of the next reply.

items.note: The warning text says older messages will be left out; the code gives no trim, compact or new-chat action, so Expected's 'what to do' is not in the code. The picker trigger's visible words were not confirmed.

items.where: Chat > keep sending messages until a usage limit is reached; the limit card appears in the chat. For the usage screen: the 'Usage details' button in the composer status line > Settings > Usage
steps: Use a Free account until its usage allowance is used up
Send a message in a chat
Read the limit card in the chat: it should name the limit, say when it resets and offer a next step
Compare with Expected: the code text is 'Usage budget exhausted for this billing period. Upgrade your plan or add credits.'
items.needs: a Free account that has used its allowance

labels.text: Usage budget exhausted for this billing period. Upgrade your plan or add credits.

items.note: The reset date line was not confirmed in the code read; the card's reset label comes from a prop that was not traced to a visible string.

items.needs: a Free account, and the owner must have opened paid upgrades (the billing waitlist is on by owner decision)
items.note: No credit-purchase dialog was found. Searched apps/web for credit purchase and top-up dialogs; the only code found is the billing waitlist gate in apps/web/lib/server/billing-waitlist-access.ts, whose message is 'Paid upgrades are opening in stages. Join the waitlist or enter an access code to continue.' (the file says the top-up panel exists in apps/web/features/billing/components/TopUpPanel.tsx but its opening control was not traced).

items.needs: a Free account
items.note: The upgrade comparison dialog exists (UpgradePlanDialog.tsx, opened through apps/web/features/billing/hooks/useUpgradePlanFlow.tsx), and 'See all plans' is its button, but the control that opens it was not found, so the path is unknown.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Cancel plan
steps: Sign in with a paid plan billed by Stripe (not Apple or Google)
Open Settings, then Billing
Click Cancel plan (it is not shown when the plan is already set to end)
Look at where you land: the code opens Stripe's billing portal in a new page with the cancel flow
Compare with Expected: Expected asks for an in-app cancel dialog that says when access ends; the code sends the user to Stripe's portal instead
items.needs: a paid account billed by Stripe
items.note: Cancellation is confirmed in Stripe's portal, not in an app dialog, so the in-app statement of the end date may not appear. The label 'Settings > Billing' is a path in the nav, not a button; 'Billing' is the nav key in packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/settings.json.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Payment > Add payment method (or Manage cards when a card is saved)
steps: Sign in with a paid account billed by Stripe
Open Settings, then Billing
Find the Payment heading and click Add payment method (or Manage cards)
Look at where you land: the code opens Stripe's billing portal, not a card form in the app
Compare with Expected: a payment-method dialog in the app that adds or replaces the card
items.needs: a paid account billed by Stripe
items.note: The card change happens in Stripe's billing portal, not an in-app dialog.

items.where: Settings > Security > (a sensitive action in the advanced account security panel)
steps: Open Settings, then Security
Start a sensitive action in the advanced account security panel
When asked, read the dialog titled 'Confirm it is you'
Choose a sign-in method (code, passkey or password) and check that the action only continues after the check passes
items.needs: a second factor or passkey set up on the account
items.note: The dialog is opened by the step-up hook used by the security panel (apps/web/features/account-security/components/AdvancedAccountSecurityPanel.tsx); the exact action in that panel that triggers it was not identified.

items.needs: a microphone, live-web
items.note: No explanation shown before the first microphone request was found. Searched apps/web and packages/ui for microphone copy. Found only messages shown after access is refused: 'Microphone permission denied. Please allow access in your browser settings.' (apps/web/features/chat/stores/voice-input-store.ts) and 'Microphone access was denied. Allow the microphone to use voice mode.' (apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts).

items.needs: a browser that offers screen capture, and a microphone is not needed
items.note: The screen capture call is navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/AttachmentMenu.tsx (line 613, the screenshot action), and the live source name 'Live screen' is in the same file (line 346). The menu item words that start this were not found, so the path is unknown. The browser's own screen picker is what the user sees before capture, not an app dialog.

items.where: Chat > ask for a tool action that needs approval (a connector or plugin tool) > the approval card in the chat
steps: Connect a tool or connector, then ask the chat to use it
When the card appears, read 'This tool requires approval before execution.'
Click Allow, or Deny to refuse this one call (Allow for this chat appears when the action is not high risk)
Check that only that one call runs or stops, as Expected says
items.needs: a connected tool or connector

labels.text: This tool requires approval before execution.

items.note: 'Allow for this chat' is also shown on the card, which Expected does not mention; 'Allow once' is defined but not used on this card.

items.where: Chat > ask for an action that would send private data to a website, a search engine or a connector > the approval card in the chat
steps: Turn on web search or connect an outside tool, then ask for something that uses it
When the approval card appears, read the high-risk warning
Read what it says goes where (the destination text)
Click Deny if the destination is not wanted, and check that nothing is sent
items.needs: web search or an outside connector

labels.text: Private data from this chat could be sent outside AGI. Check where it goes before you allow it.
Could send private data from this chat to a search engine

items.note: The destination sentence is built in tool-loop.ts; the code read does not prove the same sentence is shown on the card.

items.where: Projects > (open a project) > Project settings
steps: Open a project and then Project settings
Change the name or instructions, but do not save
Close the dialog or click a link to another page
Look for the warning: 'Your changes to this project have not been saved. If you leave now, they will be lost.' with a choice to keep editing or discard
items.needs: a project you can edit

labels.text: Your changes to this project have not been saved. If you leave now, they will be lost.

items.note: The word 'Projects' in the path comes from apps/web/app/chat/projects/page.tsx, not from a checked visible label. The same guard also covers the memory editor (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/MemoryEditor.tsx).

items.where: No menu: open the same conversation in two browser tabs (or two devices), type an unsent draft in one, then change the draft in the other
steps: Open the same conversation in two tabs
Type a draft in one tab
Type a different draft in the other tab, then go back to the first tab
Look for the dialog 'Choose which draft to keep' with 'Here' and 'Elsewhere' versions
Click Keep this version or Use the other version and check the draft matches your choice
items.needs: two browser tabs or two devices signed in to the same account
items.note: The dialog is triggered by sync, not by a control; timing of the trigger is not verified.

items.where: Conversation title menu > Export…, then the 'Export Chat History' dialog
steps: Open a conversation that has messages
Open its title menu and choose Export…
In 'Export Chat History', pick a format (Markdown, PDF, Word Document, HTML or JSON)
Click Export Markdown (or the chosen format name) and check the file downloads with the conversation in it
items.needs: a conversation with messages
items.note: The title menu's trigger words were not confirmed. The export button reads 'Export ' followed by the format name (EnhancedExportDialog.tsx line 286).

items.where: Open the menu on an assistant answer > Report this response
steps: Send a message and wait for the answer
Open the menu on that answer
Choose Report this response
Check the item changes to Reported (or Reporting… while sending) and that the report is recorded
items.needs: a chat with at least one answer
items.note: The answer menu's trigger words were not confirmed. The report is sent to /api/content-report; no reason field is offered in this menu item, so Expected's 'with a reason' is not in this path.

items.where: Account menu > Send feedback, then the 'Share feedback' dialog
steps: Open the account menu
Click Send feedback
Pick a feedback type (General feedback, Something is broken or Feature request) and write a message
Click Send feedback in the dialog and check the success message appears
items.needs: none
items.note: The account menu trigger's visible words were not confirmed; the menu item is in apps/web/shared/components/layout/AccountMenuItems.tsx.

items.where: Settings > Privacy > Share crash and error reports
steps: Open Settings, then Privacy
Read the switch 'Share crash and error reports' and its line: 'Send error reports, with sensitive fields removed.'
Turn the switch on, then off
Check the switch state persists after reloading the page
items.needs: none
items.note: No dialog before data leaves the device was found; the switch line is the only in-app explanation found, and a longer note about browser crash reports is at PrivacySection.tsx.

items.where: Settings > Privacy > Export data
steps: Open Settings, then Privacy
Find the row 'Export data' with 'Download a copy of your account data and files.'
Click Export data (it shows Preparing… while it works)
Check a file downloads and that it contains your account data
items.needs: a signed-in account

labels.text: Download a copy of your account data and files.

items.note: No confirmation dialog is in this row; Expected asks for a dialog, the code starts the download directly.

items.where: Settings > Account > Delete account > Delete
steps: Open Settings, then Account
Find the row Delete account and click Delete
Read the dialog 'Delete your account?' and what it deletes
Type DELETE in the box and read the button Schedule deletion (do not click it unless you want to schedule deletion)
items.needs: an account that can schedule deletion (some paid plans are blocked)
items.note: Deletion is scheduled with a cancellation deadline, not done at once. The Delete button is disabled when the plan blocks deletion.

items.where: Any button or link in the web app; the accessible name is heard with VoiceOver
steps: Turn on VoiceOver (Command+F5).
Tab to the Account menu button in the sidebar, then to Settings and to a few buttons on the chat page.
Listen: each control should say what it does (for example Keyboard shortcuts or Account menu for your name), not just 'button'.
items.needs: VoiceOver on macOS and a signed-in account
items.note: Inner rule with no control of its own; the check is by screen reader.

items.where: Top title of the chat page (conversation title) and section headings in Settings; seen with VoiceOver's headings list
steps: Turn on VoiceOver and open an existing chat.
Open the VoiceOver rotor (Control+Option+U) and choose Headings.
Listen for a top-level heading for the conversation title and nested headings in sections; compare with Expected.
items.needs: VoiceOver on macOS and a signed-in account with a saved chat
items.note: The title is an h1 in ConversationHeader.tsx; Settings section headings were not all checked.

items.where: Account menu > Get help > Keyboard shortcuts (menu opened from the round account button with your initial)
steps: Press Tab until the round account button is focused, then press Return.
Press Down Arrow to move through the menu items, then Right Arrow to open Get help.
Press Escape to close the menu, and check the menu closed and focus went back to the account button.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Arrow-key handling is in packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/useMenuKeyboard.ts; the Ctrl/Cmd+K command palette is also keyboard-driven (shortcut label not confirmed on screen).

items.where: Any control on any page; seen when tabbing with the keyboard
steps: Open the chat page and press Tab repeatedly.
Look at each focused control for a visible outline (2px ring).
Compare with Expected: the focused control always shows a clear indicator.
items.needs: a keyboard and a signed-in account
items.note: Rule is in apps/web/app/globals.css (focus-visible outline).

items.where: Account menu > Get help > Keyboard shortcuts (the dialog opens)
steps: Open the Account menu and go to Get help > Keyboard shortcuts.
Check that focus moved into the dialog, then press Tab several times and confirm focus stays inside it.
Press Escape and check the dialog closes.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Dialog focus handling is in packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/useDialogKeyboard.ts.

items.where: Account menu > Get help > Keyboard shortcuts; close it and see where focus lands
steps: Open the Keyboard shortcuts dialog from the Account menu, using the keyboard.
Press Escape to close it.
Check focus returns to the Get help item or the account button that opened it.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Restore logic is in packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/useDialogKeyboard.ts.

items.where: Chat page after a reply finishes; the announcement is spoken, not shown
steps: Turn on VoiceOver (Command+F5) and open a chat.
Type a short message in the composer and send it, without moving focus.
Listen for a short announcement such as Response complete, and check focus stayed in the composer.
items.needs: VoiceOver on macOS and a signed-in account
items.note: Announcement text comes from buildStreamAnnouncement in ChatMessageList.tsx.

items.where: A streaming reply in the chat; heard with VoiceOver while the reply is written
steps: Turn on VoiceOver and send a message that asks for a long answer.
Listen while the reply streams: it should speak in short chunks or once at the end, not word by word.
While it streams, the send button shows Stop the current response; check it is labelled.
items.needs: VoiceOver on macOS and a signed-in account
items.note: Chunking is in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/StreamAnnouncer.tsx.

items.where: Chat > a reply that asks to run a tool > the tool card with Needs approval and the approval buttons
steps: Open a chat and ask AGI to do a task that needs a tool (agent mode), so it asks for approval.
Find the tool card showing Needs approval or This tool requires approval before execution.
Turn on VoiceOver and check the card states the step (running, done, failed or waiting) and that the approve and deny buttons have names.
items.needs: a signed-in account whose chat asks for tool approval

labels.text: This tool requires approval before execution.

items.note: The approve and deny button text comes from TOOL_APPROVAL_ACTION_LABELS, whose exact words were not read.

items.where: Chat > any message bubble > the Copy message button under the message
steps: Open a chat with a reply on a touch device or at phone width, and tap a message.
Check the action buttons (Copy message and others) are visible without hovering.
Tap Copy message and check it works.
items.needs: a touch screen or phone width
items.note: The row shows on hover or focus, and is always visible for touch (hover:none).

items.where: Chat composer > Files menu > Upload from device (non-drag upload); artifacts panel > Resize artifacts panel (arrow keys)
steps: Open the Files menu from the chat composer and choose Upload from device; pick a file from the file picker.
Check the file is attached without dragging anything.
Click or Tab to the separator labelled Resize artifacts panel and press Left Arrow or Right Arrow to resize the panel; check it moves.
items.needs: a file to upload and a signed-in account
items.note: The control that opens the Files menu was not located in the code; the artifacts panel only shows on the desktop layout.

items.where: Settings > Appearance > Chat text size (choose Small, Default or Large)
steps: Click Account menu > Settings, then Appearance.
Find Chat text size and choose Large.
Go back to a chat and check the text is bigger and not cut off; then try a larger text size in the browser (Cmd+Plus) and check again.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The app only scales chat text; the Settings-level text size is not in the code.

items.where: Chat page in a browser at high zoom; seen by zooming the page
steps: Open the chat page in a browser window and press Cmd+Plus until zoom is 400%.
Check the page turns into one column (sidebar moves away or collapses) and there is no sideways scroll bar.
Read a long message and check no text is cut off.
items.needs: a browser with zoom and a signed-in account
items.note: Layout rules are in apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx and app-shell-layout.ts.

items.where: Settings > Appearance > Motion > Reduced
steps: Click Account menu > Settings, then Appearance.
Under Motion, click Reduced.
Open a chat that is loading or streaming and check the looping and moving animations stop or are replaced; then click System to go back.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: System follows the device setting, so the OS reduce-motion switch can be tested too; the CSS rule is in apps/web/app/globals.css.

items.where: Composer > Start voice mode > voice call screen > menu with In this chat > Captions
steps: Click Start voice mode in the chat composer and allow the microphone.
Open the menu from the call screen and turn on Captions.
Speak a sentence and check the Voice captions area shows your words and the reply as text.
items.needs: a microphone and a signed-in account with voice allowed
items.note: The button that opens the In this chat menu was not located as visible text.

items.where: Composer > Start voice mode; after the call, the spoken turns appear as messages in the chat
steps: Click Start voice mode, allow the microphone, and say two or three sentences.
End the call and go back to the chat.
Read the messages and check each spoken line appears as text in the same chat.
items.needs: a microphone and a signed-in account with voice allowed
items.note: Transcript writes go to the chat through WebChatPage.tsx.

items.where: Chat > ask AGI for a chart > the chart card > View chart data
steps: Open a chat and ask AGI to make a chart from some numbers.
Click View chart data under the chart.
Check the table shows the values and the chart has a title that matches what is plotted.
items.needs: a signed-in account; AGI must produce a chart
items.note: The chart title and summary are read by screen readers through aria-describedby.

items.where: Settings > General > Display Language, choose an Arabic or Hebrew option
steps: Click Account menu > Settings, then General.
Under Display Language, pick a right-to-left language such as Arabic.
Check the whole layout mirrors: the sidebar and menus move to the right and text aligns to the right.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The app sets document direction from the language; not every menu was checked for mirroring.

items.where: Chat composer and message bubbles; seen when you type or read text in two directions
steps: In the composer, type one line in English and a new line in Arabic or Hebrew.
Send it and read the message bubble.
Check each paragraph lines up in its own direction.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a keyboard that types Arabic or Hebrew
items.note: The composer and bubbles set dir=auto in ComposerInput.tsx and MessageBubble.tsx.

items.where: Chat composer; seen while typing with an input method (Japanese, Chinese or Korean)
steps: Switch the Mac keyboard to a Japanese or Chinese input method.
In the composer, type a word and press Return to confirm the conversion (do not send yet).
Check the message is not sent, and press Return again to send only when you want.
items.needs: a Japanese, Chinese or Korean input method and a signed-in account
items.note: Composition check is in ChatComposerNew.tsx keydown handling.

items.where: Settings > Account > Linked devices (dates shown in the list)
steps: Click Account menu > Settings, then Account.
Find Linked devices and read the dates shown for each device.
Compare the date format with your Mac's region format (day/month order and 12 or 24 hour clock).
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one linked device
items.note: Dates use the browser locale, not the Display Language picker; Passkeys dates in Settings > Security work the same way.

items.where: Settings > Billing (the Invoices and receipts page); the link from Billing to that page was not confirmed
steps: Click Account menu > Settings, then Billing.
Look for Invoices and receipts, or open the page directly at /billing/invoices.
Check each amount shows the right currency symbol and number format.
items.needs: a paid or past-paid account with invoices
items.note: The money formatter is in packages/contracts/types/src/money-format.ts; the pricing page at apps/web/app/pricing/page.tsx also shows prices but its path from the app was not confirmed.

items.where: Chat > a reply that ran commands > the tool summary line (for example ran 2 commands or ran a command)
steps: Open a chat in agent mode where AGI runs more than one command.
Read the tool summary line in the reply.
Check it says ran a command for one and ran N commands for more than one, not a plain English s on every word.
items.needs: a chat where AGI runs commands (agent mode)
items.note: Plural rules are applied with translateUiPlural; other languages (for example Russian or Arabic) were not checked in the UI.

items.where: Error notices in the chat and the app's network error messages; seen after changing Display Language and causing an error
steps: Open Account menu > Settings > General and set Display Language to another language.
Turn off Wi-Fi, send a chat message, and read the error that appears.
Check the error text is in the language you chose, not always English.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a way to cause a network error
items.note: Message text is in packages/ui/ui/src/lib/network-error.ts and apps/web/features/chat/lib/turn-error-notice.ts; not every error may be translated.

items.where: Account menu > Get help > Keyboard shortcuts (the shortcut hints show ⌘ on a Mac)
steps: Open the Account menu, go to Get help > Keyboard shortcuts.
Read the shortcut list and check the keys show the Mac symbol ⌘ (not Ctrl).
Compare with Expected. Earlier check: the dialog shows macOS labels but logs a React nesting warning (div inside p) in the console.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Shortcut notation comes from packages/ui/ui/src/platformKeys.ts; earlier run was PARTIAL (E007).

items.where: Settings > General > Display Language (choose Español or another language, then look at the page)
steps: Sign in and open Settings from the account or sidebar menu.
Open the General section and find the row labelled Display Language.
Open the Display Language menu and pick a language other than English, such as Español.
Look at the settings rows, buttons and the sidebar: long or translated labels should wrap or truncate with no overlap or clipped controls.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account, phone width optional for a second check
items.note: The Code line was unverified and the plan gave no location; I searched apps/web and packages/ui for locale, i18n, truncate and line-clamp code and found the Display Language selector (apps/web/features/settings/components/LanguageSelector.tsx) and a Spanish locale (packages/ui/i18n/locales/es). The wrap and truncate rules themselves are spread across many CSS and component files, not one control, so the tester should judge the layout by eye on the translated screens. The exact visible text of the General tab heading and the Settings menu entry was not confirmed in the code.

items.where: Sidebar > New chat
steps: Sign in to the web app.
Click "New chat" in the sidebar (or the same action in the collapsed sidebar rail).
Look at the conversation area: it should show no earlier messages.
Look at the composer at the bottom: it should be ready to type in, with the default model shown.

items.where: Sidebar > New chat
steps: Make sure your name is set: Settings > Personalization > "What should AGI call you?" (type a name and save).
Click "Sidebar > New chat".
Read the greeting above the composer.
Compare: it should say a time-of-day greeting with your name, for example "Good morning, <name>" (the wording depends on the time of day and the date).

items.note: The greeting variant is chosen by date and hour (packages/platform/utils/src/greeting.ts), so the exact wording can differ between tries.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > "What should AGI call you?"
steps: Open Settings and choose "Personalization".
Clear the field "What should AGI call you?" (its hint says "Leave empty to skip names.") and save.
Click "Sidebar > New chat".
Compare: the greeting should have no name and no personal details in it.

items.note: The save control's exact label was not confirmed in the code.

items.needs: none

items.needs: none

items.where: Sidebar > Projects
steps: Sign in and look at the "Projects" section in the sidebar.

Type a question and send it.

steps: On the new-chat screen, leave the composer empty.

Click it.

items.where: Composer > Chat | Work switch > Work
steps: On the new-chat screen, click "Work" in the Chat | Work switch above the composer.
Type a task and send it.

items.where: Sidebar > Code
steps: Sign in and click "Code" in the sidebar.
Look for the coding screen (the page at /code).

items.where: More composer options (+) > Temporary chat
steps: On the new-chat screen, click the "+" button (labelled "More composer options").
Click "Temporary chat".
Type a message and send it.
Compare: the chat should not appear in the sidebar history afterwards.

items.where: Composer footer > model button ("Auto (Recommended)")

Click it to open the model list.

items.where: New chat > line under the greeting "Workspace: <name>"
steps: Sign in to an account that belongs to an organization.
Click "New chat" in the sidebar.

Compare with the workspace the chat will be saved into.

items.where: New chat > composer project picker ("Project or folder")
steps: Click "New chat" in the sidebar.
Click the project picker in the composer (it shows "Project or folder" when Work is available, otherwise "Project").
Pick a project from the list.
Send a message and compare: the new chat should be created in that project.

steps: Create a new account and finish sign-in.

On "What do you want to do first?", look for the "How this works" section.
Click "Finish" or a starter prompt, then compare: the short introduction should cover the key features.

steps: On the new-chat screen, type text in the composer but do not send it.
Go to another page in the app, or reload the page.
Return to the new chat.

No sign-in prompt for guests was found.

items.where: Chat page, first screen after sign-in > the composer box that reads 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' > the 'Send message' button
steps: Sign in and stay on the chat page.
Click the composer box that reads 'Ask anything. Type / for commands'.
Type a short plain sentence, such as 'Plain text test'.
Click 'Send message', or press Enter if your Enter key sends in your settings.
Check that the sentence appears as your message with no formatting changes and that a reply starts.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can chat (for example a Free account)
items.note: The placeholder can change with the work mode (WORK_MODE_PLACEHOLDERS in ChatComposerNew.tsx), so the box may show different words. Whether Enter alone sends depends on a send-with-Enter setting (ChatComposerNew.tsx); its label was not found.

items.where: Chat page > the composer box (accessible name 'Message input')
steps: Click the composer.
Type 'Line one', press Shift+Enter, then type 'Line two'.
Click 'Send message'.
Check that the sent message shows two lines, with the line break kept.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can chat
items.note: 'Message input' is the box's accessible name, not necessarily visible text.

items.where: The composer box on the chat page, while typing
steps: Click the composer.
Type a line, press Shift+Enter, and repeat until there are five or more lines.
Check that the box grows taller as lines are added, then stops growing and scrolls inside the box.

items.where: Chat page > the 'Expand message input' button at the top-right corner of the composer (it shows only when the text is tall enough)
steps: Type or paste enough lines that the composer becomes tall.
Hover the top-right corner of the composer.
Click 'Expand message input'.
Check that the composer is taller than its automatic height.
Click 'Collapse message input' to return it to normal size.
items.needs: none

items.needs: none

items.where: Chat page > the 'Send message' button at the right end of the composer
steps: Leave the composer empty and hover over the 'Send message' button; read the reason shown.
Type a message.
Click 'Send message'.
Check that the message is sent and the button shows a sending state.

labels.text: Send is off until you type a message or attach a file.

items.where: Chat page > after sending a message, the 'Stop the current response' button replaces Send while the reply is streaming
steps: Send a question that needs a long answer.
While the reply is still streaming, hover the button and read 'Stop generation'.
Click 'Stop the current response'.
Check that the reply stops and the text already written stays on screen.

items.note: The composer's state after stopping (whether Send returns) was not read.

steps: Click the composer and type 'First line'.
Press Shift+Enter.
Check that the cursor moves to a new line and nothing is sent.
Type 'Second line' and send with 'Send message'.
Check that the sent message has two lines.

items.where: Chat page > the 'Message input' box for text; the '+' button next to the composer > 'Attach clipboard' for clipboard files
steps: Copy a line of plain text, click the composer, and press Cmd+V; check the text appears in the box.

items.where: Chat page > the 'Message input' box

items.where: Chat page > the 'Message input' box > paste multi-line source code

Check the notice 'That paste looked like code, so it was wrapped in a code block.' and that the text is inside a code fence.

items.where: Composer > microphone button "Start voice input" (next to the + button); click it, speak, then click "Stop recording and edit the transcript"
steps: Click the microphone button in the composer (aria label "Start voice input").

labels.text: Stop recording and edit the transcript

items.where: Composer > "Start voice mode" button at the right end of the composer (shown when the text box is empty)

Allow microphone access, speak a question, and wait for the reply to be spoken aloud.
Compare with Expected: a hands-free conversation starts from the composer and the reply is heard.
items.needs: A microphone, and an account that has the voice capability (canUseVoice). Voice is not offered in a chat that holds Google account data.

items.where: Composer > type a message while a reply is still generating > press "Send message"; the message appears in the "Queued messages" list above the text box

Press "Send message" (or Enter).
Look above the text box for the "Queued messages" list with a row starting "Queued:". Wait for the first reply to finish and check the queued message is sent then. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: A paid or Free account that can get a streamed reply long enough to type during it.

Compare with Expected: the cancelled row disappears and does not send; the edited text is sent only when you send it again.
items.needs: A paid or Free account and a reply still streaming long enough to queue a message.
items.note: Steered rows ("Sent to the running reply") have no Edit or Cancel button. Only rows still waiting in the queue do.

items.where: New chat > composer footer model button > price bars on a model row (accessible text "Price band X of Y") and the "About <model name>" card > "Credits per 1M tokens" and "Typical message".
steps: Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Look at the price bars on each row, or hover a bar to see its title.
Click the help icon "About <model name>" and read "Credits per 1M tokens" and "Typical message".
Compare: more filled bars or larger numbers mean a higher cost or faster use of the allowance.
items.needs: none
items.note: Free-pool models show no credit figures. The bar text is generated from data.

items.where: New chat > composer footer model button > model row marked "Upgrade" (locked rows show the plan that unlocks them).
steps: Sign in with a Free account.
Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Find a row with an "Upgrade" label, marked with a lock.
Compare: the row names the plan that unlocks the model, as Expected says.
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: The plan name comes from resolvePlanLockLabel (packages/ai/routing/src/model-picker.ts:247); the fallback text is "Upgrade".

items.where: New chat > composer footer model button > model row badge (Preview, Experimental, Beta or Alpha).
steps: Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Look for a badge reading "Preview", "Experimental", "Beta" or "Alpha" on a row.
Compare: the model carries the badge, as Expected says.
items.needs: a preview or experimental model in the catalogue
items.note: I did not confirm that any preview model is in the current catalogue, so the badge may not be visible.

items.where: New chat > composer footer model button > model row guidance reads "Leaving <date>".
steps: Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Look for a row whose grey line reads "Leaving" followed by a date.
Compare: the notice shows the retirement date before the model leaves the list.
items.needs: a model with a retirement date in the catalogue
items.note: The date comes from catalogue data; I did not confirm that a model with a retirement date exists now.

items.where: New chat > composer footer model button > model row guidance reads "Unavailable right now" and the row cannot be picked.
steps: Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Look for a row whose grey line reads "Unavailable right now".
Click that row and check that the model is not selected.
Compare: the row is marked unavailable and cannot be picked.
items.needs: a provider in a degraded state, which a tester cannot set up
items.note: The state depends on live provider availability; the row text is "Temporarily unavailable" inside the catalogue (ModelCatalogue.tsx:41).

items.where: New chat > composer footer reasoning control (the control whose accessible name starts "Reasoning effort:") > effort slider labelled "Reasoning effort". Settings > General > "Reasoning effort".
steps: Select a reasoning model in the composer footer model button.
Click the "Reasoning effort" control in the composer footer.
Drag the slider to a different level, or pick an option.
Send a message and compare the level chosen with Expected: the model thinks at that level.
items.needs: a reasoning model, and a paid account for the higher levels
items.note: The control is shown only for models with an effort ladder; Settings > General also has the same label.

items.where: New chat > composer footer reasoning control > "Fast mode" switch. The "Fast" pill appears when it is on.
steps: Select a model that offers a faster tier in the composer footer model button.
Click the composer footer reasoning control.
Turn on the "Fast mode" switch.
Send a message and check the "Fast" pill and the usage note: faster answers at the stated usage multiplier.
items.needs: a paid account and a model with a fast tier
items.note: The switch is disabled when fast mode is not allowed for the account or workspace; the enclosing popover was inferred from file order and not run.

items.where: New chat > composer footer "Style" button > "Response Length" row (Brief, Default, Thorough). Also Settings > Personalization > "Response length".
steps: Click the "Style" button in the composer footer.
Find the "Response Length" row.
Click "Brief" or "Thorough".
Send the same question twice, once with each setting, and compare the answer lengths with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The Settings entry point to Settings > Personalization was not traced.

items.where: No control. Effect is seen after a restart: the composer model name in a new chat matches the model last chosen.
steps: Choose a model in the composer footer model button.
Close the browser tab and open the app again.
Open New chat and read the model name on the composer footer.
Compare with Expected: the chosen model is still selected. If Settings > General > "Default model" is set to a fixed model, that setting wins over this memory.
items.needs: none
items.note: The choice is saved in localStorage under the key agi-model-store (apps/web/shared/stores/model-store.ts:376); it is per browser, not per account.

items.where: Composer footer > model name button > Models (pick a model), then send a message in the same conversation
steps: Open or start a conversation in the web app.
Click the model name button at the bottom of the message box (it opens the picker titled Models).
Choose a different model from the list.
Send a message in this same conversation and wait for the answer.
Open a new chat and look at the model name in its composer.
Compare: this conversation keeps the model you chose, and the new chat shows the default model.
items.needs: an account with more than one model available
items.note: The per-conversation save path is handleConversationModelChange in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx; the only visible error is the toast 'Could not save the model for this conversation. The previous model remains active.' Default-versus-conversation behaviour in a new chat was not traced in code.

items.where: Under an answer, click the refresh icon (Regenerate response) > Try again with > pick a model
steps: Send a message and wait for the answer to finish.
Hover under the answer and click the refresh icon (it opens a menu).
Under Try again with, click a model name.
Look at the new answer, and then open the composer model picker.
Compare: the new answer comes from the model you picked, and the composer still shows the conversation's previous model.
items.needs: an account with more than one model available
items.note: The refresh icon has no visible text, only an aria-label 'Regenerate response'. The model list comes from regenerateModelOptions, and the override is passed in handleRegenerateMessage in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx.

items.where: Hover over an answer; the model name that answered shows under it (data-testid message-answered-by in MessageBubble)
steps: Send a message and wait for the answer to finish.
Move the mouse over the answer (on touch screens the label is always shown).
Read the small muted model name under the answer.
Compare: the name matches the model that actually answered, shown on the composer or in the Try again with menu.
items.needs: none
items.note: The label text is built at runtime from the model id (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx around line 2411), so no fixed visible words exist to quote. It is hidden until hover on pointer devices.

items.where: A notice appears under an answer when a fallback happened (role status, data-testid fallback-reason-notice)
steps: Send a message with a model; wait for the answer to finish.
Look under the answer for a small notice with an alert icon and a close control.
Read the notice text: it says the different model answered and gives the reason.
Click the close control to dismiss the notice.
Compare: the notice names the model that answered and the reason, and it appears only when the chosen model failed or was unavailable.
items.needs: none; a model failure or outage is needed to trigger the notice, which a tester cannot force from the UI
items.note: The notice text is generated at runtime by describeFallbackReason (packages/contracts/types/src/chat-fallback-reason.ts; apps/web/lib/chat-fallback-reason.ts). The close control's aria-label is 'Dismiss model substitution notice' but it has no visible text. The notice is not shown while the answer is still streaming.

items.where: Composer footer > model name button > Models > choose a model that cannot handle the current chat
steps: Attach an image to the chat (use the attach control in the message box).
Click the model name button and open the Models picker.
Choose a model that cannot read images or other files in this chat.
Look for the line Switch to <model name>? with a warning sentence under it.
Read the sentence, then compare: it says what will be lost, and the two buttons are Switch anyway and Keep <current model name>.
items.needs: a file or image to upload, and an account with a model that cannot read it
items.note: The warning sentences come from evaluateModelCompatibility at runtime; the Keep button text is built from the current model name, so it is not quoted as a fixed label.

items.where: Attach a file or image, then choose a model that cannot read it; an alert appears above the message box with Use Auto, Remove attachments and Choose a compatible model
steps: Attach an image or document to the chat.
Click the model name button and choose a model that cannot read that file type.
Look at the alert above the message box: it says the selected model can't read the attachment.
To keep the files, click Use Auto, or click Choose a compatible model and pick a listed model.
To drop them instead, click Remove attachments.
Compare: the files are kept with a model that can read them, or removed, and the alert goes away.
items.needs: a file or image to upload; a Free account shows Use Free Auto instead of Use Auto
items.note: The alert text is chosen at runtime by attachmentConflictKind. For local-model attachments the alert shows Switch to a cloud model and Remove attachments instead (ChatComposerNew.tsx around line 5321-5357).

items.where: Chat transcript layout: your messages sit right-aligned in a bubble, replies sit in a plain left column
steps: Sign in and open a chat, then send any short message.
Look at your message: it should be a right-aligned bubble, and the reply a flat left column.
With VoiceOver on, move through the transcript and check you hear 'You said:' before your message and 'Assistant said:' before a reply.
Compare with Expected: the code has no avatars or names, so only the bubble-versus-column difference and the hidden headings apply.
items.needs: a Free or paid account; VoiceOver for the screen-reader step
items.note: Expected mentions an avatar and a name, but the code states 'No avatars'; the author is shown by alignment and the hidden 'You said:' heading only.

items.where: Chat screen: type in the box that reads 'Ask anything. Type / for commands', then press Enter
steps: Open a new chat after signing in.
Type 'QA test message one' in the box that reads 'Ask anything. Type / for commands'.
Press Enter.
Look at the transcript: your exact text should appear in your own message bubble on the right.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The send control's exact visible label was not found in the composer code; the Enter key path is the one confirmed.

items.where: Chat screen: attach a file or image in the composer, then send. The sent message shows the file as a thumbnail or named chip
steps: Open a new chat and use the composer's attach control to choose an image and a PDF or text file.
Send the message.
Look at your message: the image should show as a thumbnail and the file as a named chip.
Click the image thumbnail and the file chip to check they open or download.
items.needs: a file to upload (an image and a document)
items.note: The composer's attach control was not found by its label in ChatComposerNew.tsx; 'Attach File' is only a translation key, so the exact on-screen path is unconfirmed.

items.where: Composer > Connectors, pick a prompt or a resource, then send. Or type / and pick a skill, then send
steps: Open the composer's Connectors menu and choose a prompt or resource from a connected connector.
Send a message with it.
Look at your message: a chip should show 'Prompt:' or 'Resource:' and, for a skill, '/' plus the skill name.
Hover a chip to see its full name in the tooltip.
items.needs: a connected connector with a prompt or resource, or an available skill
items.note: The chip code covers only skill, prompt and connector resource; quoted text, page, editor selection and @mentions have no chip in MessageContextChips.tsx.

items.where: Hover your message > More message actions > Sent at
steps: Send a message and hover over it.
Click the 'More message actions' button at the end of the message's action row.
Read the 'Sent at' line in the menu; it shows the time.
Compare with Expected: the time appears on demand in the menu, not inline in the transcript.
items.needs: none

items.where: Hover your message > Edit message > change text > submit; then page the versions with Previous version and Next version
steps: Send a message, hover over it, and click 'Edit message'.
Change the text and submit the edit.
Look under your message for the version pager (1/2 style) with 'Previous version' and 'Next version'.
Compare with Expected: the code shows the count and pager, not the word 'Edited'; check whether the pager is the edited mark you see.
items.needs: a sent message you can edit
items.note: No visible word 'Edited' was found in the code; the only edited-state text is the screen-reader 'Edited message, version n of m'.

items.where: Hover your message > Copy message
steps: Send a message and hover over it.
Click the 'Copy message' button (tooltip 'Copy').
Click into the composer and paste.
Compare with Expected: the pasted text should match your message exactly.
items.needs: none

items.where: Hover your message > Edit message
steps: Send a message and hover over it.
Click 'Edit message' and change the text.
Submit the edit.
Look for a new reply under the edited message, and check the thread follows it.
items.needs: a sent message you can edit
items.note: The submit control's visible label was not found in the edit code, so the submit step is described by its effect.

items.where: Hover your message > Retry this message
steps: Send a message and wait for the reply to finish.
Hover over your message and click the 'Retry this message' button (tooltip 'Retry').
Look at the transcript: a fresh reply should appear.
Compare with Expected: the message text should be unchanged.
items.needs: a sent message; the button is disabled while a reply is still streaming

items.where: Hover your message > Branch conversation from here, or More message actions > Branch conversation from here
steps: Send several messages so there is a thread.
Hover a user message and click 'Branch conversation from here' (or open 'More message actions' and choose it).
Wait for the new conversation to open.
Compare with Expected: the new chat should contain the thread up to that message, and the original chat should be unchanged.

items.where: Under an edited user message: 'Previous version' and 'Next version' buttons around the count
steps: Edit a sent message and submit the edit so it has two versions.
Look under your message for the pager with the count (1/2).
Click 'Previous version' and then 'Next version'.
Compare with Expected: the count changes and the thread follows the version you chose.
items.needs: a sent message you can edit
items.note: The source file's list comment says the variant navigation is marked unfinished in the ui; quoted line references moved.

items.where: Chat screen: a long user message shows a 'Show more' link under it
steps: Paste a very long text into the composer and send it.
Look under your message for the 'Show more' link.
Click 'Show more' and check the full message appears.
Compare with Expected: the message should now be at full length.

items.where: Chat screen: after 'Show more', the same link reads 'Show less'
steps: Send a long message and click 'Show more'.
Click the 'Show less' link under the message.
Compare with Expected: the message should shrink back to its collapsed height.
items.needs: a message long enough to collapse
a way to make a send fail, such as a dropped connection
items.note: No visible failed-state text for a user message was found; a failed user save only logs to the console. The only failure copy is the composer notice "Couldn't send. Restored here so you can try again." (ChatComposerNew.tsx) and an assistant 'Response failed' label.

items.needs: a way to make a send fail
items.note: No Retry is found on a failed send: the composer restores the draft with the notice "Couldn't send. Restored here so you can try again." and the 'Retry this message' button exists on sent messages, but not as a failure action. Searched useChatStream.ts and ChatComposerNew.tsx for failed-send retry.

items.where: Chat screen: send a message while a reply is still running. A 'Queued messages' list appears above the message box
steps: Send a message that starts a long reply.
While it is still running, type a second message and send it.
Look above the message box for the 'Queued messages' list with a row that starts 'Queued:'.
Wait for the reply to finish, then check the row goes and the message appears in the transcript.

items.where: Chat screen: type text in the box that reads 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' without sending, then switch to another conversation and come back

Open a different conversation from the sidebar, then open the first one again.
Look at the message box: the draft should still be there and should not appear in the transcript.

labels.text: Couldn't send. Restored here so you can try again.

items.where: Any answer in a chat > hover over the answer's bottom line (the small model name text, for example 'Auto chose ...' when Auto picked the model)
steps: Sign in and open a chat that already has an answer, or send one question and wait for the answer.
Move the mouse over the answer's bottom action line, under the answer text.
Look for the small model text that appears on hover, for example 'Auto chose ...' or the model name, and compare with Expected: the answer is distinguishable from your message and names the model.
items.needs: a sent answer in a chat
items.note: The assistant name is not a fixed label; it comes from the model label helper, so the exact words vary by model. Screen-reader naming was not checked.

items.where: The answer area while a reply is being generated, after you press Send
steps: Send any question in a chat.
Watch the answer area below your message while the reply is generated.
Check that the text grows piece by piece and that bold, lists and code blocks show as formatted text, as Expected says.

items.note: Streaming is inner behaviour; the code that renders incrementally is in StreamingMarkdownContent. Whether it actually streams depends on the model route.

items.where: New chat > type a message > Send, then look below your message for 'Preparing'
steps: Open a new chat and type any question.
Press Send.
Look just below your message for a spinning mark with the word 'Preparing', and for the status phrase 'Generating response' (announced to screen readers only).
Compare with Expected: a visible working indicator appears before or while the text arrives.
items.needs: a working model route
items.note: 'New chat' is the label of the new-chat control in the chat page; the sidebar position was not mapped.

items.where: A reasoning-capable answer > under the answer, click 'Thinking process (N steps)'
steps: Send a question to a model that produces reasoning (choose a reasoning model in the model picker).
When the answer finishes, look under it for a row starting with 'Thinking process'.
Click the row to expand it.
Compare with Expected: a collapsible list of the reasoning steps appears and collapses again on a second click.
items.needs: a model that returns thinking steps
items.note: The row only appears when the answer has thinking steps; it is not shown for all models.

items.where: An answer that used a tool > click the tool timeline row under the answer
steps: Send a question that makes the assistant use a tool (for example a web search or a file tool).
When the answer finishes, look for the tool timeline row under the answer.
Click the row (its toggle is labelled 'Toggle tool timeline') to expand it.
Compare with Expected: each tool's name, status and result appear inside.

items.note: The per-tool name, status and result fields were not individually traced to visible words.

items.where: An answer that used web search > click a numbered citation marker in the answer text
steps: Send a question that needs current information, such as a news question, with web search on.
When the answer finishes, look for small numbered markers in the answer text.
Click one marker.
Compare with Expected: it opens or points to the source the claim came from.

labels.text: Project files used in this answer

steps: Send a question that uses web search and wait for the answer to finish.

Click 'Download generated file' on the card (or 'Share generated file').

Click one card.
Compare with Expected: the artifact opens in the artifact panel or viewer.

items.where: Any answer > action row under the answer > 'Copy message' (tooltip 'Copy')
