items.where: Top bar of a chat that has messages > "Share conversation" button (text "Share" shows on wide windows) > dialog "Share conversation" > "Create public link · 7 days" (or "Copy" once a link exists). Per answer: hover the answer, open "More message actions" > "Share answer".
steps: Open or start a chat and send one message so the chat has messages.
Click the "Share conversation" button in the top bar (on wide windows it reads "Share").
In the dialog "Share conversation", leave the expiry at 7 days and click "Create public link".
Look for the link to appear with a "Copy" button and check it opens the same conversation.
For one answer: hover it, click "More message actions", then click "Share answer" and look for the system share sheet or an error toast "This answer could not be shared".
items.needs: a signed-in account with a chat that has at least one message; the answer share uses the system share sheet where the browser provides one
items.note: The header button is labelled "Share" in visible text and "Share conversation" in its accessible name; the dialog has a workspace audience option too, which I did not trace further.

items.where: Any answer > "More message actions" (the three-dot button under the answer) > the usage block at the bottom of the menu (tokens, model, request id, seconds). The model name is also shown under the answer on hover as the answered-by label.
steps: Send a message and wait for the answer to finish.
Hover the answer and look for the name of the model under it.
Click the "More message actions" button under the answer.
Scroll to the bottom of the menu, below the separator, and look for the token usage block and a time in seconds such as "2.4s".
Compare the model shown there with the Expected: which model answered and its usage.
items.needs: a completed answer from a route that sends token counts (not every provider sends them)
items.note: The usage block has no fixed heading. It appears only when the answer carries token counts, and its wording comes from the TokenUsageDisplay component; the model name under the answer is data, not a fixed label.

items.where: A chat whose answer fails after some text has already arrived > the answer keeps its text above a status line "Response failed" (with the reason after it), or "Response cancelled. Partial response saved.", or "Response finished with errors".
steps: Send a message that a provider fails partway through (for example by a provider outage or a timeout).
Look at the answer: the text that arrived should still be there, above a status line.
Read the status line: it should say "Response failed" followed by the reason, or "Response finished with errors".
Compare with Expected: the partial text must be kept and clearly marked incomplete, with the reason.
items.needs: a provider failure after output has started; this cannot be made on demand from the UI

labels.text: the part that arrived is kept above

items.note: The reason line is only shown on the turn's status row when the answer had run activity; with no activity it is a single row "Response failed: <reason>" from MessageBubble.tsx. The reasons for an interrupted turn are in a map in ChatMessageList.tsx. I did not verify a live reproduction.

items.where: An answer that the safety layer stops > the notice "The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons." with a "Report issue" button under it.
steps: Send a prompt that the model's safety layer refuses (the app cannot choose this on demand).
Look under the answer for the notice "The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons."
Check that it is not styled as an ordinary answer or a generic error.
Click "Report issue" and look for the feedback dialog that opens for a safety appeal.
Compare with Expected: a distinct refusal state with a next step.
items.needs: a prompt that triggers a provider safety refusal; this cannot be forced from the UI

labels.text: The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons.

items.note: The notice shows only when the last finish reason is a refusal or content filter. I did not find a separate refusal label for the status row.

items.where: Send a message > click the stop control while the answer is still being written > the answer shows "Response stopped." with a "Try again" button under it.
steps: Send a message that gives a long answer.
While the answer is still streaming, click the stop button (accessible name "Stop the current response").
Look under the answer for "Response stopped." and check the text that already arrived is still shown.
Click "Try again" and compare with Expected: the answer is marked stopped, keeps what arrived, and offers to try again.
items.needs: none for a Free account; a message with a long answer so you have time to press stop
items.note: The stop button has no visible word, only its accessible name. A stopped turn also gets the status line "Response cancelled. Partial response saved." from ChatMessageList.tsx. I did not verify the stop control live.

items.where: A turn that returns nothing > the answer row shows "Response failed: no response was returned." with a "Retry" button.
steps: Send a message to a model route that returns no text (the app cannot choose this on demand).
Look for an explicit status line "Response failed" with the reason "no response was returned.", not an empty answer bubble.
Check that a "Retry" button is shown with it.
Click "Retry" and compare the new outcome with Expected: an explicit no-response error with retry, not an empty bubble.
items.needs: a model route that returns an empty response; this cannot be forced from the UI
items.note: The same reason text also exists in packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/errors.json. The error-state wording is built in ChatMessageList.tsx and MessageBubble.tsx, and I did not reproduce it live.

steps: Start a new chat, send one message, and wait for the reply.
Look at the chat header title and the sidebar row for this conversation.
Check that the title is a short name based on the message, not 'New chat' or blank.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account
items.note: Title is set on the server in persist-message.ts; the chat header title button has aria-label 'Conversation options' (ConversationTitleMenu.tsx). No visible control was found.

items.where: Chat header > conversation title (button named 'Conversation options') > Rename
steps: Open a conversation that already has a title.
Click the title at the top of the chat.
Choose Rename, type a new name, and press Enter.
Reload the page and check the new name is still shown in the header and sidebar.
items.needs: none
items.note: The sidebar row menu also has Rename (packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/SessionItem.tsx). Escape cancels the rename.

items.where: Sidebar > conversation row > More options for [conversation name] > Pin (then Unpin)
steps: Hover a conversation row in the sidebar and click its More options button.
Click Pin.
Check the conversation moves to the top of the list.
Open its More options again and click Unpin.
Check it returns to its normal place.
items.needs: none
items.note: The row menu is not shown in the 'simple' sidebar mode (SessionItem.tsx checks !simple).

items.where: Chat header > conversation title (Conversation options) > Archive; restore from Sidebar > Archived ({count}) > the conversation > Unarchive
steps: Open a conversation, click its title, and choose Archive.
Check it disappears from the main sidebar list.
Open the sidebar filter labelled Archived (count) and find the conversation.
Open its menu and choose Unarchive, then check it is back in the main list.
items.needs: none
items.note: The restore item from the sidebar row menu is shown as an icon (ArchiveRestore) in SessionItem.tsx; its text was not confirmed.

items.where: Chat header > conversation title (Conversation options) > Delete
steps: Open a test conversation and click its title.
Choose Delete.
Check whether a confirmation appears before anything is removed.
Confirm, then check the conversation is gone from the sidebar and the Archived list.
items.needs: a test conversation you can delete
items.note: The menu item calls onDelete directly; the confirmation step was not found in the menu file, so check the handler before judging it. Sidebar row menu also has Delete (SessionItem.tsx).

items.where: Chat header > conversation title (Conversation options) > Duplicate as branch
steps: Open a conversation with several messages.
Click its title and choose Duplicate as branch.
Check a new conversation opens with the same messages.
Send a message in one conversation and check the other does not change.
items.needs: none
items.note: The visible word is 'Duplicate as branch', not 'Duplicate'. The item shows only when the fork handler is passed (onFork).

items.where: Chat header > conversation title (Conversation options) > Move to project (shows Change project when already in a project)
steps: Make sure at least one project exists.
Open a conversation that is not in a project and click its title.
Choose Move to project and pick a project name.
Open the project and check the conversation is listed there.
items.needs: a project already created
items.note: The menu item only appears when projects exist. The sidebar row menu also has Move to project (SessionItem.tsx).

items.where: Composer > Work or Chat mode buttons (Work is shown when the account can use Work mode)
steps: Open a conversation in Chat mode, or start a new chat.
Click Work in the composer mode buttons and check it becomes pressed.
Send a task and check the Work session panel opens for later turns.
Click Chat and check the mode switches back.
items.needs: an account that can use Work mode
items.note: The buttons are disabled while a reply is running. Switching to Chat clears the project and working folder (ChatComposerNew.tsx).

items.where: Composer > More composer options (plus button) > Use incognito (shows Exit incognito when on)
steps: Open a conversation and click More composer options.
Read the line under the temporary chat row: 'Stays out of your history, search, memory and Library.'
Click Use incognito and check the row changes to Exit incognito.
Check the chat is marked temporary, and send a message to see it is kept out of history.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Stays out of your history, search, memory and Library.

items.note: The trigger is named only by its aria-label 'More composer options'. The temporary rows show only when showTemporaryChat is set.

items.where: Open a conversation > press Command+F > Search messages box
steps: Open a conversation with several messages.
Press Command+F.
Type a word that appears in the conversation.
Check the matching messages are highlighted and the search box stays open. Press Escape to close it.
items.needs: a conversation with repeated words
items.note: The shortcut is Command+F on Mac (metaKey); it is set in ChatMessageList.tsx.

items.where: Open a conversation > Command+F > type a word > Go to next match / Go to previous match buttons
steps: Open search with Command+F and type a word with several matches.
Click Go to next match and check the transcript scrolls to the next match.
Click Go to previous match and check it goes back.
Compare the position with the match count shown in the search bar.
items.needs: a conversation with several matches for one word
items.note: These are icon buttons with aria-labels; the visible text is not shown.

items.where: Open a long conversation > scroll up > Scroll to bottom button
steps: Open a conversation with many messages.
Scroll up to an older message.
Click the Scroll to bottom button that appears.
Check the view jumps to the latest message.
items.needs: a conversation long enough to scroll
items.note: It is an icon button with an aria-label; no visible text.

items.where: Chat transcript > a message with branches > Previous branch / Next branch arrows with the n/total count
steps: Open a conversation that has branches.
Find a message with the branch control under it.
Click Next branch, then Previous branch.
Check the n/total count and the shown messages change to match the branch.
items.needs: a conversation that already has branches
items.note: How a user creates a branch (onBranch in MessageBubble.tsx) has no visible label found yet.

items.where: Chat header > conversation title (Conversation options) > Export…
steps: Open a conversation with several messages.
Click its title and choose Export….
Choose the format in the export step and save or download the file.
Open the file and check all messages, the title and the timestamps are there.
items.needs: none
items.note: The format choices (Markdown, PDF, JSON) were not found in the menu file; check the export handler in WebChatPage.tsx before judging them.

items.where: Chat header > Share conversation button (or Conversation options > Share…)
steps: Open a conversation that has messages.
Click Share conversation.
Read the read-only snapshot note and the access and expiry choices (1, 7 or 30 days).
Create a link only with a test conversation, then check the link appears.
items.needs: a test conversation and an account allowed to share
items.note: Creating a link makes a public URL; only do it on a test conversation.

items.where: Chat header > Share conversation > Revoke share (or Revoke every link)
steps: Open Share conversation on a conversation that has a live link.
Find the link in the Conversation link field.
Click Revoke share or Revoke every link and read the confirmation.
Confirm, then open the link in a private window and check it no longer works.
items.needs: a live link you created
items.note: Revoked links cannot be restored, and the dialog says a new link can still be created.

items.where: Chat header or Work session panel > Open Chat details (or Close Chat details) > Details
steps: Open a conversation and open the chat details panel with the Open Chat details control.
Find the Details section.
Compare the shown rows with the expected: created and updated time, model, message count, id and project.
items.needs: none
items.note: The exact rows in the Details section were not confirmed in the code read.

items.where: Open the session dock (Open ... session dock) > Context, Sources sections
steps: In an AGI Work conversation, open the session dock.
Find the Context section and read the tools and files it lists.
Find the Sources section and check its entries.
Compare with Expected: files, instructions, memory and token budget.
items.needs: a Work conversation with a run
items.note: Instructions, memory and token budget were not found in these dock sections; only tools and files were confirmed.

items.where: Composer > More composer options > Deep Research (and the Web search and Run code toggles)
steps: Open a conversation and set Deep Research or Web search on from the composer.
Send a message and read the reply.
Send a second message and check the same tool is still on in this conversation.
Open another conversation and check its tools are separate.
items.needs: none
items.note: Toggles are stored per conversation (composerTogglesByConversation in WebChatPage.tsx); the Web search toggle's own row was not found in the plus menu.

items.needs: a connected account
items.note: A 'Connectors' row exists in ComposerPlusMenu.tsx but renders as a coming-soon item (line 1776); the per-conversation disabledConnectorIds is passed at WebChatPage.tsx near line 2763, with no visible picker found. Searched for the conversation connector picker in apps/web/features/chat and found none.

items.where: Open the session dock (Open ... session dock) > Progress
steps: Start a Work task from a conversation.
Open the session dock.
Find the Progress section and check the task's status matches what the run shows.
items.needs: a Work conversation with an active run
items.note: The task list code at WorkSessionPanel.tsx line 295 was not verified in this read.

steps: Sign in to the same account in a second browser or device.
Open the sidebar there and find the conversation started on the first device.
Send a message from the second device and check it appears on the first after a reload.
items.needs: a second browser or device signed in to the same account
items.note: Cross-device sync is the server's job (persist-message.ts), shown in the sidebar (SessionItem.tsx); no separate control found.

items.where: Composer: type a message and press Send message; the chat then shows Preparing before the answer
steps: Open a new chat in the web app.
Type any short question in the composer.
Press the Send message button.
Look for the Preparing line with the spinning mark under your message, before any answer text appears.
items.needs: none

items.where: Composer: send a second message while the first reply is still running; a Queued chip appears beside the send button
steps: Send a question that gives a long answer.
While it is still answering, type a second message in the composer.
Press Send message.
Look for the Queued chip next to the send button (with a count if more than one is queued).
items.needs: none
items.note: A separate Queued row also exists in ChatComposerNew.tsx; which one shows depends on composer state, not verified in the running app.

items.where: Composer: send a message with an attachment; the chat shows Preparing before the model answers
steps: Open a new chat.
Attach a file with the attachment control in the composer.
Type a question about the file and press Send message.
Look for Preparing while the file is read, before the answer starts.
items.needs: a file to upload
items.note: No separate wording for reading context, attachments or memory was found; the only visible word is Preparing.

items.where: Composer: send a question that needs web search; the activity timeline shows Searching the web
steps: Send a question that needs current information from the web.
Look at the activity timeline above the answer while it runs.
Look for Searching the web, followed by the search summary if one is shown.
items.needs: a turn that uses web search

items.where: Composer: ask the model to run Python code; the code block shows Running Python while it runs
steps: Ask the model to calculate something by running Python code.
Look for the code execution block in the answer.
Look for Running Python while the step is executing, then the Output section when it finishes.
items.needs: a model route that runs code

items.where: Composer: send a request that uses a connected connector; the activity step names the connector with Using
steps: Connect a service in the app's connectors settings, then open a new chat.
Ask for something that needs that service.
Look at the activity timeline for a step that names the service with Using.
Check that the step shows the call in progress until it finishes.
items.needs: a connected connector account
items.note: The connector sentence is built from the summary text; the exact settings path to connect a service was not traced.

items.where: Composer: send a request that needs approval for a tool step; the turn shows Needs approval
steps: Send a request that triggers a tool needing approval.
Look for the Needs approval label in the activity timeline.
Look for the note Waiting for approval. This response is partial; review the tool request to continue.
Check that approve and deny controls appear on the tool step.
items.needs: a tool that asks for approval
items.note: The exact approve and deny button words were not found by search; the tester should read them on screen.

items.where: Composer: send a task where the assistant asks a question mid-task; the activity shows Waiting for your input
steps: Send a task that is vague, so the assistant needs a detail from you.
Look for the Waiting for your input label in the activity timeline.
Find the question card in the answer and type a reply into it.
Check that the turn continues after you reply.
items.needs: a task that makes the assistant ask a question
items.note: The answer control's exact visible words were not checked.

items.where: Shown in the chat thread when the first answer text arrives; the Generating response line gives way to the answer
steps: Send a question in a new chat.
Watch the Generating response line under your message.
As soon as the first words appear, check that the Generating response line is gone and the answer text is shown.
items.needs: none

items.where: Composer: send any question; the answer text appears word by word in the chat thread
steps: Open a new chat and type a question that gives a longer answer.
Press Send message.
Watch the answer grow in the chat thread while it is still running.
Check that the text grows in pieces, not all at once when the answer finishes.
items.needs: none

items.where: Composer: ask for a list, a table or a code block; check it while the answer is still streaming
steps: Send a request such as Make a table of three fruits with their colours, or Write a short Python function.
Watch the answer while it is still streaming.
Check that the table, list or code block is drawn correctly before the answer finishes.
Check that the finished answer shows the same structure.
items.needs: none

items.where: Composer: ask for a file or document; the chat shows Creating while it is built, then Created a file
steps: Ask the assistant to create a document or a small file.
Look at the artifact row in the answer while it is being made.
Look for the word Creating and the Show the code being written action.
Check that the row changes to Created a file when it is done.
items.needs: none

items.where: Composer: ask for an image or a video; the media card shows generation progress
steps: Ask the assistant to generate an image of a simple object.
Look at the media card in the answer while it generates.
Check that a progress or generating state is shown before the picture appears.
items.needs: a model route that generates images
items.note: The generating text on the media card was not found by search; the progress UI is in MessageBubble.tsx around the media card.

items.where: Chat thread: a finished turn shows no loading line and its state is named for screen readers
steps: Send a short question and wait for the answer to finish.
Check that the Generating response line and the Preparing line are gone.
Check that the answer is marked complete for screen readers, for example with the Response complete announcement.
items.needs: none
items.note: Response complete is a status string for assistive tech and was not seen as a visible label; a visible completed label was not found.

items.where: Chat thread or activity timeline: a run with some failed steps shows Finished with errors
steps: Send a request that uses several steps, such as a search plus a tool call.
Let one step fail, or wait for a run where a step fails.
Look for Finished with errors in the activity timeline or the Response finished with errors line under the answer.
Check that it is not shown as Response complete or Response failed.
items.needs: a multi-step turn where one step fails
items.note: No visible label Partially completed was found in the code.

items.where: Composer: while an answer is running, press Stop generation; the chat shows Stopping the Cloud task
steps: Send a question that gives a long answer.
Press the stop button in the composer (its tooltip says Stop generation).
Look for the Stopping the Cloud task line in the answer, below the text.
Check that the line stays until the run has stopped.
items.needs: none

items.where: Chat thread: after Stop, the answer keeps the text that arrived and shows Response stopped. with Try again
steps: Send a long question and press Stop generation partway.
Check that the text that arrived is still shown above.
Look for the line Response stopped. with a Try again button.
Look for Response cancelled. Partial response saved. in the message status if shown.
items.needs: none

items.where: Chat thread: if the network drops during a turn, the line Reconnecting... shows until it resumes
steps: Send a long question.
Turn off Wi-Fi on the Mac while the answer is running.
Look for the Reconnecting… line under the answer.
Turn Wi-Fi back on and check whether the answer continues.
items.needs: a way to drop the network connection

items.where: Shown by reopening a chat while a reply is running; the answer carries on instead of starting again
steps: Send a long question in a chat.
Close the browser tab while the answer is still running.
Open the same chat again from the sidebar.
Check that the answer continues from where it was, and that the text does not start again from the top.
items.needs: a turn that is still running when the tab is closed
items.note: No visible Resuming word was found; the effect is seen only through the answer continuing.

items.where: Chat thread: a rate-limited turn shows the rate-limit notice under the failed reply, with Retry
steps: Send a message to a model that is receiving too many requests.
Look for the notice under the reply.
Check that it says to wait and retry, and names another model if your plan has one.
items.needs: a provider rate limit, which is hard to make happen on demand

labels.text: This model is receiving too many requests right now.

items.where: Chat thread: a turn blocked by an account usage limit shows the usage notice with Usage
steps: Use an account that has reached its usage limit.
Send a message.
Look for the notice: You have reached a usage limit on your account.
Check that it points to Usage to see when it resets.
items.needs: an account at its usage limit

labels.text: You have reached a usage limit on your account.

items.note: The Usage screen location was not traced in the menus.

items.where: Chat thread: a turn that fails because sign-in expired shows the session notice
steps: Let the session expire, or sign out in another tab, then send a message.
Look for the notice: Your session ended before this turn finished.
Check whether a Sign in again control is offered next to the notice.
items.needs: an expired session

labels.text: Your session ended before this turn finished. Sign in again, then retry.

items.note: The code has the words Sign in again in the notice text, but no sign-in button tied to it was found.

items.where: Activity timeline: when a step needs your desktop and it is offline, the step shows Waiting for your desktop
steps: Start a task that needs the desktop app, with the desktop app closed.
Look at the activity timeline in the chat.
Look for Waiting for your desktop, with the device name if one is shown.
items.needs: the desktop app linked and then offline

items.where: Chat thread: when the model provider is unavailable the notice offers Retry or another model
steps: Send a message to a model whose provider is down or overloaded.
Look for the notice under the reply.
Check that it says the provider is temporarily unreachable and offers Retry or another model.
items.needs: a provider outage, or a free route that is overloaded

labels.text: The model provider is temporarily unreachable.

items.where: Chat thread: a message that is too long or an attachment the model cannot read shows the fix to make, with Retry
steps: Paste a very long message, or attach a file the model cannot read.
Send it.
Look for the notice that names the problem, such as This message is too long for the selected model.
Check that the text is put back in the composer so you can fix and resend.
items.needs: a very long message or an unsupported attachment

labels.text: This message is too long for the selected model.

items.note: Failed-turn text restore was reported in an earlier run, not checked here.

items.where: Chat > send a message > the answer stops part way through > look for the "Retry" button under the failed turn
steps: Sign in and open a new chat from the first screen.
Send a long request, such as "Write a detailed 2000-word guide", so the answer runs for a while.
Wait for the connection or provider to fail while text is still arriving (this is not something a tester can force on demand; if it does not happen, mark it unsure).
Check that the text that already arrived stays on the page, and that the message says the response stopped part way through and the part that arrived is kept above.
Check that a "Retry" button is offered, and that the failed state is shown in the turn's activity details.
items.needs: a way to make the provider fail mid-answer (no reliable on-demand trigger found in the code); a Free account can reach the fallback route

labels.text: The part that arrived is kept above.

items.note: The failure text comes from the stream_interrupted error code (apps/web/features/chat/lib/turn-error-notice.ts line 149 and apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/upstream-error-copy.ts line 101); the exact trigger is not reachable on demand, and the English text is also in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx line 117 as a lookup.

items.where: Sidebar > Recents > open a conversation that ended as failed or stopped, after quitting and reopening the app
steps: Start a chat and let one turn finish as failed (for example a provider error) or stop it with the stop control.
Note the turn's final state: the failure text, or the stopped state.
Quit the app completely and open it again, then sign in if asked.
Find the same conversation under Recents in the sidebar and open it.
Compare the conversation and that turn's final state (failed or stopped) with what you noted before the restart.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can produce a failed or stopped turn
items.note: The restore path was located in code (packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/SessionItem.tsx and the messages persist route) but the exact sidebar section shown on the web app was not confirmed visually; the label Recents is from the shared locale file.

items.where: No control; its effect is seen in the conversation after reopening, and as a desktop notification when the reply is ready
steps: Start a long answer in a chat.
Close the browser tab or window while the answer is still generating.
Wait a minute or two, then open the app or the same conversation again from Recents.
Check that the answer is complete or still being produced, and that a desktop notification titled "Your reply is ready" appeared when the app was in the background.
items.needs: a signed-in account; desktop notification permission for the notification part
items.note: This is server-side behaviour in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts (durable run start near line 642) with the resume logic in apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts near line 3118; whether the run keeps going after a tab closes was not confirmed by reading the code alone.

items.where: Chat screen > type in the box 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' > click 'Send message'
steps: Click the message box on the chat screen.
Type: Write three short paragraphs about the sea. Leave a blank line between each paragraph.
Click 'Send message'.
When the answer finishes, check that each paragraph is separate with space between them, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Paragraph rendering is part of every answer and has no control of its own.

items.where: Chat screen > type in the box 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' > click 'Send message'
steps: Click the message box.
Type: Write a short guide with a # heading, a ## heading and a ### heading, one line under each.
Click 'Send message'.
Check that the three lines show as headings of different sizes and no # signs appear, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Chat screen > type in the box 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' > click 'Send message'
steps: Click the message box.
Type: Write three sentences: one with **bold** words, one with *italic* words, one with ~~strikethrough~~ words.
Click 'Send message'.
Check that bold, italic and struck-through text show with the right style and no asterisks or tildes remain.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: No custom style for strikethrough was found in the code I read; it uses the default text style, so check it looks struck through.

items.where: Chat screen > type in the box 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' > click 'Send message'
steps: Click the message box.
Type: Write a numbered list of four steps to make tea, starting the numbering at 3.
Click 'Send message'.
Check that the list is numbered and the first item shows the number 3, with indented items, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Chat screen > type in the box 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' > click 'Send message'
steps: Click the message box.
Type: Write a bulleted list of four fruits.
Click 'Send message'.
Check that each fruit has a bullet marker and is indented, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Chat screen > type in the box 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' > click 'Send message'
steps: Click the message box.
Type: Write a bulleted list of three countries. Under the second country add a nested bulleted list of two cities.
Click 'Send message'.
Check that the two cities sit one level deeper than their country, with more indent, as Expected says.

items.note: The list rules are at packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownContent.tsx lines 450-480, not lines 349; nesting uses the default list items.

items.where: Chat screen > type in the box 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' > click 'Send message'
steps: Click the message box.
Type: Write a to-do list in Markdown with one item done using - [x] and one item not done using - [ ].
Click 'Send message'.
Check that the first item shows a ticked box and the second an empty box, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: In chat answers the checkboxes only show their state; clicking them changes nothing, because only the artifact preview passes a toggle handler.

items.where: Chat screen > type in the box 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' > click 'Send message'

Type: Quote one famous line from a book, written as a Markdown blockquote starting with >.
Click 'Send message'.
Check that the quote is indented with a vertical bar at its left and looks different from normal text, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Chat screen > type in the box 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' > click 'Send message'

Click 'Send message'.
Check that a horizontal divider line appears between the two paragraphs, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: No custom divider component was found; the line comes from the default page styles, so check it is visible in light and dark themes.

items.where: Chat screen > type in the box 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' > click 'Send message'
steps: Click the message box.
Type: Write one sentence that names the command `ls -la` in backticks.

items.where: Chat screen > type in the box 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' > click 'Send message' > hover the code block
steps: Click the message box.
Type: Write a Python function in a fenced code block that prints hello, with normal indentation.
Click 'Send message'.
Hover the code block and check the monospace text keeps its indentation and the 'Copy code' button is there, as Expected says.

items.where: Chat screen > type in the box 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' > click 'Send message' > click the link in the answer

Type: Write one sentence with the link [example site](https://example.com) in it.

items.where: Chat screen > type in the box 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' > click 'Send message' > click the address in the answer

Click 'Send message'.
Check the address shows as an underlined link, click it and see it open in a new tab, as Expected says.

items.note: Bare links are turned into links by remark-gfm (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/remarkPlugins.ts line 1).

items.where: Chat screen > type in the box 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' > click 'Send message' > click the footnote marker
steps: Click the message box.
Type: Write one sentence and put the footnote marker [^1] after it, then end the answer with the note [^1]: a short source note.

Click the marker and check it jumps to the note at the bottom, and that the note links back, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Footnote links are handled in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownContent.tsx lines 336-360; no superscript style was found in the code I read, so check the marker looks raised.

items.where: Chat screen > type in the box 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' > click 'Send message'
steps: Click the message box.

items.where: Chat screen > type in the box 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' > click 'Send message' > scroll the table sideways
steps: Click the message box.

Scroll the table sideways inside the answer (or swipe on a phone width) and check the page does not overflow and the last columns can be reached, as Expected says.

items.note: The sideways scroll is in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownTable.tsx line 146, not MarkdownContent.tsx line 460; a table with more cells in a row than its header is shown as a read-only code block instead.

items.where: Chat screen > hover over a table in an answer (on touch screens the buttons always show) > click the 'Download as CSV' button at the top right of the table

Hover over the table so its buttons appear.
Click the 'Download as CSV' button (icon only).
Open the downloaded table.csv and check its rows match the table, as Expected says.

items.note: Only CSV download exists in the code read; no XLSX option was found, so Expected's XLSX part cannot be checked.

items.where: Chat screen > type in the box 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' > click 'Send message'
steps: Click the message box.

items.where: Chat screen, while an answer is still typing in after 'Send message' is clicked
steps: Click the message box and type: Write a 300-word article with a heading, some bold words and a bulleted list.
Click 'Send message'.
Watch the answer while it types: headings and bold text should show as formatted, not as raw # or ** marks.
When it finishes, compare with the same text in the final answer, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Streaming rendering is shown only while the reply streams; it has no control of its own.

items.where: Chat screen, while an answer that contains a code block is still streaming in
steps: Click the message box and type: Write a 20-line Python script in a fenced code block.
Click 'Send message'.
Watch while the answer streams: the code should appear inside a code box as soon as the opening fence arrives, before the closing fence.
When it finishes, check the code box stays whole, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The fence closing is handled in packages/platform/utils/src/markdownSource.ts (closeUnterminatedCodeFence); a streaming-only effect.

items.where: Any assistant answer that contains HTML tags
steps: Click the message box and type: Reply with exactly this text: bold and
Click 'Send message'.

items.note: The model decides whether HTML appears; the sanitizer runs in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownContent.tsx around line 821, and user messages show tags as plain text.

items.where: Chat screen > type in the box 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' > click 'Send message' > click the link in the answer
steps: Click the message box.

items.where: Chat screen > type in the box 'Ask anything. Type / for commands' > click 'Send message' > drag-select in the answer
steps: Click the message box and type: Write a heading, a paragraph, a bulleted list and a short Python code block.
Click 'Send message'.

items.where: Chat with at least one message > click 'Conversation options' near the title > 'Print' or 'Export…'
steps: Open a chat that has an answer with a heading, a list, a table, a code block and a formula.
Click 'Conversation options', then click 'Export…'.
In the dialog 'Export Chat History', choose 'PDF' or 'Word Document' and click the export button.

Open the file and compare its headings, lists, tables, code and maths with the answer on screen, as Expected says. For print, click 'Conversation options' > 'Print' and check the print preview keeps the same formatting.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The export button text is built as 'Export' plus the format name; output formatting was not checked in code. A separate per-answer 'Save as document' item exists under 'More message actions'.

steps: Click the message box.

Click 'Send message'.
Check the Arabic and Hebrew text is right-aligned and reads right to left, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Direction is set with dir="auto" on the message text (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx) and detected in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/textDirection.ts.

items.where: Open a conversation with an answer > press Command+F (Ctrl+F also works) > the "Search messages..." field at the top of the message list
steps: Open a conversation whose answer has several paragraphs and repeated words.
Press Command+F. The "Search messages..." field opens and is selected.
Type a word that appears in the answer.
Look at the rendered answer: the matching words should be highlighted in the text itself, not only in the search field.
Press Enter for the next match and Shift+Enter for the previous one, or use "Go to next match" and "Go to previous match"; check that the view moves to each match.
Press Escape or click "Close search" to end the search.
items.needs: a conversation with an answer (any signed-in account that has one)
items.note: Command+F is handled in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx and accepts Command or Ctrl; the match count display was not confirmed in the code.

items.where: Open a conversation > the Conversation options button at the top of the chat (icon button, no visible text) > Print, or Export… > Export Chat History dialog > Export PDF
steps: Open a conversation with an answer that has a heading, a list, a table, a code block and a math formula.
Click the Conversation options button at the top of the chat, then click Print.
In the print preview, compare the headings, lists, table, code and math with the screen.
Cancel the print. Click the Conversation options button, then click Export….
Choose PDF in Export Chat History, click the Export PDF button, open the downloaded file and compare its headings, lists, table, code and math with the screen.
items.needs: a conversation with a formatted answer (heading, list, table, code, math)
items.note: The menu shows only when the conversation has messages and a title; the header button's visible name is only the aria label "Conversation options"; the export button label is built as "Export" plus the format name (EnhancedExportDialog.tsx line 286), and export builds the file from the conversation's Markdown.

items.where: Any chat message that contains Arabic or Hebrew text (sent by you or written by the assistant)
steps: Type a message in Arabic or Hebrew in the message box and send it.
Ask the assistant for a short answer written in Arabic or Hebrew.
Look at the user and assistant bubbles: the text should start from the right edge and be right-aligned, with the direction following the text.
items.needs: a keyboard that types Arabic or Hebrew
items.note: No control exists; the message text sets dir="auto" (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:2839), so direction follows each message's text.

labels.text: This diagram could not be drawn

items.where: Ask a question that needs a web search, then look under the answer for the "Sources" button, and look for small source chips inside the answer text

Type a question about a current topic that needs web search, for example "What is the latest news about <topic>? Include sources." and send it.

Click a chip; it opens the source in a new tab.
Compare: the chip names the site, and the chip opens the linked source.

Move the mouse away; the card closes. Click the chip only if you want to open the source.
