items.where: Artifacts panel > Download artifact (title "Download") > Download source (.ext)
steps: Open a code or text artifact in the Artifacts panel.
Click the Download button (title "Download", aria-label "Download artifact").
Click Download source; the item text ends with the file extension, for example "Download source (.html)".
Open the downloaded file and compare it with the code shown in the Source view.
items.needs: none
items.note: The menu item text is built from the language, so the extension part varies by artifact.

items.where: Artifacts panel > Download all
steps: Create a chat with two or more artifacts so the Artifacts panel shows them.
Click the Download all button (title "Download all artifacts as zip").
Wait for the toast "Preparing artifact download…" to finish.
Open the downloaded artifacts.zip and check that each artifact is inside.
items.needs: two or more artifacts in one conversation
items.note: The button shows only when there are more than one artifact (ArtifactsPanel.tsx:735); the zip is built in apps/web/features/chat/utils/downloadArtifacts.ts:163.

items.where: Artifacts panel > Publish (globe button, aria-label "Publish artifact to a public link")
steps: Open an artifact in the Artifacts panel and sign in if asked.
Click the Publish button (globe icon, title "Publish"). Its label is visible only on wide panels.
Choose an audience: "Anyone with the link", "Everyone in this workspace" or "Only people you invite".
Wait for the toast "Published · link copied to clipboard" or "Published. Copy the link from the bar below."
Open the link in a private window and compare the page with the artifact.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Whether a Free account can publish was not checked in the code.

items.where: Artifacts panel > Version history (title "Version history") > Restore beside an older version
steps: Open an artifact that has more than one version.
Click the version counter button (title "Version history") to open the list.
Click Restore beside an older version, then Restore in the confirmation "Restore version N?".
Check that the content matches the older version and that a new latest version was added.
items.needs: an artifact with at least two versions
items.note: A second route exists: the more menu item "Restore version N" (ArtifactPreview.tsx:2346) when viewing an older version. The label of the trigger that opens that menu was not confirmed.

items.needs: a Free account or a paid account, and a workbook request
items.note: No insert-chart control was found in apps/web or packages/ui. Charts come only from the workbook file builder (apps/web/lib/services/managed-workbook-builder.ts, a sheet's optional chart field, bar, line or pie), so the route is asking chat for an .xlsx file with a chart. The visible route and its download control were not verified.

items.where: Presentation artifact > Edit chart data > Chart type
steps: Ask chat for a slide deck that includes a chart, then open the presentation artifact.
Click the Edit chart data button under the slide.
Open the Chart type selector and choose Line or Pie (Bar, Line and Pie are the options).
Click Apply.
Compare the chart on the slide with the chosen type.
items.needs: a presentation with a chart (ask chat to make one)
items.note: The selector is only in the deck chart editor; the spreadsheet artifact has no chart-type control in the files checked.

items.where: Presentation artifact > Edit chart data
steps: Open a presentation artifact that has a chart.
Click Edit chart data.
Look at the Chart data table: one row per data point, one column per series.
Change a value in a cell, add or remove a row, then click Apply.
Compare the plotted values with the table.
items.needs: a presentation with a chart
items.note: The editor edits the chart's own rows and series values. No picker for a sheet cell range was found, so Expected's cell-range wording is only partly matched.

items.where: Chat > Code Execution block > click Code Execution to expand
steps: Attach a data file and ask chat to analyse it with Python and draw a chart.
Wait until a Code Execution block appears under the reply; it says Running Python… while it runs.
Click the Code Execution header to expand it.
Look for the Output label, any text output, and any chart image.
Compare with Expected: code, output and charts should all be visible.
items.needs: a data file to upload, and an account that allows code execution (plan not verified)
items.note: CodeExecutionBlock shows output and images. The Python source itself was not found in this component, so whether the code is visible was not verified.

items.where: Chat > table artifact > click a column heading to sort
steps: Ask chat for a result as a table or spreadsheet, then open the table artifact.
Click a column heading.
Look for the arrow and the change in row order.
Click the same heading again and check that the order reverses.
Compare with Expected: the result table is sortable.
items.needs: none beyond a chat that returns a table
items.note: Sorting is in the spreadsheet artifact. The text Sort by is the hover title of each heading button, not a visible label. Whether a query or analysis produces this table was not verified.

items.needs: a spreadsheet artifact
items.note: The web download menu offers only Download as CSV for tables. The Export as Excel item in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/ArtifactRenderer.tsx shows only when a host passes onExportNative, and apps/web does not use ArtifactRenderer. An .xlsx file can be requested from chat through the file tool in apps/web/lib/services/managed-office-file-service.ts, but its download control was not found.

items.where: Spreadsheet artifact > Download artifact > Download as CSV
steps: Open a spreadsheet or table artifact.
Click the download icon (its hidden name is Download artifact).
Click Download as CSV.
Open the saved .csv file.
Compare the rows and columns with the table on screen.
items.needs: a spreadsheet or table artifact
items.note: The menu item appears only for artifact types spreadsheet, table and csv.

items.where: Chart artifact > PNG
steps: Ask chat for a chart, then open the chart artifact.
Click the PNG button in the chart toolbar.
Open the saved .png file.
Compare the picture with the chart on screen.
items.needs: a chart artifact
items.note: The PNG button has the hidden name Download <chart name> as PNG. Nothing in the chart export code produces a file other than PNG.

items.where: Document artifact > Download artifact > Download as Word (.docx)
steps: Ask chat to analyse the data and write a report, then open the document artifact.
Click the download icon (its hidden name is Download artifact).
Click Download as Word (.docx) or Download as PDF.
Open the saved file.
Compare its formatting with Expected: a formatted report.
items.needs: a document artifact
items.note: The menu items appear only for document artifacts that are not already PDF or DOCX. Whether an analysis turns into a document artifact was not verified.

items.needs: a slide deck from chat
items.note: The presentation download menu offers Download as PDF only, in apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx. No pptx download label was found. A .pptx file can be requested from chat through apps/web/lib/services/managed-office-file-service.ts, but its download control was not found.

items.where: Chat (first screen after sign-in) > composer "Add attachments and tools" (plus icon) > Output > Presentation, then send a message asking for a slide deck
steps: Sign in and open a new chat on a model that supports Office file creation.
Click the plus icon in the composer (its accessible name is "Add attachments and tools").
Click "Output", then click "Presentation" so it is checked.
Type a short request such as "Make a 3-slide deck about our launch plan" and send it.
When the reply shows a generated file card, click "Download" on the card (or open the preview and click "Download").
Open the downloaded file in PowerPoint or Keynote and compare with Expected: it should be a .pptx file.
items.needs: a Free or paid account on a model where Office file creation is allowed (the Output row is disabled otherwise)
items.note: The quoted Code line is stale; the export is done by the create_office_file tool (format pptx) in apps/web/lib/services/managed-office-file-service.ts, which the chat calls and attaches as a generated file for download. The plus button has no visible text, only an icon with that accessible name, and the card's download button label was only partly confirmed in the source (the card's own button has no visible text; "Download" is the preview button text).

items.where: Open a text document artifact in a chat reply > Download artifact (the Download button) > Download as PDF
steps: Open a chat that has a text document (Word-style or markdown) shown as an artifact.
Click the Download button on the artifact card (its title is Download).
Click Download as PDF in the menu.
Open the downloaded PDF and compare its text with the Expected line: a PDF of the document.
items.needs: a chat that already has a text document artifact
items.note: The PDF item is shown only when the artifact is a text document; the file was not run.

items.needs: a spreadsheet artifact in a chat
items.note: Searched ArtifactPreview.tsx for PDF export; the spreadsheet/table download menu offers Download as CSV only, and PDF export is limited to text documents and presentations. The Code line pointed to apps/web/lib/server/container-files.ts:197, which is server code with no visible control.

items.where: Open a presentation artifact in a chat reply > Download artifact (the Download button) > Download as PDF
steps: Open a chat that has a presentation (slide deck) artifact.
Click the Download button on the artifact card.
Click Download as PDF in the menu.
Open the downloaded PDF and check that it has one page per slide, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a chat that already has a presentation artifact
items.note: This menu item uses the in-browser deck export, not the E2B office template named as unfinished in the plan, so the owner step is not tested by this path.

items.where: Composer > Files > Upload from device, choose a PDF, then ask for a summary
steps: Click the Files button in the message box.
Click Upload from device and choose a PDF file.
Wait until the PDF shows in the message box, type Summarize this PDF and send.
Compare the reply with the PDF content, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a PDF file to upload

items.where: Composer > Files > Upload from device, choose a PDF, then ask a question about it
steps: Click the Files button in the message box.
Click Upload from device and choose a PDF file.
Type a question about a fact in the PDF and send.
Check that the answer matches the PDF, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a PDF file to upload

items.where: Effect is seen in the answer to a chat question that names a page of an attached PDF
steps: Attach a multi-page PDF using Files > Upload from device.
Ask a question that names one page, for example what is on page 3.
Check that the answer uses the content of that page, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a multi-page PDF file
items.note: No control of its own; the page selection is done by the server, and the Code line's quoted code was not found in the file.

items.where: Composer > Files > Upload from device, choose a PDF, then ask for its plain text
steps: Click the Files button in the message box.
Click Upload from device and choose a PDF file.
Type Give me the plain text of this PDF and send.
Compare the reply with the text in the PDF, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a PDF file to upload
items.note: There is no separate text-extraction button; it is reached by asking in chat.

items.where: Composer > Files > Upload from device, choose a scanned PDF (image only), then ask for its text
steps: Click the Files button in the message box.
Click Upload from device and choose a scanned PDF with no text layer.
Type Read the text in this scanned PDF and send.
Check whether the reply contains the readable text of the scan, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a scanned PDF with no text layer
items.note: No OCR control exists; OCR runs on the server for image-only PDFs.

items.where: Composer > Files > Upload from device, choose a PDF with a table, ask for the table, then the spreadsheet artifact > Download as CSV
steps: Attach a PDF with a table using Files > Upload from device.
Type Extract the table from this PDF as rows and columns and send.
If a table artifact appears, click the Download button on its card.
Click Download as CSV and open the file; compare the rows and columns with Expected.
items.needs: a PDF file that contains a table

items.where: Connectors (web address /connectors) > DocuSign card
steps: Open the Connectors page from the web app.
Find the DocuSign card.
Click it and follow the connect steps.
Check that a DocuSign connection appears as connected, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a DocuSign developer app (the owner step is unfinished) and an outside account (DocuSign)
items.note: The connect button label and the card's display name were not verified in the code; sending for signature was not traced past the catalog entry.

items.where: Generated Word, Excel or PowerPoint file in a chat reply > Preview (the Preview button on the artifact card)
steps: Open a chat that produced an office file (docx, xlsx or pptx) as an artifact.
Click the Preview button on the artifact card.
Look at the preview next to the file's download option.
Compare the preview with the Expected line: a preview that matches the exported file.
items.needs: a chat that produced an office file
items.note: Matching the preview to the exported file is not judged here; the Preview button's exact placement was not confirmed.

items.where: Open an artifact in the artifacts panel (title "Artifacts") > Download artifact (title "Download") > Download as HTML
steps: Sign in and open a chat that has an HTML artifact (ask AGI to make a web page if none exists).
Open the artifacts panel from the "Artifacts" button and select the artifact so its preview opens.
Click the download button (tooltip "Download", aria-label "Download artifact") in the preview header.
Click "Download as HTML" in the menu.
Open the downloaded file in a browser and compare it with Expected: a standalone HTML file of the design.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account, and a chat with an HTML artifact
items.note: The quoted line 745 and WebChatPage line 5834 no longer contain the feature; the "Download as HTML" item is at ArtifactPreview.tsx line 2388 and only appears when the artifact has more than one download option, which HTML artifacts do.

items.where: Artifacts panel (title "Artifacts") > Download all (aria-label "Download all artifacts as zip")
steps: Sign in and open a chat that has two or more artifacts.
Open the artifacts panel from the "Artifacts" button.
Click "Download all" in the panel header (the button only shows when the panel holds more than one artifact).
Wait for the toast "Artifact download ready" and open the zip file from Downloads.
Compare with Expected: the zip holds the artifacts as files. For an image artifact, open its preview and click the header button with aria-label "Download image" to export the image instead.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account, and a chat with two or more artifacts
items.note: Image export is a separate control in the preview header (ArtifactPreview.tsx line 3466, aria-label "Download image") and the ArtifactsPanel.tsx line 745 and downloadArtifacts.ts line 108 cover the zip; the quoted WebChatPage line 5834 no longer contains the feature.

items.where: Open an artifact with more than one version > Previous version (aria-label "Previous version") or the version counter "Version N of M" (Version history) > More artifact actions > Show changes or Restore version
steps: Sign in and open an artifact that has been edited at least once (two or more versions).
Click "Previous version" in the preview header to show an earlier version.
Click "More artifact actions" and choose "Show changes" to compare it with the version before it; check the summary line and the highlighted text.
To restore, click "More artifact actions" and choose "Restore version N", then click "Restore" in the dialog "Restore version N?".
Compare with Expected: the earlier version is shown again as the newest version, and the version counter increases.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account, and an artifact with at least two versions
items.note: "Show changes" is hidden for PDF, DOCX and image artifacts and needs a previous version; "Restore version" appears only when the shown version is not the latest; the version history list also has a "Restore" button per version (aria-label "Restore version N", ArtifactVersionHistory.tsx line 171).

items.where: Sidebar > Sites
steps: Click Sites in the sidebar.
Look at the list: one card per published site, with its name, its link, a visibility label and a More actions (⋯) button.
Click the ⋯ button on a card and check it offers Rename, Sharing and Unpublish.
Compare with Expected: the list shows each site's state and its actions.
items.needs: a published site (see S33.04)
items.note: The Sites page is the dashboard; Settings > Privacy > Shared links > Manage also has a second list named Published artifacts (apps/web/features/settings/sections/PublishedArtifactsSection.tsx) with Open, Copy, History and Unpublish.

items.where: Sidebar > Sites > Create
steps: Click Sites in the sidebar, then click Create.
In the chat, ask AGI to build a small app or page, for example: build a page with a button that counts clicks. Wait for the artifact to appear in the side panel.
Click Publish in the artifact panel. If the panel is narrow, open the More (⋯) button and choose Publish.
Compare with Expected: the assistant built the app from your prompt, and a link now appears above the panel with a Copy link button.
items.needs: a chat that runs on the cloud (not Local or BYOK); the Web panel refuses cloud publishing for Local, BYOK or unknown origins
items.note: The refusal for Local, BYOK and unknown origins is stated in apps/web/app/features/artifacts/page.tsx.

items.needs: none
items.note: No separate preview deployment or preview URL found; searched 'preview URL', 'preview link' and 'preview deployment' in apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts, apps/web/features/sites, apps/web/app/shared-artifact and apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts. The Publish link (S33.10) is the nearest match.

items.where: Sidebar > Sites > open a site > Settings > URL > Copy link
steps: Click Sites in the sidebar and click the name of a published site.
Open the Settings tab and find the URL section.
Click Copy link, then open a private browser window (not signed in) and paste the link.
Compare with Expected: the published site opens at its public address without signing in.
items.needs: a published site (see S33.04) and a private browser window
items.note: The artifact panel also shows the link after Publish, in a bar with a Copy link button (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx).

items.where: Sidebar > Sites > ⋯ on a site card > Sharing > Your workspace
steps: Click Sites in the sidebar.
On a site card, click the ⋯ button, then Sharing.
Choose Your workspace. If you belong to no workspace the option is greyed out with the text 'Join or create a workspace to share with its members only.'
Compare with Expected: with a workspace, the site is saved as workspace-only; open its link from a signed-out private window and check it does not open for a visitor outside the workspace.
items.needs: a workspace; a second member account is needed to check that members can open it
items.note: The artifact panel uses different wording for the same choice ('Everyone in this workspace (N)' in apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx); the signed-out check is a tester step, not a confirmed behaviour in the code.

items.where: Open the public link of a published app that uses AI, and use the app's own AI control
steps: Open the public link of a published app that uses AI in a window.
Use the app's AI action.
Compare with Expected: the app answers. If no model is available for the request, the message 'No model on your plan can answer this app right now.' appears instead.
items.needs: none

labels.text: No model on your plan can answer this app right now.

items.note: The allowance is checked on the server per request (managed usage reservation in artifact-runtime-service.ts) and has no screen; the message is the failure text for an unavailable model route, not an allowance counter.

items.where: Sidebar > Sites > site name > Settings > Versions > Restore
steps: Click Sites in the sidebar and click the name of a site that has been published more than once.
Open the Settings tab and scroll to the Versions section.
Click Restore on an older version (not the one marked Live).
Compare with Expected: the restored version is now marked Live and is the newest entry; the section says restoring republishes it as the newest.
items.needs: a published site with at least two publishes (republish it once after S33.04)
items.note: Restore calls the server and then refreshes the site; the exact wording of the Live marker is 'Live'.

items.where: Sidebar > Sites > ⋯ on a site card > Unpublish
steps: Click Sites in the sidebar.
On a test site card, click the ⋯ button, then Unpublish.
Read the confirmation dialog, which names the site and says the link stops working; click Unpublish to confirm or Cancel to stop.
Compare with Expected: a toast says the site was unpublished and the link no longer works; open the old link in a private window to check it is unavailable.
items.needs: a test site you can unpublish; this cannot be undone
items.note: The same action is also at Sites > site name > Settings > Unpublish site; the confirm button text 'Unpublish' is in apps/web/features/sites/hooks/useSiteActions.ts.

items.where: Chat > open an artifact in the side panel > More (⋯) > Duplicate
steps: Open a chat that has an artifact and open the artifact in the side panel.
Click the More (⋯) button in the panel.
Click Duplicate.
Compare with Expected: a toast says 'Duplicated. Edits here no longer touch the original.' Edit the copy and open the original to check it did not change.
items.needs: a chat with an artifact
items.note: Whether Duplicate is listed in every layout was not confirmed from the code.

items.where: Chat > open a text artifact in the side panel > Download > Download source
steps: Open a text or code artifact in the side panel.
Click the Download icon in the panel.
Click Download source (.<language>), for example .py or .html.
Compare with Expected: a file with the raw source downloads; open it in a text editor to check it matches the artifact.
items.needs: a text or code artifact
items.note: The Download source item sits in the download menu for text artifacts; the exact condition under which the menu offers it was not fully traced.

items.where: Open a published site's public link > scroll to the bottom > Report infringement or impersonation
steps: Copy a published site's link from Sites (Settings > URL > Copy link) and open it in a window.
Scroll to the bottom of the page.
Click Report infringement or impersonation.
Compare with Expected: the report page titled 'Report infringing or impersonating content' opens with the published page's address filled in.
items.needs: none
items.note: The only report link on a published site is for infringement or impersonation; no general abuse button was found, and takedown is an admin route (apps/web/app/api/admin/takedown/route.ts).

items.where: Sidebar > Sites > ⋯ on a site card > Rename, then save a name that breaks the usage policy
steps: Click Sites in the sidebar, then on a site card click the ⋯ button and Rename.
Type a name that breaks the usage policy and save.

Compare with Expected: the save is refused with 'This name cannot be used because it violates the AGI Workforce usage policy.' Other content moderation (review and takedown) has no screen for the visitor.
items.needs: a test site; do not use real or offensive content beyond what the policy check needs

labels.text: This name cannot be used because it violates the AGI Workforce usage policy.

items.note: The rename path that reaches this check was not traced end to end; the refusal text is confirmed in the route, and review and takedown for a published page are operator-side only.

items.where: Sidebar > Sites > ⋯ on a site card > Unpublish
steps: Click Sites in the sidebar and click a test site's name, then open the Data tab and note the Shared data and Personal data lists.
Go back, click the ⋯ button on the card, then Unpublish, and confirm.
Compare with Expected: the link stops working for everyone and the confirmation said visitor data is deleted; check the old link is unavailable.
items.needs: a test site you can unpublish; this cannot be undone
items.note: No separate 'Delete app' control was found; Unpublish is the only removal, its confirmation says visitor data is deleted (apps/web/features/sites/hooks/useSiteActions.ts), and whether the app record itself is removed was not confirmed.

items.where: Open a conversation with messages > press Command+F (or click the search control in the chat header if shown)
steps: Open a conversation that has several messages.
Press Command+F. A bar with the placeholder "Search messages..." appears.
Type a word that appears in the conversation.
Click "Go to next match" or "Go to previous match" (or press Enter and Shift+Enter in the box).
Check the match count beside the box and that the view jumps between the matching messages, as Expected says.
items.needs: a conversation with several messages that contain a shared word
items.note: The Command+F listener is in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx; the on-screen control for opening it was not confirmed.

items.where: Sidebar > Search > Search your workspace (type a title or message text, press Enter)
steps: Click "Search" in the sidebar, or press Shift+Command+F.
Type a word from a past conversation's title or messages in the box "Search your workspace" and press Enter.
Leave the category on "All" and read the results list.
Click a result that is a conversation and check that it opens that chat.
Compare with Expected: titles and message text are both matched and the chat opens.
items.needs: a Free or paid account with at least one past conversation containing a known word
items.note: Which conversations are visible in history is decided by the server route apps/web/app/api/search/route.ts, not by visible text.

items.where: Sidebar > Search > Projects (category chip), or Sidebar > Projects > Search projects...
steps: Click "Search" in the sidebar.
Type the name or a word from the description of a project.
Click the category chip "Projects" under the box, then read the results.
Click a result with the project's name and check that it opens that project.
Compare with Expected: the project is found by name or description.
items.needs: a Free or paid account with at least one Project
items.note: The Projects page search field was found in ProjectGallery.tsx; I did not confirm that the Projects page is the screen a person reaches from the sidebar label.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Search files and projects
steps: Click "Library" in the sidebar.
Click in the box "Search files and projects" and type part of a file name.
Watch the list narrow to matching items.
Clear the box and check that the full list returns.
Compare with Expected: the box filters Library items by name.
items.needs: a Free or paid account with some saved files, images or documents in Library
items.note: The box's accessible name is "Search the library by name"; the API passes the query to the server, and I did not verify whether prompt text is also matched.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Artifacts (tab) > Search files and projects
steps: Click "Library" in the sidebar.
Click the tab "Artifacts" under the search box.
Type part of an artifact's title in "Search files and projects".
Click the matching artifact to open it.
Compare with Expected: the artifact is found by title and opens.
items.needs: a Free or paid account with at least one saved artifact
items.note: The old route /chat/artifacts redirects to the Library surface filter; content matching beyond the title was not confirmed.

items.where: Chat composer > + > Connectors
steps: Open a new chat and click the "+" in the composer.
Click "Connectors" to open its submenu.
Turn on a connected source (for example Drive or Slack) with its checkbox.
Send a question that asks for information stored in that source.
Compare with Expected: the answer draws on the connected source.
items.needs: a paid account with at least one connected work source (Drive, Slack or Notion)
items.note: The submenu shows a coming-soon item when connectors are not released, and the server-side retrieval was not checked.

items.where: Chat composer > + > Search the web (menu item; the active chip reads "Web search")
steps: Open a new chat and click the "+" in the composer.
Click "Search the web" to turn it on, then check the chip that shows "Web search".
Ask a question about a current public topic.
Read the answer and look for sources or citations from the web.
items.needs: none
items.note: The menu item was found in AttachmentMenu.tsx; I did not confirm it is the exact menu the web composer shows.

items.where: Sidebar > Search > Filters > From Date / To Date
steps: Click "Search" in the sidebar and type a query.
Click the "Filters" button under the box.
Click "From Date" and pick a date, then "To Date" and pick a later date.
Read the results list and check that every result falls inside the chosen range.
Compare with Expected: results outside the range are not shown.
items.needs: a Free or paid account with past conversations spread over several dates
items.note: The Filters panel only appears when the search can filter conversations; filtered-result accuracy is not verified by the code read.

items.needs: a Project with sources added
items.note: Found the project Sources panel (apps/web/features/projects/components/SourcesPanel.tsx) with filter, sort and search controls, but found no visible control for a named source collection or for limiting chats to one.

items.where: Sidebar > Search > Recent Searches (shown when the box is empty)
steps: Click "Search" in the sidebar and run one search so it is stored.
Close the dialog, open "Search" again and leave the box empty.
Look for the "Recent Searches" heading with query chips under it.
Click a chip and check that the query runs.
Compare with Expected: a previous query is offered and can be picked.
items.needs: none
items.note: Only recent searches were found; no popular or typed-completion suggestions were found in the code.

items.where: Chat > under the latest answer > Follow-up suggestions
steps: Send a question that uses web search and wait for the answer to finish.
Look below the answer for the region "Follow-up suggestions".
Click one suggestion.
Check that it is sent as the next message in the chat.
Compare with Expected: a tap sends the refined query.
items.needs: a Free or paid account; follow-up suggestions must be turned on in settings
items.note: The suggestions show only when the follow-up setting is on, so the settings label was not checked.

items.needs: a query that the assistant finds ambiguous
items.note: Found the clarify tool name ask_clarifying_questions in apps/web/lib/services/clarify-tool-service.ts and a clarify card at apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/cards/ClarifyCard.tsx, but did not read its visible wording or confirm the path a person takes.

items.where: Sidebar > Search > type a query > results list
steps: Click "Search" in the sidebar and type a word you know is in a chat.
Press Enter and wait for the results.
Read each result: it shows a type label (for example "Title", "Project" or "Artifact") and the matched word in highlight.
Compare with Expected: each result shows a preview before it is opened.
items.needs: a Free or paid account with a known word in past chats
items.note: Result previews in the dialog were found; citation previews are covered under S34.25.

items.where: Chat > answer with web sources > "Sources" button under the answer > Citations / More
steps: Ask a question that uses web search and wait for the answer.
Click the "Sources" button under the answer.
Read the sections "Citations" and "More" in the panel.
Check that each source card shows a title, site and link.
Compare with Expected: each source card has at least title, site and link.
items.needs: a Free or paid account with web search turned on
items.note: Card fields (title, site, link) were not read line by line.

items.where: Chat > answer with citations > hover or tap a numbered citation chip
steps: Ask a question that uses web search and wait for the answer.
Hover (or tap on a touch screen) over a citation chip in the answer text.
Read the preview that opens over the answer.
Check it shows the source title, site and snippet.
Compare with Expected: the preview shows without leaving the answer.
items.needs: a Free or paid account with web search turned on
items.note: The chip preview is built in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/CitationChip.tsx; the exact preview words for title and snippet were not extracted.

items.where: Chat > answer > "View N sources" button > More
steps: Ask a question that uses web search and wait for the answer.
Click the compact line "View N sources" under the answer.
Look for the "More" section after "Citations".
Compare the full list with the sources the answer used and consulted.
Compare with Expected: the compact summary expands to the full list.
items.needs: a Free or paid account with web search turned on, and an answer with several sources
items.note: The count label is a translation template; the spoken number depends on how many sources the answer has.

items.where: Chat > answer > click a citation chip or a source card title
steps: Ask a question that uses web search and wait for the answer.
Click a citation chip, or a source in the Sources panel.
Check that a new browser tab opens with the original page.
Compare with Expected: the original page or document opens.
items.needs: a Free or paid account with web search turned on
items.note: The links open in a new tab (target _blank) in CitationChip.tsx and ResearchPanel.tsx; the visible link text was not extracted.

items.where: Chat > answer > hover or tap a citation chip > read the "Retrieved" line
steps: Ask a question that uses web search and wait for the answer.
Hover or tap a citation chip.
Read the date line that starts with "Retrieved" and any published date above it.
Compare with Expected: the source shows its publication or retrieval date.
items.needs: a Free or paid account with web search turned on
items.note: The date appears only when the source has the date data; the Sources panel date display was not confirmed.

items.where: Sidebar > Search > type a nonsense word (for example zzqx9) and press Enter
steps: Click "Search" in the sidebar.
Type a word that matches nothing and press Enter.
Read the empty state: "No results found" with "Try different keywords or clear filters".
Check that old results are not kept on screen.
Compare with Expected: an explicit empty state is shown.
items.needs: none
items.note: The unavailable state shows "Search could not be completed" with a "Retry" button; reaching it needs the search service to fail, which a tester cannot trigger from the UI.

items.where: Composer > + menu > Deep Research, then send a question
steps: Open the + menu under the chat box.
Click Deep Research so it is switched on.
Type a research question and press send.
Look for the Deep research status card in the reply, showing a phase such as Planning research.
items.needs: a paid account (a Free account sees the Upgrade to use Deep Research message)
items.note: The visible name of the + button itself was not found in the code; the menu row label is confirmed.

items.where: Composer > + menu > Deep Research, send a question > Research plan card > Deliverable
steps: Turn on Deep Research and send a question.
When the Research plan card appears, find the Deliverable box.
Pick Executive summary or Full report.
Open the Format list and pick a format such as Bullet brief, then compare with the choices shown in Expected.
items.needs: a paid account

items.where: Research plan card (shown after sending a Deep Research question) > Add a step / Remove this step / Start research
steps: Send a Deep Research question and wait for the Research plan card.
Change the words in a step box (Research step 1, 2...).
Click Add a step, or click the X beside a step to remove it.
Click Start research and check that the searches follow the edited steps.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: The plan card only appears while the run is waiting for approval.

items.where: Research plan card > Add a source > My files / Only this site / Never this site / Connected app > Add
steps: On the Research plan card, open the Add a source list.
Choose a kind: Only this site, Never this site, My files or Connected app.
Click Add.
Look for the chip under Sources for this run, or the text Searching the whole web. Add a source to narrow it. when the list is empty.
items.needs: a paid account; for Connected app, a connected work app

items.where: Research plan card > Add a source > Only this site or Never this site, then type a site > Add
steps: On the Research plan card, set Add a source to Only this site or Never this site.
Type a domain in the Site to add box (placeholder nature.com, who.int) and press Enter, or click Add.
Look for the chip, which reads Never plus the domain for a restricted site.
Start the run and compare the report's sources with the chosen site rule.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: Enforcement happens on the server; the code I read does not show how a run is judged against the rule.

items.where: Research plan card > Add a source > My files > Add
steps: On the Research plan card, set Add a source to My files.
Click Add.
Look for the My files chip under Sources for this run.
Start the run and check that the report cites your uploaded material.
items.needs: a paid account, a file to upload
items.note: The card adds a My files source, but I found no file picker in this component; where the files are chosen was not confirmed.

items.where: Research plan card > Add a source > Connected app > Choose an app > Add
steps: On the Research plan card, set Add a source to Connected app.
Open the Choose an app list and pick a connected app.
Click Add.
Look for the app's name as a chip under Sources for this run.
items.needs: a paid account, a connected work app (such as Drive or Slack); the option only appears when an app is connected
items.note: How an app gets connected was not confirmed in this file.

items.where: Chat reply > Deep research status card (above the answer)
steps: Start a Deep Research run and watch the status bar of the reply.
Read the phase text, such as Planning research, Searching the web or Writing report.
Read the counts on the right: searches and sources, and the elapsed time (m:ss).
Check that the counts go up while the run is working.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: Counts only appear once they are above zero.

items.where: Deep research status card > Research plan step list under the status bar
steps: Start a Deep Research run and let it work.
Look at the list under the status bar, labelled Research plan.
Read the status word on each step, and Not run on steps that were dropped.
Compare with the steps as they run.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: This is a step list with status words, not a dated timeline. The status words for running and queued come from runStatusLabel, which I did not open, so their exact wording is unverified.

items.where: Under the answer, click View N sources (or the globe button titled Research sources) > Sources tab
steps: Under a Deep Research answer, click the View N sources button.
In the side panel, check that the Sources tab is selected.
Read the Citations and More lists.
Compare the list with the sources the run visited.
items.needs: a paid account, a finished or running Deep Research answer

items.where: Research side panel > Sources tab (open from View N sources)
steps: Open the Sources tab of the research side panel.
Click or read a source row: the host, the Published and Retrieved dates, and the excerpt.
Compare the evidence excerpts with the report's statements.
items.needs: a paid account, a finished Deep Research answer
items.note: Excerpts appear only when the source has one; I did not confirm the excerpt display in the row markup.

items.where: Research side panel > Report tab > Planned questions
steps: Open a finished report in the Report tab.
Find the section headed Planned questions.
Read each line marked Answered or Not answered, and the reason under open questions.
Compare with the report body.
items.needs: a paid account, a finished report with planned questions
items.note: The code shows questions with their status, not findings grouped under each question.

items.where: Deep research status card > Steer
steps: While the run is searching, click Steer.
Type in the box Add a focus, a question or a source to cover.
Click Send.
Look for the line Your guidance is applied when the current step finishes, and the plan updates to follow it.
items.needs: a paid account, a run that is still searching

labels.text: Add a focus, a question or a source to cover

items.where: Deep research status card > Pause, then Resume
steps: While the run is searching, click Pause.
Wait for the label to read Pausing… and then the status to read Research paused.
Click Resume (optionally type guidance in the box next to it).
Check that the run continues from the step it stopped at.
items.needs: a paid account, a run that is still searching

items.where: Composer > Stop the current response (tooltip Stop generation) during a run; or Research plan card > Cancel before searching starts
steps: Start a Deep Research run.
Click the stop button in the composer while the run works, or click Cancel on the Research plan card before it searches.
Look for the status Research stopped and the note (stopped by you).
Check that the run no longer adds searches.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: I did not confirm that the composer stop button also records the run as cancelled; the plan Cancel path does set the phase to interrupted.

items.where: Research side panel > Report tab (or Library) > report banner after a stopped run
steps: Stop a Deep Research run after some searching has happened.
Open its report from the Report tab.
Read the banner under the title, which begins This report is followed by the report status.
Check that the report has the material gathered before the stop.
items.needs: a paid account, a run that is stopped before the report is written
items.note: The partial-report banner text is built from the report status; the word partial was not found in the report view code, so the label wording is unverified.

items.where: Under the answer, View N sources > Report tab (or Library > open a report) > Read report full screen
steps: Open a finished report in the Report tab.
Check the title, the summary, the body and the sources.
Click Read report full screen to open the reader at full size.
items.needs: a paid account, a finished report

items.where: Report reader > Contents box (above the body)
steps: Open a finished report with at least three headings.
Look for the box titled Contents.
Click one heading in the list.
Check that the page scrolls to that section.
items.needs: a paid account, a finished report with three or more headings

items.where: Report reader > body, numbered citations; Research side panel > Sources tab
steps: Open a finished report that has numbered citations in its text.
Click a citation number in the body.
Check that it takes you to or opens its source.
Compare the link with the matching source in the Citations list.
items.needs: a paid account, a finished report with citations
items.note: The link format was read from the code, not seen on screen; the exact visible look of a citation number was not confirmed.

items.where: Plan card > Deliverable > Format > Prose with comparison tables; then read the report body
steps: Send a Deep Research question and wait for the Research plan card.
Under Deliverable, open Format and pick Prose with comparison tables.
Start research and open the finished report.
Check that tables render in the body. Charts written as chart blocks render inline in the body.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: Charts have no control of their own; they appear only when the model writes a chart block, so the tester cannot choose them.

items.where: Research side panel > Library tab (open from View N sources or the Research sources button)
steps: Open the research side panel and click the Library tab.
Read the list of reports, newest first.
Click a report title to reopen it.
Scroll to the end of the list and check for Load older reports.
items.needs: a paid account, at least one past report (the empty state says No reports yet)

items.where: Report reader toolbar > Run again
steps: Open a finished report.

Look for a new Deep research status card in the chat.
Compare the new run's results with the old report.
items.needs: a paid account, a finished report with a question

items.where: Report reader toolbar > Markdown, PDF or Word
steps: Open a finished report.
Click PDF in the toolbar and check that a file downloads.
Repeat with Word and Markdown.

items.needs: a paid account, a finished report

items.where: Report reader toolbar > Artifact
steps: Open a finished report.

Look for a new artifact opened from the report.

items.needs: a paid account, a finished report
items.note: Whether the artifact becomes an interactive page depends on the model; the toolbar button only creates the artifact.

items.where: Deep research status card > Get a notification when this research finishes > Enable
steps: Start a Deep Research run in the browser while the card shows Searching the web.
Click Enable in the footer and allow notifications in the browser prompt.
Wait for the run to finish or fail.
Look for the browser notification and the completed status in the chat.
items.needs: a paid account, a browser that allows notifications, a run that stays active

labels.text: Get a notification when this research finishes

items.note: The footer only shows while the run is active and browser permission is still default; push notifications were not checked.

items.where: Composer plus button > Research (turn on), send a research question, then wait for the "Research plan" card to show its "Start research" button. The line "You have ... available right now." sits above "Start research".
steps: Sign in with an account that has managed usage (a paid or Free plan with credits).
In the message box, open the plus (attachment) menu and choose "Research" so it is checked.
Type a research question and send it.
Wait until the "Research plan" card appears and asks you to approve the plan (it is not running yet).
Look under the plan steps for "Estimated cost: up to about ..." and the line "You have ... available right now." Compare the credit amount with the remaining credits you expect.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account with managed credits; the research plan must be waiting for approval
items.note: The Expected line says runs or credits; the screen shows only a credit amount ("You have X available right now."), with no run count, and the line is hidden when usage data is missing. The item's "Where to find it: not written yet" is outdated because the code exists at apps/web/features/chat/components/research/ResearchCostEstimate.tsx and is used by ResearchActivity.tsx:805. The exact plus-button label was not found in the files read, so the menu opener is described by position only.

items.where: In a chat answer that searched the web: small pill chips showing a site name sit at the end of claims. Each chip's accessible name reads "Source {{indices}}: {{sites}}".
steps: Sign in and open a chat.
Send a question that makes the answer search the web for current facts.
Look for small rounded pill chips with a site name placed right after a sentence in the answer.
Compare with Expected: claims should carry an inline marker naming the source.

items.note: The code does not show which question triggers web search, so the tester must find one that does.

items.where: Chat answer > "Show sources" button under the answer (tooltip "Sources") > Research panel tab "Sources".
steps: Open a chat answer that used web sources.
Hover the book icon under the answer and click "Show sources".
In the panel on the right, look at the bold first line of each source row.
Compare with Expected: each cited source shows its title.

items.where: Chat answer > "Show sources" button under the answer > Research panel tab "Sources" (the grey line under each source title).
steps: Open a chat answer that used web sources.
Click "Show sources".
Read the grey line under each source title; it shows the site domain.
Hover a site-name pill in the answer to see the same info in the tooltip.
Compare with Expected: each source names its publisher or site.
items.needs: a web-search answer
items.note: The shown domain is the publisher's, not the search router's, per the code comments.

items.where: Chat answer > "Show sources" button > Research panel tab "Sources" > click a source row.
steps: Open a chat answer that used web sources and click "Show sources".
Click one source row.
Look for a new browser tab opening the source page.
Compare with Expected: the source opens from its row.

items.where: Chat answer > "Show sources" button > Research panel tab "Sources" (source row text); also the "Report" tab > Sources list.

Look at the grey line under a source title for a date.
If there is no date, check the "Report" tab on a Deep Research report.
Compare with Expected: cited sources show a publication date when the source has one.

items.note: The date is shown only when the source provides one, so an answer may show none.

items.where: Chat answer > "Show sources" button > Research panel tab "Sources" (grey line under a source title).
steps: Open a chat answer that used web sources and click "Show sources".
Read the grey line under a source title.
Look for "Retrieved" followed by a date.
Compare with Expected: each source shows when it was retrieved.

items.where: Chat answer: source chips show a globe icon for web sources; project files show a file icon in the group "Project files used in this answer"; past chats show a chat icon in the group "Previous chats this answer used".
steps: Open a chat answer that used web sources and look at the small globe icon in the site-name pill.
Open a chat answer that cited a project file (see S36.09) and look for the file icon.

items.where: Chat answer > hover a site-name pill (tooltip) or > "Show sources" > Research panel tab "Sources" (text under the source title).

Click "Show sources" and read the short text under a source title.

items.note: The code shows the source snippet, trimmed to 180 characters, but does not mark it as a quote, so the tester judges that by reading.

In the answer, find the group of chips "Project files used in this answer".
Read the chip that shows the file name and "p." followed by a number.
Click the chip and look whether the file preview opens on that page.
Compare with Expected: the citation names the page and opens the file there.

labels.text: Project files used in this answer

items.where: Chat answer that used past chats > group "Previous chats this answer used" > click a chip (opens the earlier chat at that message).

Ask a question that makes the answer draw on that earlier chat.
Find the group "Previous chats this answer used" under the answer.
Click one chip and look for the earlier chat opening with that message highlighted.
Compare with Expected: the citation opens the exact message.

items.where: Chat answer: the source chip sits right after the sentence it supports (site-name pill).

Read each sentence and find the small pill chip placed right after it.
Hover the chip to see which source it names.
Compare with Expected: each chip sits at the claim it supports.

Look for a site-name chip showing "+" and a number.
Hover the chip and read the tooltip list.
Compare with Expected: all sources for the claim are visible.

items.where: Chat > Deep research report > "Report" tab in the Research panel > bottom of the report, section "Sources".

Open the downloaded file.

items.where: Projects list in another app signed in with the same account
steps: Sign in with the same account in another app (desktop, mobile or the Chrome extension).
Open Projects in that app.
Check that the same notebook list appears and that the notebook opens with its sources.
items.needs: a second app signed in with the same account
items.note: Sync is server-side; no control was found in the code, and the other apps were not checked.

items.where: Sidebar > Study > Start studying
steps: Sign in and click Study in the sidebar.
On the Study page, type a subject in the field 'What are you studying?' (for example: eigenvalues).
Leave How set to 'Learn it' and click 'Start studying'.
Look at whether a new chat opens at /chat/<id> with the study tutoring started, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account (none special)
items.note: The sidebar container was not opened; 'Study' is the nav item label in app-nav-items.ts (the navStudy translation key was not found in any translation file). The same Study row also appears in the chat composer '+' menu (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerPlusMenu.tsx, label 'Study'), but the exact text of that '+' button was not found. Session creation itself was not checked.

items.where: Sidebar > Study > What are you studying?
steps: Sign in and click Study in the sidebar.
Click the field 'What are you studying?' and type a learning goal or topic (for example: photosynthesis).
Check that 'Start studying' stays disabled while the field is empty and becomes enabled once text is typed.
Compare the form with Expected: the user has stated the topic before the session starts.
items.needs: none
items.note: The field is a single text input for the topic; the Study page has no separate 'goal' field, so the goal is entered as the topic.

items.where: Sidebar > Study > What are you studying?
steps: Sign in and click Study in the sidebar.
Click the field 'What are you studying?' and type the subject (for example: German dative case).
Optionally open the 'Course material' drop-down (shown only when the account has projects) and choose 'From project: <name>' or 'None'.
Compare with Expected: the user has picked the subject to study and it appears in the session title after starting.
items.needs: none (a project is needed to see the 'Course material' drop-down)
items.note: Subject is entered as free text in 'What are you studying?'; there is no list of subjects. 'Course material' picks a project, not a subject, and only appears when projects exist.

items.where: Sidebar > Study > Where you are with it
steps: Sign in and click Study in the sidebar.
Open the drop-down 'Where you are with it' and choose 'Some background' (other choices: 'New to it', 'Know it well').
Type a topic, leave How as 'Learn it', and click 'Start studying'.
In the new chat, ask a basic question and compare the tutor's explanation depth with Expected: it should adapt to the chosen level.
items.needs: none
items.note: The level choice is sent to the server as part of the session, and its effect on the tutor is inside the server instruction (apps/web/features/study/lib/study-session.ts), so the adaptation is only visible in the chat answers, not on the Study page.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Persistent memory
steps: Sign in, open Settings, then click Personalization.
Find the row "Persistent memory" and note the switch next to it.
Turn the switch off, then start a new chat and say a fact you know is saved.
Check the reply does not use the saved fact, and turn the switch back on.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The entry point to Settings was not located; the command palette lists "Settings" (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/CommandPalette.tsx), and the Personalization page is mapped in apps/web/features/settings/components/WebSettingsModal.tsx.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Search past chats
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Find the row "Search past chats" and its switch.
Turn it off, then ask a question that refers to an older chat.
Check the reply does not quote excerpts from your other chats; turn it back on.
items.needs: a signed-in account with older chats

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Manage memories
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Click the "Manage memories" button under the memory counts line.
The page scrolls to the memory list headed by the "Memory facts" list.
Compare the list with the saved count shown as "saved memories" above it.
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories (the button is disabled when there are none)

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Manage memories > Search memory
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization, then click "Manage memories".
Click the box with the placeholder "Search memory".
Type a word from one saved memory.
Check only memories containing that word remain in the list.
items.needs: a signed-in account with several saved memories
items.note: The code shows the search box with this placeholder; whether it is hidden for short lists was not checked.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Manage memories
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization, then click "Manage memories".
Look at the group headings in the memory list.
Compare the headings with the topics in Expected: Preferences, About you, Decisions, Context, Summaries, Skills, Other.
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories of different kinds
items.note: The grouping is built in code; whether each group heading is drawn visibly was not confirmed.

items.where: Settings > Reflect > Work in progress
steps: Open Settings, then click Reflect.
Look for the section headed "Work in progress".
Compare the listed items with the projects or work you are pursuing in your chats.
items.needs: a signed-in account with chats about ongoing work
items.note: The section appears only when there are ongoing-work items, so it may be absent for a new account.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Manage memories > Add a new fact
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization, then click "Manage memories".
Click the box with the placeholder "Example: I prefer Python over JavaScript for data work."
Type a fact, then click the "Add" button.
Check the new fact appears in the memory list with "Added by you", then start a chat and check it is used.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Chat composer > type "Remember that" followed by the fact
steps: In a chat, type "Remember that" followed by a fact, such as a preference, and send.
Read the assistant reply for a confirmation that it was saved.
Open Settings > Personalization > Manage memories and look for the fact.
items.needs: a signed-in account with Persistent memory on
items.note: The phrase comes from the help text; a confirmation message in the reply was not found in the code, so the tester should compare with the reply shown.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Save memories from chats
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Confirm "Persistent memory" and "Save memories from chats" are on.
Have an ordinary chat that states a lasting fact about you, such as your job.
Open Manage memories and check the fact was added without you asking.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Manage memories > click a memory's text
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization, then click "Manage memories".
Click the text of a saved memory; it opens for editing.
Change the wording and save it.
Start a new chat and check the reply uses the corrected wording.
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories
items.note: The edit control is the memory text itself with the accessible name "Edit memory"; the saving button text in the editing view was not checked.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Manage memories > Delete memory fact (trash icon)
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization, then click "Manage memories".
Hover a memory and click its trash icon (accessible name "Delete memory fact").
In the dialog "Delete this memory?", click "Delete memory".
Check the memory is gone from the list.
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories
items.note: The trash icon has no visible text; the tester should find it by its position at the right end of each memory row.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Clear all memories
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Click "Clear all memories".
In the dialog "Delete all memory facts?", read the text, then click "Forget everything".
Check the saved count now shows no saved memories and the Manage memories list is empty.
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Manage memories > Pin memory (pin icon)
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization, then click "Manage memories".
Click the pin icon (accessible name "Pin memory") on a memory.
Check the icon changes to the unpin icon ("Unpin memory") and the memory is marked as pinned.
Compare with Expected: a pinned memory is kept and preferred.
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories
items.note: The pin icon has no visible text.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Manage memories > source line under each memory
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization, then click "Manage memories".
Read the small line under each memory.
Compare the lines with Expected: "Added by you", "Learned from a chat" (with a link to the chat), or "Imported".
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories from more than one source

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Manage memories > date text under each memory
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization, then click "Manage memories".
Read the small line under a memory that ends with "Updated" and a date.
Edit that memory, then check the date changes to today.
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories

items.where: Applied by the server when you state a newer fact in a chat
steps: In a chat, state a newer fact that contradicts a saved memory, such as a new employer.
Open Settings > Personalization and look for the older fact under "Replaced memories".
items.needs: a signed-in account with a saved memory to contradict
items.note: Effect visibility is inferred from the Replaced memories list; the code does not show a direct notice in the chat, so compare with the list.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Replaced memories > Use the replaced one instead
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Find the list labelled "Replaced memories" (it appears only when memories conflict).
Read the rule line: "Pinned wins, then ones you added, then the newest."
Click "Use the replaced one instead" on an entry and check it returns to the active memories.
items.needs: a signed-in account with two conflicting memories
items.note: The list appears only when a conflict exists, so a tester may need to create one first.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Import memory from other AI providers > Start import
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Click "Start import" on the row "Import memory from other AI providers".
In the dialog, upload a memory export file or pick items, then preview them.
Confirm the import and check the imported memories appear in Manage memories with "Imported".
items.needs: a file to upload, or a memory export from another assistant

labels.text: Import memory from other AI providers

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Export memories
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Click "Export memories" (it is disabled when there are no memories).
Open the file that downloads and read it.
Compare its contents with the list in Manage memories.
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories

items.where: Sidebar > project row menu > Project settings > Add a memory only this project uses
steps: In the sidebar, open the menu of a project and choose Project settings (the dialog title is "Project settings").
Find the memory list in the dialog and the box labelled "Add a memory only this project uses".
Add a memory there, then open a chat in a different project and check it is not used.
Check the global memory list in Settings > Personalization shows the project memory with "Only in" and the project name.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least two projects

labels.text: Add a memory only this project uses

items.note: The sidebar menu item text was not found; the dialog is said to open from the sidebar row context menu in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Where a memory applies; and the workspace page titled Sharing
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization, and read "Where a memory applies".
Open the workspace page titled "Sharing" (apps/web/app/workspace/sharing/page.tsx).
Check work and workspace memories are listed apart from personal memories and that a personal chat does not show workspace memories.
items.needs: a workspace (organization) account
items.note: The path to the workspace console from the sidebar was not confirmed.

items.where: Chat reply > Show sources (sources button) > Memory section
steps: Send a question that a saved memory should shape, then wait for the reply.
Click the "Show sources" button under the reply.
In the panel, look for the section headed "Memory" with a count and the memory excerpts used.
Compare with the reply: a reply that came only from saved memories shows the note "This answer came from your saved memories, not the web."
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories and a chat that uses them

labels.text: This answer came from your saved memories, not the web.

items.where: Chat composer > Temporary chat (header shows "Temporary chat")
steps: Turn on "Temporary chat" in the chat composer and send a message containing a new fact about you.
Check the header shows "Temporary chat".
Open Settings > Personalization > Manage memories and confirm the fact is not in the list.
Start a later normal chat and check it does not refer to the temporary chat.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The composer control text was not found; the header label is from the code. The 'Temporary chat' row in the composer is referenced in apps/web/features/desktop-host/hooks/use-temporary-chat.ts.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Never remember
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Find the section headed "Never remember".
Type a term in the box labelled "Term to never remember" and click "Add".
Ask the assistant to remember a fact with that term and check it is not saved; a credential should also be refused.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The automatic refusal of credentials is server behaviour; the tester can only check it by the saved list.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Clear all memories
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization, then click "Clear all memories".
Read the dialog text, which says "Your chats are not deleted."
Confirm with "Forget everything".
Check the memory count is zero and your chats are still listed in the sidebar.
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories and chats
items.note: Whether deleting chats also clears memory was not verified in the files named; only the reset path was found.

items.where: Saved memory has no control for model choice; its effect shows in chat. Check Settings > Personalization > Memory, then chat with two different models.
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization, and scroll to the Memory section. Note one saved fact, for example a preferred name or a work detail.
Start a new chat with the first model in the model picker and ask a question that needs that fact, such as "what do you know about my work?".
Start another new chat, switch to a different model in the model picker, and ask the same question.
Compare the two answers: both should use the same saved fact, and Memory should be unchanged between the two chats.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account with Memory turned on, and at least two models available to pick
items.note: The model picker's visible label was not found in the web code, so the tester must find it on the composer. The Settings entry point is only confirmed as the word 'Settings' in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:96, not as a web sidebar button.

items.where: No control for sync. Its effect is seen on a second signed-in client: Settings > Personalization > Memory.
steps: On client A (the web app), open Settings, then Personalization, and add a memory with a unique phrase such as "test fact 39-32".
Sign in to the same account on client B (desktop, mobile or the extension) and open its Memory list in Settings.
Check whether the phrase from step 1 appears on client B. Then ask a chat question on client B that depends on that fact.
Compare with Expected: the memory should appear and be used on every signed-in client.
items.needs: two clients (web plus desktop, mobile or the extension) signed in to the same account; a Free account or a paid account with Memory on
items.note: The store in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/stores/memoryStore.ts persists facts locally as well as syncing them to the server, so a memory saved on one client only shows on another after the sync completes; device-local memories do not sync. The code audit did not confirm which Memory list on client B holds a server-synced fact.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > About you > What should AGI call you?
steps: Sign in, open the account menu and choose Settings, then choose Personalization.
Scroll to About you and type a nickname in the field with the placeholder Nickname or first name.
Wait for the save status to show Saved, then start a new chat and ask a question.
Check that the reply uses that name, as in Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Opening Settings from the account menu relies on AccountMenuItems.tsx using the Settings label; the account menu trigger's own visible text was not confirmed. Onboarding also asks Preferred name (OnboardingWizard.tsx) but this item is the Settings path.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > About you > More about you
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Scroll to About you and type background in More about you, for example interests or your situation.
Wait for Saved, then start a new chat and ask a question that needs the background.
Check that the reply takes the background into account, as in Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Settings > Personalization > About you > What best describes your work?
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Scroll to About you and open the What best describes your work? menu.
Pick a role from the list, wait for Saved, then ask a question in a new chat.
Check that the reply is pitched at that role, as in Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The role choices come from WORK_DESCRIPTIONS in a constants file; the list's visible text was not read.

items.where: Composer > Style > Response Style
steps: In a chat, click the Style control in the composer.
Under Response Style, pick Concise, Explanatory, Learning or Formal (or Default).
Send a question and look at the reply shape.
Check that the reply follows the chosen style and only one style is active, as in Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The same choice is also in Settings > Personalization > Style and tone > Response style.

items.where: Composer > Style > Response Length (Brief, Default, Thorough)
steps: In a chat, click the Style control in the composer.
Under Response Length, pick Brief, then send a question.
Pick Thorough, send the same question, and compare the lengths.
Check that the reply length changes with the choice, as in Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: Settings > Personalization > Response length uses other labels (Default, Shorter, Longer), so the two controls are not the same list.

items.where: Composer > Style > Formal
steps: In a chat, click the Style control in the composer.
Pick Formal under Response Style.
Send a casual question and read the reply.
Check that the wording is formal, as in Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: Settings > Personalization > Style and tone > Response style also lists Formal.

items.where: Composer > Style > Response Style (Default, Concise, Explanatory, Learning, Formal)
steps: In a chat, click the Style control in the composer.
Pick one preset under Response Style, for example Concise.
Send a question and compare the reply with the Expected tone.
Switch to a different preset, send again, and check that the reply changes.
items.needs: none
items.note: The code has no separate tone control; the named presets are the only tone choice found.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Characteristics > Warmth
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Scroll to Characteristics and open Warmth.
Pick More, then ask a question in a new chat.
Check that the reply is warmer, and repeat with Less to compare, as in Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Characteristics > Enthusiasm
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Scroll to Characteristics and open Enthusiasm.
Pick More, then ask a question in a new chat.
Check that the reply is more enthusiastic, and repeat with Less to compare, as in Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Characteristics > Headers and lists
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Scroll to Characteristics and open Headers and lists.
Pick Less, ask a question in a new chat, then pick More and ask again.
Check that the first reply is prose and the second uses headers and bullets, as in Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Preferred formatting (Not set, Prose, Bullet lists, and others) is a second control for the same idea.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Characteristics > Emoji
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Scroll to Characteristics and open Emoji.
Pick Less, ask a question in a new chat, then pick More and ask again.
Check that emoji appear only on the More reply, as in Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Style and tone > Technical level
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Under Style and tone, open Technical level and pick Beginner.
Ask a technical question in a new chat.
Check that the reply is explained for a beginner, then pick Expert and compare, as in Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Style and tone > Response language
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Under Style and tone, open Response language and pick a language other than Match my message.
Send a message in English in a new chat.
Check that the reply is written in the chosen language, as in Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: This is separate from Display Language in General, whose label is in apps/web/features/settings/sections/GeneralSection.tsx.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Instructions for AGI
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Type standing instructions in the Instructions for AGI box and wait for Saved.
Start a new chat and ask a question that the instruction should change.
Turn off the switch labelled Apply instructions for AGI, ask again in a new chat, and compare, as in Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > project row menu > Project settings > Instructions
steps: In the sidebar, open a project's menu and choose Project settings.
Type text in the Instructions box and click Save.
Open a chat inside that project and ask a question.
Check that the reply follows the project instructions, as in Expected.
items.needs: a project
items.note: The sidebar menu item that opens Project settings was not confirmed by its visible text; the dialog title was used instead.

items.where: Composer > Style (in one chat)
steps: In a chat, click the Style control and pick a style such as Concise.
Send a question in this chat and check the reply is short.
Open a second chat and leave its style at Default.
Check that the second chat keeps its own style and the Settings default is unchanged, as in Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The per-chat scope was read from the code, not tested.

items.where: Composer > Style > Create Custom Style > Writing sample
steps: In a chat, click the Style control and choose Create Custom Style.
Type a Name, paste text into Writing sample, and click Save.
Select the new style and ask for a short piece of writing.
Check that the reply matches the voice of the sample, as in Expected.
items.needs: a sample of your own writing (paste text)

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Reset response style
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Change Response style and a few Characteristics.
Click Reset response style and read the toast.
Check that the controls return to Default and the toast says Response style is back to the defaults, as in Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Composer > Style > Explanatory
steps: In a chat, click the Style control and pick Explanatory under Response Style.
Ask how a simple process works.
Check that the reply gives reasoning and context, as in Expected.
items.needs: none

items.where: Composer > Style > Learning
steps: In a chat, click the Style control and pick Learning under Response Style.
Ask a question about a topic you want to learn.
Check that the reply goes step by step with check-ins, as in Expected.
items.needs: none

items.where: Composer > Style > Concise
steps: In a chat, click the Style control and pick Concise under Response Style.
Ask a question that normally gets a long answer.
Check that the reply is short and direct, as in Expected.
items.needs: none

items.where: Composer > Style > Create Custom Style (edit with the pencil, delete with the trash icon)
steps: In a chat, click the Style control and choose Create Custom Style.
Enter a Name and a Style instruction, then click Save. Use the Edit control on the style to change it and Save changes.
Select the style, ask a question, and check the reply follows it.
Use the Delete control, read the confirmation and choose Delete style, then check the style is gone, as in Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The Edit and Delete controls use aria labels Edit {name} and Delete {name}; the confirmation says the style cannot be recovered.

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > project row menu > Project settings > Personalization
steps: Open a project's Project settings from its sidebar menu.
Under Personalization, check or uncheck Use your profile and instructions for AGI.
Click Save, open a chat in that project, and ask a question.
