Check that the reply uses your personal instructions only when the box is checked, as in Expected.
items.needs: a project and a saved personal instruction

labels.text: Use your profile and instructions for AGI

items.note: The sidebar menu item that opens Project settings was not confirmed by its visible text.

items.where: The + button under the message box > Temporary chat. Or Settings > Privacy > Start new chats as temporary (sets the default for new chats).
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Click the + button under the message box and click Temporary chat.
Look for the Temporary chat banner in the top bar and the line Stays out of your history, search, memory and Library.
Compare with Expected: a temporary chat can be started from the chat surface.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The + menu button has no visible text found in the code, and the Settings default applies to new chats only.

items.where: Start a chat with the + button > Temporary chat. The label Temporary chat sits in the top bar of the chat, and hovering it shows the retention note.
steps: Start a temporary chat as in S41.01.
Send a message and wait for the reply.
Check that the label Temporary chat stays in the top bar while the chat is open, with the Personalized or Unpersonalized switch beside it.
Compare with Expected: the banner stays visible for as long as the chat is open.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The banner is hidden on small screens for the explanation text only (CSS hidden sm:inline), the label stays.

items.where: Chat top bar: hover the Temporary chat label. Also Settings > Privacy > How we protect your data.
steps: Start a temporary chat and hover the Temporary chat label in the top bar.
Read the text shown: Won't be saved to your history and skips memory for this turn.
Open Settings > Privacy and expand How we protect your data.
Send a temporary chat, then search the history for a word from it and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account; a second search after the chat is finished
items.note: The code says temporary chats are left out of search, but the earlier check reported the completed chat appearing in global search, so the expected behaviour may not match.

items.needs: a signed-in account with Memory on

labels.text: Temporary chats never read or save memory.

items.note: The code disables the + menu Memory row in a temporary chat (memoryDisabled when isIncognito) and says memory is never read, so no choice is offered; I searched ChatComposerNew.tsx for memory handling and found no per-chat read choice.

items.where: No control; the effect is that the memory of a temporary turn is skipped, shown only by the note on the temporary chat.
steps: Start a temporary chat and hover the Temporary chat label.
Read the text Won't be saved to your history and skips memory for this turn.
Compare with Expected: nothing from the temporary chat should appear in memory.
items.needs: a signed-in account with Memory on

labels.text: Won't be saved to your history and skips memory for this turn.

items.note: A tester cannot see the memory store directly from the UI in the code I read, so this can only be compared through the note.

items.where: Chat top bar > Personalized / Unpersonalized switch, shown only in a temporary chat.
steps: Start a temporary chat.
Look at the switch in the top bar, which reads Personalized by default.
Click it and read the title hint: Personalized uses your profile, instructions and response style.
Send a message and compare the reply with Expected: custom instructions apply only when Personalized is on.
items.needs: a signed-in account with custom instructions set
items.note: none

items.where: The + button under the message box > Plugins, while a temporary chat is open.
steps: Start a temporary chat.
Click the + button under the message box and open Plugins.
Read the note under the Temporary chat row: Won't be saved to your history or show up in search, and skips memory.
Compare with Expected: the note should say how a connector behaves in a temporary chat, such as asking before each call.
items.needs: a signed-in account; a connector connected

labels.text: Won't be saved to your history or show up in search, and skips memory.

items.note: The connector wording is in the retention note under the Temporary chat row, not next to Plugins itself.

items.where: The + button under the message box > the file attach row while a temporary chat is open. Also Settings > Privacy > How we protect your data.
steps: Start a temporary chat and click the + button.
Hover or read the attach row note: Kept out of your Library and deleted with this temporary chat.
Open Settings > Privacy > How we protect your data and read: A temporary chat and its attachments are removed after 30 days.
Compare with Expected: the note should match what happens to an attached file.
items.needs: a file to upload; a signed-in account

labels.text: Kept out of your Library and deleted with this temporary chat.

items.note: The attach row's exact visible label was not located; the note is shown on that row.

items.needs: a signed-in account and an image or video generated in a temporary chat
items.note: I searched apps/web/lib/server/media-assets.ts and apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts; they set a temporary_chat flag but I found no visible keep or save control for generated output.

items.where: The + button under the message box > Temporary chat (switch it off) > Save chat in the dialog.
steps: Open a temporary chat with a few messages.
Click the + button and click Temporary chat to turn it off.
In the dialog Save this chat?, click Save chat.
Open the chat from the sidebar history and check the messages are there, and compare with Expected: everything is kept.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The dialog appears only when the chat has messages to keep; an empty chat changes without a dialog.

items.where: The + button under the message box > Temporary chat (switch it off), then read the dialog Save this chat?.
steps: Open a temporary chat with messages.
Click the + button and click Temporary chat to turn it off.
Read the dialog text: the number of messages, and any files, will be kept in your history.
Click Save chat, or close the dialog to cancel, and compare with Expected: the user sees what is kept before confirming.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: This dialog and the one for S41.10 are the same dialog; it states the count of messages and says the chat then follows memory and data settings.

items.where: Settings > Privacy (Start new chats as temporary, How we protect your data, How we use your data, and the Only use models that do not train on your chats switch).
steps: Open Settings > Privacy.
Find the switch Start new chats as temporary and read its line: Not saved to history or search, and deleted after 30 days.
Expand How we protect your data and How we use your data.
Compare with Expected: history, model training and retention each have a separate control or statement.
items.needs: a signed-in account

labels.text: Only use models that do not train on your chats

items.note: The earlier check marked the privacy controls as UI-only, and the retention text is inside expandable sections.

items.where: Settings > Privacy: the short line under each switch, such as Start new chats as temporary, and the expandable sections.
steps: Open Settings > Privacy.
Read the grey line under Start new chats as temporary: Not saved to history or search, and deleted after 30 days. Project chats are saved.
Read the grey line under Privacy requests and expand How we protect your data.
Compare with Expected: each setting explains what it does in place.
items.needs: a signed-in account

labels.text: Not saved to history or search, and deleted after 30 days. Project chats are saved.

items.note: The explanation for each setting is in the Privacy page, not on the chat surface.

items.where: Settings > Privacy > Where each feature processes your data.
steps: Open Settings > Privacy.
Expand Where each feature processes your data.
Read the rows, for example Chat: Cloud, then the AI provider that serves the model you chose.
Compare with Expected: each feature names where its data is processed.
items.needs: a signed-in account

labels.text: Where each feature processes your data
Cloud, then the AI provider that serves the model you chose.

items.note: none

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > (arrow button beside it) > Start from a template > Daily briefing
steps: Sign in and click Scheduled in the sidebar.
Click the arrow button beside New task, then click Start from a template.
Click the card named Daily briefing (it shows Weekdays at 8:00 AM).
Submit the Create Schedule dialog (the submit button's exact text was not checked).
Look for the new schedule card named Daily briefing with a Next: row of upcoming times, and compare with Expected (recurring, generated and delivered).
items.needs: A paid account (Scheduled tasks are available on Basic and higher plans). A Free account may see the page locked.
items.note: Delivery is shown on the Scheduled page and by the Scheduled task finished notification (see S42.17); the in-app delivery path was not traced end to end.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch > Local Time and Time Zone fields
steps: Click Scheduled in the sidebar, then New task.
Click Create from scratch (or start from a template).
Set Recurrence, then change Local Time.
Change Time Zone (the field offers a list of zones).
Save, then look at the card's Next: row, whose tooltip reads Times are shown in <zone>, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: A paid account (Basic or higher).
items.note: The ScheduleForm line cited in Code moved; the Local Time and Time Zone fields are at lines 387 and 510 today.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > the briefing's card > its on/off switch (labelled Pause or Resume by name)
steps: Click Scheduled in the sidebar.
Find the Daily briefing card.
Click its switch to pause it; look for the Paused text on the card and the message Schedule paused.
Click the switch again; look for Schedule resumed and the card's Paused text going away, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: A paid account with at least one schedule.
items.note: The switch has no visible text; it is labelled only by its aria-label Pause <name> or Resume <name>.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Time and focus > Quiet hours
steps: Open the account menu at the bottom of the sidebar and click Settings.
Click Time and focus.
Turn on Quiet hours and set a start and an end time that differ.
Keep the page open during those hours (or set a window that includes now) and look for the banner Quiet hours are active.
Holding of push notifications happens on the server; check on a phone with push that a non-exempt notification is held, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: A way to see push notifications (a phone with AGI installed) for the hold to be checked. Web alone only shows the Quiet hours are active banner.
items.note: Approvals and failures are exempt from the hold, as the page text says. The push hold lives in apps/web/lib/services/push-notification-service.ts (heldByQuietHours); its cited line moved.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Notifications > Scheduled task finished
steps: Open the account menu and click Settings, then Notifications.
Find the row Scheduled task finished with its channel switches (Email, Mobile push).
Turn the channels on or off and note the change.
Run a scheduled task and wait for it to finish, then check the email or phone push for the finished or failed message.
Compare what arrives with Expected.
items.needs: An email inbox and/or a phone with AGI push, plus a scheduled task that can run.
items.note: Earlier check only saw the channels; delivery was not tested. The web settings row offers Email and Mobile push, not a browser channel, for this event.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Reflect
steps: Open the account menu, click Settings, then Reflect.
Read the page. If it says Turn on Memory and Save memories from chats to create a recap, turn those two settings on under Personalization and reload.
Choose a range in the Reflect range dropdown (Past 30 days by default).
Look for the usage reflection (topics and times) and compare with Expected.
items.needs: Memory and Save memories from chats turned on, and a paid or signed-in account with past chats. Without them the page is blocked.

labels.text: Turn on Memory and Save memories from chats to create a recap.

items.note: The earlier check named Generate from past chats, but the code's visible text says Save memories from chats. Memory is the gate, as the earlier check found.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Reflect > Reflect range > Past year
steps: Open the account menu, click Settings, then Reflect.
Open the Reflect range dropdown and choose Past year.
Wait for the recap to reload.
Look at the recap for the last 365 days and compare with Expected (a recap of the past year).
items.needs: Memory and Save memories from chats turned on, with a year of chats.
items.note: No screen says Annual recap. The recap is the Past year range of the Reflect page, not a calendar-year report. Gated the same way as S42.19.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Time and focus > Break reminder
steps: Open the account menu, click Settings, then Time and focus.
Set Break reminder to the shortest value offered.
Go back to a chat and keep using AGI in the same tab until the chosen time has passed.
Look for the box Time for a break? and compare with Expected.
items.needs: Patience: the reminder needs the chosen amount of visible time in AGI that day.
items.note: The reminder is shown once a day, per the page text (one gentle nudge each day). The minimum option length was not checked.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Time and focus
steps: Open the account menu and click Settings.
Click Time and focus in the settings list.
Look for the sections Break reminder and Quiet hours on the page.
Change one of them, look for the save status line, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: A signed-in account.
items.note: The nav label Time and focus comes from packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/settings.json (key time-focus).

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > the briefing's card > History icon (title Run History)
steps: Click Scheduled in the sidebar.
On the Daily briefing card, click the History icon (title Run History).
Look at the list of past runs with their status (for example completed, failed, timeout).
Open a run to see its result, and compare with Expected (past briefings kept as a browsable history).
items.needs: A schedule that has run at least once.
items.note: No visible text says saved editions. Recent results (RecentScheduleResults.tsx) is also a history list, but its visible heading was not found in the code.

items.where: Chat > composer plus menu > Add photos & files > choose one image > type a question > send
steps: Open a new chat in the web app.
Open the plus menu in the message box and click "Add photos & files".
Choose one image file.
Type a question about the image, such as "What is in this picture?", and send.
Look for an answer that describes the image. Expected: the model answers from the image, with no upload refusal message.
items.needs: an image file
items.note: The attach path exists, but the upload scanner webhook (UPLOAD_SCAN_WEBHOOK_URL) is only confirmed in code; a live check is needed.

items.where: Chat > composer plus menu > Add photos & files > choose two or more images > type a comparison question > send
steps: Open a new chat in the web app.
Open the plus menu and click "Add photos & files".
Choose two or more image files at once.
Type "Compare these two images" and send.
Look for an answer that names details from both images. Expected: the model received and compared all attached images.
items.needs: two image files
items.note: Whether the picker accepts more than one file in one pick is not checked in the files read.

items.where: Chat > composer plus menu > Attach clipboard (after copying a screenshot), or Chat > Add photos & files > choose a screenshot file
steps: Take a screenshot with the macOS screenshot keys and leave it on the clipboard.
Open a new chat and open the plus menu.
Click "Attach clipboard" (or use "Add photos & files" and pick the screenshot file).
Type "What does this screenshot show?" and send.
Look for an answer that explains what is on the screen. Expected: the model describes the screenshot.
items.needs: a screenshot
items.note: Whether Attach clipboard accepts an image on the clipboard was not confirmed; pasting into the message box was not traced.

items.where: Chat > composer plus menu > Add photos & files > choose a photo or scanned PDF > type "Read this document and explain it" > send
steps: Open a new chat and open the plus menu.
Click "Add photos & files" and choose a photo or a scanned PDF of a document.
Type "Read this document and explain it." and send.
Look for an answer that reads text from the document and explains it. Expected: the model reads the scanned document.
items.needs: a photo or scanned PDF of a document
items.note: Whether a scanned PDF is accepted as an image was not confirmed in the files read.

items.where: Chat > composer plus menu > Add photos & files > choose a chart image > type a question about trends > send
steps: Open a new chat and open the plus menu.
Click "Add photos & files" and choose a chart image.
Type "What trend does this chart show?" and send.
Look for an answer that names the data series and the trend. Expected: the model interprets the chart.
items.needs: a chart image

items.where: Chat > composer plus menu > Add photos & files > choose a diagram image > type "Explain the structure of this diagram" > send
steps: Open a new chat and open the plus menu.
Click "Add photos & files" and choose a diagram image.
Type "Explain the structure of this diagram." and send.
Look for an answer that names the parts and how they connect. Expected: the model explains the diagram structure.
items.needs: a diagram image

items.where: Chat > composer plus menu > Add photos & files > choose a photo of handwritten notes > type "Transcribe these notes" > send
steps: Open a new chat and open the plus menu.
Click "Add photos & files" and choose a photo of handwritten notes.
Type "Transcribe these notes." and send.
Look for a transcription that matches the handwriting. Expected: the model transcribes or answers about the notes.
items.needs: a photo of handwritten notes

items.where: Chat > composer plus menu > Add photos & files > choose an image with text > type "Extract the text in this image" > send, then copy the reply
steps: Open a new chat and open the plus menu.
Click "Add photos & files" and choose an image that contains text.
Type "Extract the text in this image." and send.
Select the text in the reply and copy it, then paste it somewhere.
Look for the copied text to match the text in the image. Expected: the text can be copied and reused.
items.needs: an image with text
items.note: There is no separate OCR control; extraction is done by asking in the chat.

items.where: Chat > composer plus menu > Add photos & files > choose an image with several items > type "How many are there?" > send
steps: Open a new chat and open the plus menu.
Click "Add photos & files" and choose an image with a countable number of items.
Type "How many of these are in the image?" and send.
Count the items yourself and compare with the answer. Expected: the model gives a count.
items.needs: an image with countable objects

items.where: Chat > composer plus menu > Add photos & files > choose two scene images > type "Describe the differences" > send
steps: Open a new chat and open the plus menu.
Click "Add photos & files" and choose two scene images at once.
Type "Describe the differences between these two scenes." and send.
Look for an answer that names differences in both images. Expected: the model describes the differences.
items.needs: two scene images
items.note: Multi-file selection in one pick was not confirmed in the files read.

items.where: Chat > composer plus menu > Add photos & files > choose a photo or screenshot of the problem > type "What is wrong and what should I try?" > send
steps: Open a new chat and open the plus menu.
Click "Add photos & files" and choose a photo or screenshot of a device, error or setup.
Type "What is wrong here and what should I try?" and send.
Look for numbered troubleshooting steps that refer to the picture. Expected: the model gives troubleshooting steps.
items.needs: a photo or screenshot of a problem

items.where: Library > open an image item > Remix (then the composer opens with the image attached); or Chat > plus menu > Add from library > pick the image > Edit or Variation
steps: Click "Library" in the sidebar.
Open an image item in the library list.
Click "Remix" in its menu.
The new chat opens with the image attached. Check the image chip and the "Edit" or "Variation" option.
Type a change, such as "Make the sky red", and send. Expected: the image is used as the reference input for the new generation.
items.needs: a previously saved image in the library
items.note: Remix is a host action passed from apps/web/features/library/components/LibraryView.tsx; the Edit and Variation chips are in apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx and appear only in image mode.

items.where: Chat > message box: the + button > Create image; then type a prompt and press the send button
steps: Open a chat and click the + button beside the message box, then click Create image.
Type a prompt into the message box.
Press the send button.
Look for the Generating image card, then check that an image replaces it in the conversation, as Expected says.
items.needs: an account with image generation enabled
items.note: The aria-label of the + button was not found in the code, so it is described by position only.

items.where: Chat > message box: Create image mode on, then the button labelled Select image model (shows the model name) > pick a model
steps: Click the + button beside the message box, then click Create image.
Click the button with the current model name (aria-label Select image model).
Pick a different model from the list.
Send a prompt and compare the caption Generated with <model> on the result with Expected.
items.needs: an account with image generation enabled
items.note: The list only offers models the account's deployment marks as enabled; the picker is not shown until the media models have loaded.

items.where: Chat > message box (Create image on) > Style > Image style menu > pick a preset such as Photorealistic
steps: Turn on Create image from the + button.
Click the button labelled Style (aria-label Add a style to the prompt).
Click a preset such as Photorealistic in the Image style menu.
Check the message box: the preset words were added to the prompt, then send and compare the look with Expected.
items.needs: an account with image generation enabled
items.note: A preset does not set a separate style option; it appends its phrase to the prompt text.

items.where: Chat > message box (Create image on) > + button > Add photos & files
steps: Turn on Create image from the + button.
Click + and choose Add photos & files, then attach images.
Check that the first attached image is treated as the one to edit and the others as references (the code shows the notice Attach up to ... images: the first is edited and the others guide it.).
Send and compare the result with Expected.
items.needs: a file to upload (up to several images)
items.note: No separate visible reference slots were found; reference images are the extra attachments after the first, per the code at ChatComposerNew.tsx around line 3777.

items.where: Chat > message box (Create image on) > button labelled Auto (aria-label Select aspect ratio) > pick a ratio
steps: Turn on Create image from the + button.
Click the button with the aspect ratio text (aria-label Select aspect ratio).
Pick a ratio from the list.
Send and check the picked ratio on the generated image.
items.needs: an account with image generation enabled
items.note: The ratio list comes from the selected model's options, so some ratios may be missing for some models.

items.where: Chat > message box (Create image on) > Transparent button
steps: Turn on Create image and choose a model that supports editing.
Click the button labelled Transparent (tooltip: Return the image on a transparent background).
Check that the button shows as on, then send a prompt.
Compare the background of the result with Expected.
items.needs: an account with image generation enabled and a model that supports editing

labels.text: Return the image on a transparent background

items.note: The button only appears when the chosen image model supports editing.

items.where: Chat > message box: Stop generation (the send button turns into this while an image is generating)
steps: Start an image from Create image with a prompt and send it.
While the Generating image card shows, click the stop button (tooltip Stop generation).
Look for the card Image generation stopped before a result was received.
Compare with Expected: the job is cancelled and not billed further (billing cannot be seen on screen).
items.needs: an account with image generation enabled and time to press stop before the image finishes

labels.text: Image generation stopped before a result was received.

items.note: The generating card itself has no stop button; the stop path is the composer button, which calls the image cancel logic in WebChatPage.tsx. The code path for a media placeholder shows Stop generating in MediaGenerationPlaceholder.tsx, and it was not confirmed whether images use it.

items.where: Chat > the image card after a stop or failure > Try again
steps: Stop an image generation as in S44.18, or use one that failed.
Click the Try again button on the card.
Check that a new Generating image card appears with the same prompt.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: an account with image generation enabled and a stopped or failed image

labels.text: Image generation stopped before a result was received.

items.note: When a rate limit applies the button text becomes Try again shortly or Try again in Ns, and the button is not clickable until it is over.

items.where: Chat > generated image > Revise this image (pencil button) > Variation
steps: Open a generated image in chat and click Revise this image.
Click the Variation button in the panel.
Look for a new image of the same prompt in the same card, with the earlier versions still reachable through the Previous version and Next version buttons.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: an account with image generation enabled and a model that supports editing
items.note: Variation is disabled unless the model supports editing, and the tooltip says why.

items.where: Sidebar: Library > Library page (grid view is the default); filter Images
steps: Click Library in the sidebar.
Look at the grid of saved items and click the Images filter if shown.
Use the Grid view button to confirm the grid mode.
Compare the saved images with Expected.
items.needs: saved images in the Library

items.where: Library > click an image to open its viewer (dialog named <name> viewer)
steps: Open Library from the sidebar.
Click an image in the grid.
Check the full-screen viewer opens, and use Zoom in and Zoom out.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: saved images in the Library
items.note: The exact click that opens the viewer was not confirmed in the code; the dialog and its zoom buttons were found at LibraryView.tsx around lines 1202 to 1243.

items.where: Chat > generated image card: the caption Generated with <model> · <ratio>
steps: Look at the caption under a generated image in chat.
Check that it shows the model name and the ratio when not Auto.
Compare with Expected (prompt, ratio, size, quality).
items.needs: a generated image in chat
items.note: The card shows the model and ratio; no visible size or quality text was found in the card, and the full prompt display was not confirmed (the card title is the prompt cut to 40 characters).

items.where: Library > item menu > Remix (the prompt is loaded into the message box)
steps: Open Library and open the menu of a generated image.
Click Remix.
Check the message box now holds the image's prompt and the image is attached.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a saved generated image in the Library
items.note: The name of the item menu trigger was not confirmed in the code.

items.where: Library > item menu > Remix (the same action also sets the model and ratio)
steps: Open Library and open the menu of a generated image.
Click Remix.
Check the model and the ratio shown in the composer match the original image.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a saved generated image in the Library
items.note: No separate Reuse settings control was found; it is the same Remix action.

items.where: Chat > generated image > More actions > Save to Library
steps: Click More actions on a generated image card.
Click Save to Library.
Look for the toast Saved to your Library. It stays after this chat is gone.
Open Library from the sidebar and check the image is there.
items.needs: an account with image generation enabled

items.where: Library > item menu > Add to project > dialog Add to project
steps: Open Library and open the menu of a generated image.
Click Add to project.
Choose a project in the dialog titled Add to project.
Open that project and check the image is listed.
items.needs: a Project and a generated image in the Library
items.note: The menu item appears only when the file type is accepted for projects, and the item menu trigger name was not confirmed.

items.where: Chat > generated image > More actions > Download
steps: Click More actions on a generated image card.
Click Download.
Open the file that downloads and check its size and sharpness.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: an account with image generation enabled
items.note: The Download control in the share sheet (aria-label Download image) also exists; full quality was not verified in code.

items.where: Chat > generated image > Copy (tooltip and label Copy image)
steps: Click Copy on a generated image.
Look for the Copied text on the button.
Paste into another app and check that the image itself is pasted, as Expected says.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: an account with image generation enabled
items.note: The image-copy function body was not read; the link-copy in the share sheet is a separate control labelled Copy link.

items.where: Chat > generated image > Revise this image (pencil button) > describe the change and send
steps: Click Revise this image on a generated image.
Type the change in the box and press the send control.
For a masked edit, click Select area, then Mask image, and paint the area.
Compare the result with the source image and Expected.
items.needs: an account with image generation enabled and a model that supports editing
items.note: Without editing support the panel only regenerates from the text; the code path for editing the source pixels was not run.

items.where: Chat > assistant message > message menu > Report this response
steps: Open the menu of a generated image's assistant message.
Click Report this response.
Look for the text Reporting… then Reported, and the toast Reported. Thank you: our trust and safety team will review it.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: an account with image generation enabled

labels.text: Reported. Thank you: our trust and safety team will review it.

items.note: The report item sits in the assistant message menu; that the image card messages show it was not confirmed, and the menu trigger name was not found.

items.where: Machine-readable provenance is sent with the file response (apps/web/app/api/files/[id]/route.ts), not a visible control
items.needs: none
items.note: No visible text saying AI-generated was found in ImageGenerationCard.tsx; the only visible attribution is the Generated with caption. Provenance is in the file route's response headers (route.ts:250).

items.where: Composer (message box) > + button > Add photos & files, then pick a picture. Turn on image mode with + > Create image first.
steps: Click + at the left of the message box and turn on Create image (image mode).
Click + again and click Add photos & files, then choose a picture from your Mac.
Check that the picture appears as an attachment above the message box.
Type a change in the message box and press send.
Look that the result is an edit of your picture (the uploaded picture is the first attachment, and the composer shows the Edit option in the Attached image action menu).
items.needs: an image file on the Mac and an account that can use image generation
items.note: The + button's own label was not confirmed; the tester should look for the plus icon at the left of the message box.

items.where: A generated image in chat > hover it and click New version. From the Library: Library > Actions for <image name> > Remix.
steps: Open a chat with a generated image, or open Library from the sidebar.
In chat, move the pointer over the image and click New version.
In Library, click the Actions for the image's file name button and click Remix.
Check that the Revise this image panel opens with the image and its original prompt (or that the composer is in image mode with the image attached).
items.needs: an image generated earlier, in this chat or an older one
items.note: The Library entry in the sidebar was not confirmed; the Library page header text was found.

items.where: Generated image > New version > type in the box Describe a change to this image... > click Apply this change to the image.
steps: Hover a generated image in chat and click New version.
Click in the box that says Describe a change to this image...
Type a change such as make the sky red.
Click the send button labelled Apply this change to the image (or press Enter).
Look that the image above is edited to match the change, and that a new version is added.
items.needs: a generated image in a chat

labels.text: Describe a change to this image...
Apply this change to the image

items.where: Generated image > New version > Select area, then paint over the part of the image to change.
steps: Hover a generated image and click New version.
Click Select area in the Revise this image panel.
Drag the mouse over the part of the image to change.
Click Apply this change to the image after typing a change, or look at the painted area before applying.
Look that only the painted area is changed (the composer hint says nearby content may change too).
items.needs: a generated image in a chat and a model that supports editing
items.note: The tester should expect the edit to be only as precise as the model allows; the code's own hint says nearby content may change too.

items.where: Revise this image panel > Select area > paint something > Clear selection.
steps: Open New version on a generated image and click Select area.
Paint over an area of the image with the mouse.
Look for the Clear selection button that appears next to Cancel selection.
Click Clear selection.
Look that the painted area disappears in one click and the Clear selection button goes away.
items.needs: a generated image in a chat and a model that supports editing
items.note: The Clear selection button only appears after something is painted; a mask file attached with Add mask is removed with the Remove mask button instead.

items.where: Composer > Create image (image mode) > attach a picture > click Transparent > type a prompt > send.
steps: Click + and turn on Create image.
Attach a picture with + > Add photos & files.
Click the Transparent button in the row under the message box so it is highlighted.
Type a prompt such as remove the background and send.
Look that the result shows the subject on a transparent background (checker pattern or transparent in Preview).
items.needs: an image file on the Mac and an account that can use image generation
items.note: The Transparent button shows only when the selected image model supports editing, and its hover text is Return the image on a transparent background.

items.where: Generated image > New version > Aspect ratio > choose a wider ratio.
steps: Hover a generated image and click New version.
Click the Aspect ratio button at the top of the Revise this image panel.
Choose a wider option such as 16:9.
Wait for the new version to generate.
Look that the picture is larger and the new side areas match the original scene.
items.needs: a generated image in a chat and a model that supports editing
items.note: Outpainting is reached only through the Aspect ratio menu; the composer's Attached image action menu does not offer it, as its code comment says.

items.where: Generated image > New version > Aspect ratio > choose a different ratio.
steps: Hover a generated image and click New version.
Click the Aspect ratio button (its hover text is Generate this image with a different aspect ratio).
Choose a different ratio such as 1:1 or 9:16.
Wait for the new version.
Look that the same scene is reframed to the new shape rather than a new unrelated picture.
items.needs: a generated image in a chat and a model that supports editing

labels.text: Generate this image with a different aspect ratio

items.note: If the chosen ratio equals the current one, nothing is generated.

items.where: Composer > + > Create image (image mode) > + > Add photos & files for a second picture (the first picture is edited, the others guide it).
steps: Turn on Create image from the + menu.
Attach the source picture with + > Add photos & files.
Attach a second picture the same way.
Type a prompt that asks for the subject or layout of the second picture, and send.
Look that the result uses the subject, layout or style of the reference picture.
items.needs: two image files on the Mac and an account that can use image generation
items.note: The composer has no label that says reference image for pictures; the limit notice says the first is edited and the others guide it, and the reference route is shown only through the attachment order.

items.where: Generated image > New version > the Image versions arrows (Previous version / Next version) under the image.
steps: Hover a generated image and click New version, then close the panel.
Look for the Image versions group under the image with the counter, for example 1 / 2.
Click Previous version to see the original.
Check that the original image still exists next to the new version.
items.needs: a generated image that has been edited at least once

items.where: Composer > Create image > Transparent on, attach a transparent PNG, send; then the Download button on the result.
steps: Turn on Create image and attach a transparent PNG with + > Add photos & files.
Click Transparent so it is highlighted, type a prompt and send.
Click the Download button on the result image card.
Open the downloaded file in Preview and look for a transparent background (checker pattern).
items.needs: a transparent PNG file on the Mac and an account that can use image generation
items.note: Whether alpha survives editing and storage is not proven by the code audit; the steps only make it visible.

items.where: Composer > "Add attachments and tools" button (icon only, the plus) > Create video, then type in the box "Describe the video you want" and press send
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Click the icon button labelled "Add attachments and tools" beside the message box.
Click "Create video" in the menu. The composer switches to video mode.
Type a prompt into the box that says "Describe the video you want" and press the send button.
Wait for the chat reply. Look for a clip with the text "Your video is ready." to compare with Expected.
items.needs: a plan that includes video (the code offers "Create video" only when video generation is available to the account; which plan is not confirmed)
items.note: The plus button has no visible text, only an icon, so the tester must find it by its tooltip or label. Whether the generated clip actually appears was not checked here.

items.where: Composer in video mode > the button showing the video model name (opens the list of video models)
steps: Turn on video mode as in S46.01 (Add attachments and tools > Create video).
Look at the pill beside the composer. It shows the current video model name, or "Checking video models…" or "No video model available".
Click that pill to open the model list.
Click a different model name.
Check that the pill now shows the new name and that the next video uses it.
items.needs: a plan that includes video with more than one video model in the catalog
items.note: The pill has no visible prefix; its accessible name is "Select video model", which is not shown on screen. Confirming that the chosen model is the one that generates the clip was not checked.

items.where: Composer in video mode > the length pill that shows a number of seconds (for example "8s") > pick a "seconds" entry
steps: Turn on video mode as in S46.01.
Click the pill that shows a length such as "8s".
Pick another length from the list, shown as for example "5 seconds".
Check that the pill now shows the chosen length.
Send the prompt and compare the clip length with Expected.
items.needs: a plan that includes video; a model that offers more than one length
items.note: The pill is hidden when the chosen model offers only one length, and also for promotional models. The pill's accessible name is "Select video length", which is not visible.

items.where: Composer in video mode > the aspect-ratio pill (for example "16:9") > pick an option
steps: Turn on video mode as in S46.01.
Click the pill that shows a ratio such as "16:9".
Pick another ratio from the list.
Check that the pill shows the new ratio.
Send the prompt and compare the clip's shape with Expected.
items.needs: a plan that includes video; a model that offers more than one aspect ratio
items.note: The pill is hidden when the model offers only one aspect ratio. Its accessible name is "Select video aspect ratio", which is not visible.

items.where: Composer in video mode > the quality pill (shows the quality label for the resolution) > pick an option
steps: Turn on video mode as in S46.01.
Click the pill that shows a quality label.
Pick another quality from the list.
Check that the pill shows the new quality.
Send the prompt and compare the clip's resolution with Expected.
items.needs: a plan that includes video; a model that offers more than one quality
items.note: The UI calls the resolution "quality"; the visible label text comes from VIDEO_QUALITY_LABELS, which was not opened. The pill is hidden when there is only one quality option.

items.where: Chat > the video message after sending, in the box "Your video is still being generated"
steps: Send a video prompt as in S46.01.
Look at the chat message while it generates.
Look for the box "Your video is still being generated" and the progress text.
Look for a percentage and an elapsed time on the placeholder.
Compare with Expected: progress should change while the video is made.
items.needs: a plan that includes video; a clip that is still generating

labels.text: Your video is still being generated

items.note: The percentage appears only when the provider reports progress. The placeholder shows a percentage and a time, as in MediaGenerationPlaceholder.tsx; whether the percentage moves was not checked.

items.where: Composer in video mode > the small text "About" followed by a credit amount, next to the length, ratio and quality pills
steps: Turn on video mode as in S46.01.
Choose a length, ratio and quality.
Look at the small text beside the pills, for example "About 12 credits".
Hover over it to read the full sentence, which says whether the cost settles when delivered.
Compare with Expected: the estimate should change when the options change.
items.needs: a plan that includes video; a signed-in account with a credit balance
items.note: The estimate is shown before generating. The file showed no sign of an after-generation actual cost, so that half of Expected was not confirmed. The estimate's wording is a template, so the visible words are "About" plus an amount.

items.where: Chat > the video placeholder while it generates > "Stop generating"
steps: Send a video prompt as in S46.01.
While the placeholder shows its percentage, look for the button "Stop generating".
Click "Stop generating".
Watch the button change to "Stopping…" and then a note.
Compare with Expected: the job should stop and the clip should not be delivered.
items.needs: a plan that includes video; a clip that is still generating when the tester clicks
items.note: The button shows only when the placeholder has a task ID. The Stopping and note wording was seen in the code, but whether the job truly stops was not checked.

items.where: Chat > the failed video message > "Try video again"
steps: Find a video message that failed, with the text "Video generation ended".
Read the line below it. It says "Trying again starts a new generation." if a retry is allowed.
Click "Try video again".
Look for a new placeholder with "Your video is still being generated".
Compare with Expected: the new job should use the same length, ratio and quality as the failed one.
items.needs: a video job that has failed and is allowed to be retried (hard to produce on demand)
items.note: The button appears only when the job is marked retryable. Older failed attempts show only the resend text. The retry path reuses the saved aspect, resolution and duration, as the code in WebChatPage.tsx shows.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Videos tab
steps: Click "Library" in the left navigation.
Click the "Videos" tab.
Look at the list of finished clips.
Click one clip to open it.
Compare with Expected: all finished clips should be together in one place.
items.needs: at least one finished video in the account
items.note: The code shows a Videos tab, but the view layout (gallery or list) was not confirmed from the code.

items.where: Chat > the finished video message, under "Your video is ready." (native player controls); or Library > Videos > open a clip
steps: Open a chat where a clip shows "Your video is ready."
Click the play control on the clip.
Click again to pause.
Drag the timeline to a new point and check the clip jumps there.
Repeat in Library > Videos to compare with Expected.
items.needs: a finished clip
items.note: Controls are the browser's native video controls, so their look depends on the browser.

items.where: Chat > the finished video message > hover over the clip and click "Download video" (icon at the top right of the clip)
steps: Open a chat where a clip shows "Your video is ready.".
Move the mouse over the clip, or press Tab until the icon is focused.
Click the icon labelled "Download video" at the top right.
Check the file saved to the Downloads folder as a video file.
Compare with Expected: the saved file should be the finished clip.
items.needs: a finished clip; a Mac with a browser that saves downloads
items.note: The icon has no visible text, only an accessible name. If the clip fails to load, a text link "Download video" appears instead.

items.where: Open an existing chat from the sidebar > empty message box > round button 'Start voice mode' (waveform icon, right end of the box)
steps: Sign in and open an existing chat that already has messages.
Leave the message box empty and make sure the selected model is a cloud model.
Click the round waveform button named 'Start voice mode' at the right end of the message box.
Look: the message box is replaced by the voice bar, and the chat you opened is still on screen. Compare with Expected: voice starts bound to that chat.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access; a microphone; a cloud model selected
items.note: The button shows only when the message box is empty, voice access is granted and the model is a managed cloud model (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx, voiceManaged).

items.where: Sidebar > 'New chat' > empty message box > round button 'Start voice mode' (right end of the box)
steps: Click 'New chat' in the sidebar.
Leave the message box empty.
Click 'Start voice mode'.
Look: a voice call starts on the new chat. Compare with Expected: a brand-new chat is created for the call.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access; a microphone; a cloud model selected
items.note: No separate control for a new voice chat was found; it uses the same button as S48.01. Whether the new chat is created at call start was not traced in the UI.

items.where: Open a chat that already has messages > round button 'Start voice mode' (right end of the message box)
steps: Open a chat with several earlier messages.
Click 'Start voice mode'.
Look at the header: the word 'Voice' appears next to the logo.
Speak one sentence and wait for the reply.
Look: your words and the reply appear in the same list as the typed messages, above the voice bar. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access

items.where: Voice view > round orb in the middle of the screen (its name is 'Hide the transcript and focus the orb')
steps: Start a voice call (see S48.01).
Click the orb in the middle of the screen.
Look: the transcript fades and the orb is the focus of the view.
Click the orb again and look for the name 'Show the transcript again' on it.
Compare with Expected: a separate full-screen voice layout.
items.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access

labels.text: Hide the transcript and focus the orb

items.note: No separate full-screen page was found. The closest is this focus mode, which fades the transcript inside the same voice view.

items.where: Voice view > round orb in the middle of the screen
steps: Start a voice call (see S48.01) and wait until the call is idle and waiting for you.
Look at the orb: it shows its listening state.
Optional: with VoiceOver on, listen for the announcement 'Listening'.
Compare with Expected: a visible and announced listening state.
items.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access
items.note: The word 'Listening' is not drawn on screen (the orb label is hidden in the voice view). The visible cue is the orb; the word is only in the screen-reader announcement.

items.where: Voice view > round orb in the middle of the screen
steps: Start a voice call and ask a short question.
Wait for the assistant's reply to start playing.
Look at the orb: it changes while the reply plays.
Optional: with VoiceOver on, listen for 'Assistant is speaking'.
Compare with Expected: a visible speaking state.
items.needs: a microphone; a speaker or headphones; a signed-in account with voice access
items.note: The word 'Speaking' is not drawn on screen; the visible cue is the orb.

items.where: Voice view > line with a spinner under the orb reading 'Working on your request' (with a 'Stop the task' button)
steps: Start a voice call.
Ask for something that needs a tool or a lookup.
Look under the orb for a spinner and the text 'Working on your request', with a 'Stop the task' button beside it.
Compare with Expected: a visible thinking or working state while the assistant works.
items.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access
items.note: The line shows when a tool runs or the backend is busy. Which requests trigger it depends on the model and the task.

items.where: Voice view > round orb in the middle of the screen
steps: Start a voice call.
Speak a long sentence at normal volume.
Look at the orb: it grows and shrinks with your voice.
Wait for a reply and look at the orb again.
Compare with Expected: a visual follows the live audio level.
items.needs: a microphone; a speaker or headphones; a signed-in account with voice access
items.note: No separate waveform bar was found; the orb itself follows the audio level (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/VoiceOrb.tsx).

items.where: Voice view > bottom voice bar > round microphone button (named 'Turn off microphone')
steps: Start a voice call.
Click the round microphone button in the bottom bar.
Look: the icon changes to a crossed-out microphone, the button turns red, and its name becomes 'Turn on microphone'.
Look at the call timer: it keeps running.
Click the button again and check the microphone is back on. Compare with Expected: mute without ending the call.
items.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access
items.note: Pressing Space while the voice bar's text field is empty also toggles mute (VoiceComposer.tsx).

items.where: Voice view > bottom voice bar > round X button named 'End voice session' (right end)
steps: Start a voice call and talk for a moment.
Click the X button 'End voice session'.
Look: the voice bar closes, the normal message box comes back, and the call timer stops.
Compare with Expected: the call is closed.
items.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access
items.note: Escape also ends the call. Settling of usage is not visible on screen.

items.where: Voice view > round '+' button at the left of the bottom bar > menu 'In this chat' > 'Pause call'
steps: Start a voice call.
Click the round '+' button at the left of the bottom bar.
Click 'Pause call' under the menu heading 'In this chat'. Hmm: the item sits under the heading 'This call'.
Look: a notice says the call is paused and a 'Resume' button appears.
Click 'Resume' and check the call comes back without starting over. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access
items.note: The paused notice says the call is closed while paused, so check whether resume keeps the same conversation against Expected.

items.where: No on or off switch found; the effect shows across turns in the voice view
steps: Start a voice call.
Say one thing and wait for the reply to finish.
Say a second thing without touching any button.
Look: the orb returns to listening and takes the second turn without a tap.
items.needs: a microphone; a speaker or headphones; a signed-in account with voice access
items.note: No hands-free switch was found in the code. The check is only whether a second turn needs no tap.

items.where: Seen in the voice view while the orb shows the speaking state
steps: Start a voice call and ask for a long answer.
While the orb shows the speaking state and the reply is playing, start talking over it.
Look: the spoken reply stops and the orb moves to listening. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a microphone; a speaker or headphones; a signed-in account with voice access; a live voice service
items.note: Unverified in the code. It depends on the external voice service, so the result may vary by session.

items.where: Voice view > gear button 'Voice settings' (next to 'Voice' in the header) > voice name between the arrows 'Previous voice' and 'Next voice'
steps: Start a voice call.
Click the gear button 'Voice settings'.
Click 'Next voice' and look at the name in the middle change.
Click the voice name dots below, if shown, to pick another voice.
Close the dialog, let the assistant speak, and check the voice matches the name you chose. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a microphone; a speaker or headphones; a signed-in account with voice access
items.note: The dots appear only when there are 2 to 16 voices.

items.where: Voice view > gear button 'Voice settings' > under the voice name, button 'Play sample'
steps: Start a voice call and open 'Voice settings'.
Look under the voice name and arrows for the button 'Play sample'.
Click 'Play sample' and listen.
Compare with Expected: a sample of the voice plays before you choose it.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access; a speaker or headphones
items.note: Unfinished. apps/web/public/voice-samples/manifest.json is empty, so 'Play sample' does not appear until the sample files are generated (plan owner step: OPENAI_API_KEY=<server key> node scripts/generate-voice-samples.mjs, then commit apps/web/public/voice-samples).

items.where: Voice view > gear button 'Voice settings' > 'Language' picker (first option 'Auto-detect')
steps: Start a voice call and open 'Voice settings'.
Click the 'Language' picker and choose a language other than 'Auto-detect'.
Close the dialog and speak in that language.
Compare with Expected: the spoken language is used for recognition. Check the transcript and reply.
items.needs: a microphone; a speaker or headphones; a signed-in account with voice access
items.note: Whether recognition follows the choice is confirmed only by a live call.

items.where: Voice view > gear button 'Voice settings' > 'Audio output' button (shows 'System default' or a device name)
steps: Start a voice call and open 'Voice settings'.
Click the 'Audio output' button and open its list.
Choose a different speaker from the list.
Let the assistant speak and check the sound comes from the chosen speaker. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a browser that can switch speaker output (the code checks for this); a second audio output device
items.note: The picker checks browser support before switching output. What it shows in an unsupported browser was not traced.

items.where: Voice view > round '+' button at the left of the bottom bar > 'This call' > 'Captions'
steps: Start a voice call.
Click the round '+' button at the left of the bottom bar.
Click 'Captions' under the heading 'This call'.
Speak, and let the assistant reply.
Look for lines labelled 'You' and 'Assistant' appearing as text. Compare with Expected: captions of both speakers.
items.needs: a microphone; a speaker or headphones; a signed-in account with voice access

items.where: Open the chat after the voice call (the voice turns are saved as messages in that chat)
steps: Make a short voice call with two spoken turns.
Click the X button 'End voice session' to finish the call.
Look at the chat: your spoken turns and the replies appear as messages in order.
Reload the page and check the same messages are still there. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a microphone; a speaker or headphones; a signed-in account with voice access
items.note: If a voice turn cannot be saved, a warning toast appears (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx).

items.where: Voice view > tool row above the orb after a tool runs; then, in the chat above, the 'Stopped thinking' or 'Thought for' link under an assistant reply opens 'Activity'
steps: Start a voice call and ask for a task that uses a tool.
Look above the orb for the tool row with the tool name and result.
Scroll up in the chat while the call stays open and click the link under an assistant reply.
Look: the 'Activity' panel opens and lists the steps. Press Escape to close it. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access; a task that uses a tool
items.note: The link under the reply shows only while voice mode is on (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx). The text 'Thought for' is built from a number in VoiceActivityAffordance.tsx.

items.where: Voice view > card above the orb for an action that needs approval, with buttons such as 'Allow once', 'Allow for this chat' and 'Deny'
steps: Start a voice call.
Ask for an action that needs approval, such as one that changes something.
Look for the approval card in the voice view.
Click 'Allow once' or 'Deny'.
Look: the card closes and the call continues without leaving voice. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access; a task that asks for approval
items.note: Which buttons appear depends on the action's scopes (apps/web/features/chat/components/approvals/ToolApprovalCard.tsx).

items.where: Voice view > under the tool row, a link 'Open' followed by the file name (images show as a picture link)
steps: Start a voice call and ask for a task that creates a document.
Look under the tool row for 'Open' with a file name.
Click the link.
Look: the file opens in a new browser tab. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access; a task that creates a file
items.note: Only files with paths under /api/files/ are shown as links (VoiceModeSurface.tsx).

items.where: Voice view > a line 'Reconnecting, attempt N of M' above the orb when the connection drops
steps: Start a voice call.
Turn off Wi-Fi for a few seconds.
Look above the orb for 'Reconnecting, attempt' with a spinner and a count.
Turn Wi-Fi back on and look again: the line goes away and the call continues, or an error with 'Try again' appears. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access; a way to drop the connection (for example Wi-Fi off)
items.note: There is no button; the state appears only when the connection drops.

items.where: Voice view > notice with 'Upgrade' and 'Continue in text' when voice usage runs out
steps: Use voice until the voice allowance is used up.
Look in the voice view for the usage notice with the buttons 'Upgrade' and 'Continue in text'.
Click 'Continue in text' and check you return to the text message box in the same chat. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: an account whose voice usage is used up
items.note: The notice text comes from the server error, so its wording is not fixed in the code.

items.where: Voice view > X button 'End voice session' at the right end of the bottom bar (or Escape), then the normal message box
steps: In a call on a chat that has messages, click the X button 'End voice session'.
Look: the normal message box returns in the same chat, with the earlier voice turns above it.
Type a message and send it.
Compare with Expected: the send goes into the same unfinished conversation.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access; a microphone
items.note: The bottom voice bar also has a text field that sends a normal turn without leaving voice (VoiceComposer.tsx).

items.where: Open an earlier chat from the sidebar, then with the message field empty click Start voice mode
steps: Sign in and open a chat that already has a voice conversation or earlier turns.
Leave the message field empty so the round button on the right shows its voice icon.
Click the button labelled Start voice mode.
Check that the voice view opens for that same chat and that the assistant answers with the earlier turns in mind (ask it what you talked about before).
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: The code starts voice on the open chat's conversation ID and loads earlier context for that conversation; I did not find a sidebar label for the earlier chat, and the needs value of a paid account is a guess.

items.needs: a computer paired with the Desktop app
items.note: The remote coding page is at the route apps/web/app/code/computer/page.tsx, with a Task box that has a Start voice input button (dictation) and a Send to computer button, but RemoteComputerLink, which should link to it, has no caller in apps or features, so I could not confirm a menu path; the page offers dictated task text, not a voice conversation.

items.where: Start voice mode, then while a task is running click Stop the task
steps: Open a chat, leave the message field empty and click Start voice mode.
Ask for an action that takes a while, such as a web search.
While the status line with a spinner is showing, click Stop the task.
Check that the status line goes away, the call stays open and the voice conversation still works. The task should stop without ending the call.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: Stop the task appears only when the agent status is shown and calls cancelBackendWork; I found no separate control that stops only the spoken reply (the only other stop-like labels are Do not send that and Stop sharing your camera), so the spoken-reply half of Expected is not confirmed.

items.where: Message box > microphone button (no visible text; its label is "Start voice input"), then "Stop recording and edit the transcript"
steps: Sign in and open a chat with an empty message box.
Click the microphone button next to the message box, labelled "Start voice input".
Say a short sentence while the recording strip is shown.
Click "Stop recording and edit the transcript" (the square button).
Wait for "Transcribing" to disappear, then look at the message box: the spoken words should appear there, as in Expected.
items.needs: a microphone

labels.text: Stop recording and edit the transcript

items.note: The microphone button has no visible text, only an accessible label; the Settings switch that enables it is described under S49.03.

items.where: Message box > microphone button "Start voice input", then "Stop recording and edit the transcript"
steps: Start dictation with the "Start voice input" microphone button and say a sentence.
Click "Stop recording and edit the transcript".
When "Transcribing" finishes, click into the message box.
Edit a word in the transcript, then check that the text changed and nothing has been sent yet.
items.needs: a microphone

labels.text: Stop recording and edit the transcript

items.note: Pressing Enter while recording sends the transcript straight away (DictationStrip.tsx handleKeyDown), so testers should not press Enter if they want to edit first.

items.where: Settings > Voice > "Dictation language" (dropdown under the Dictation switch)
steps: Open Settings and click "Voice".
Make sure the "Dictation" switch is on.
Open the "Dictation language" dropdown and choose a different language.
Close Settings, click "Start voice input", and speak in the chosen language.
Check that the transcript comes back in that language, as in Expected.
items.needs: a microphone
items.note: The code does not show how the Settings window is opened from the app; the path above starts at the Settings screen.

items.where: Message box > "Start voice input" microphone button, then "Stop recording and edit the transcript"
steps: Click "Start voice input", say a sentence, then click "Stop recording and edit the transcript".
Watch the strip show "Transcribing".
When the strip goes away, look at the message box for the final transcript.
Compare the text with what you said.
items.needs: a microphone
items.note: The "Transcript ready" text is only announced to screen readers (use-dictation.ts), not shown on screen.

items.where: Message box > "Start voice input" microphone button; on failure the strip shows "Try again"
steps: Click "Start voice input", say a sentence, then click "Stop recording and edit the transcript".
If transcription fails, the strip shows an error with a "Try again" button (or "Dismiss voice input error" to close it).
Click "Try again" and check that the transcript is produced without recording again.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a microphone; a way to make transcription fail (the code does not say how a tester should cause a failure)
items.note: The failure message in the code reads "That recording could not be transcribed. Try again." (use-dictation.ts); the "Try again" button is in DictationStrip.tsx.

items.where: Message box > "Start voice input" microphone button, then the round "Discard recording" button at the left of the strip
steps: Click "Start voice input" and say a sentence.
Click "Discard recording" (the X button at the left of the strip).
Check that the strip closes and the message box is unchanged, with no transcript added.
Optional: repeat and press Escape instead of clicking the X; the recording should be discarded the same way.
items.needs: a microphone

items.where: Effect seen in the message box: the whole recording appears as one transcript after "Transcribing"; the request is made by the transcription endpoint (apps/web/app/api/voice/transcribe/route.ts)
steps: Click "Start voice input", say a longer sentence, then click "Stop recording and edit the transcript".
Watch the strip: no partial text appears while speaking; "Transcribing" shows until the whole transcript is ready.
Compare with Expected: the full transcript arrives in one piece after the recording stops.
items.needs: a microphone

labels.text: Stop recording and edit the transcript

items.note: The transcription handler file does not name its mode; batch behaviour is inferred from the single POST and the Transcribing state, not verified against a running request.

items.where: Message box (empty) > "Start voice mode" button, then the live call screen with "End voice session"
steps: Sign in, open a chat and leave the message box empty.
Click the button labelled "Start voice mode" (it appears next to the message box when there is no text).
Allow the microphone and speak; watch whether your words appear as text while you are still talking.
Click "End voice session" when done.
items.needs: a microphone
items.note: The live path is a voice call (live-voice-session.ts), not the dictation strip; the code shows transcript turns but not where they are shown on screen, so the exact spot is unverified.

items.needs: a microphone
items.note: Searched apps/web for notice, agree, consent and recorded in the voice, composer, dictation and live-voice files; found no recording notice. The only consent code is for named model providers (apps/web/features/models), which is unrelated.

items.needs: a conversation with dictated or voice text
items.note: No transcript-only export found. The nearest is "Export…" in the conversation title menu (apps/web/features/chat/components/ConversationTitleMenu.tsx), which exports the whole conversation, not a recording transcript.

items.needs: none
items.note: No retention or delete control for voice recordings or transcripts found. The only retention control is the workspace "Retention window" in apps/web/features/settings/sections/WorkspacePolicySection.tsx, which is not shown to be about voice. The store has an internal clearTranscript (apps/web/features/chat/stores/voice-input-store.ts), with no button found.

items.where: Effect seen in the message box: Cmd+Z (the normal undo shortcut) after dictated text is inserted
steps: Click "Start voice input", say a sentence, then click "Stop recording and edit the transcript" and wait for the text to land in the message box.
Click into the message box and press Cmd+Z.
Compare with Expected: the dictated text should be removed by the normal undo.
items.needs: a microphone

items.where: Chat, under an assistant reply > More message actions > Read message aloud
steps: Sign in to the AGI Web app and open a conversation that has an assistant reply.
Move the pointer over the assistant reply, then click the button labelled More message actions.
Click Read message aloud in the menu.
Look for the reply being spoken aloud, and for the same menu item now reading Stop reading message while it plays.
items.needs: a browser that supports speech synthesis, with at least one system voice
items.note: The Read message aloud item appears only when the browser supports speech and the reply has readable text; I did not trace whether the More message actions button is hover-only on desktop.

items.where: Settings > General > Preferences > Backup read-aloud voice
steps: Sign in, open Settings, and choose the General tab.
Scroll to the Preferences heading and find the row Backup read-aloud voice.
Open the drop-down labelled Backup read-aloud voice and choose a voice; each option shows its name and language code in brackets, and Browser default is the first option.
Click Preview next to the drop-down and listen; compare the voice and language with what you chose.
items.needs: a browser with at least one system voice; the row shows a message instead if the browser has no voices
items.note: There is no separate language picker for read-aloud; the language comes with the chosen voice. The menu entry that opens Settings was not traced to its exact label, so the first step names the General tab only.

items.where: Settings > General > Preferences > Read-aloud speed
steps: Sign in, open Settings, and choose the General tab.
Scroll to the Preferences heading and find the row Read-aloud speed.
Click Slow, Normal or Fast; the chosen button is shown as pressed.
Open an assistant reply, use Read message aloud, and compare the pace with the Normal setting.
items.needs: a browser with speech synthesis support; the row is hidden when speech is not supported
items.note: The speed applies to browser read-aloud only (rates in apps/web/shared/stores/web-settings-store.ts); the separate Live voice pace row in the same section is for live voice conversations. The menu entry that opens Settings was not traced to its exact label.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > Browse (then Add from the catalog)
steps: Open Settings and choose Skills under the Customize group.
Click Browse at the top right of the Skills page.
Look for the catalogue list of skills, including ones not yet installed.
Click one skill name to open its detail page and check it opens.

items.note: The Browse button comes from the shared directory panel; the catalogue and detail views are the same screens used for the Installed list.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Skills

Look at the list of skills shown for this account.
Check the Status column of each row (for example 'Available' or an installed state).
Compare the rows with the skills you know are active for this account.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The list header 'Installed' is the catalogue label for skills; the Status column text comes from the skill data, not a fixed label.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > Add > Create a skill
steps: Open Settings, then Skills.
Click Add and choose Create a skill.
Fill in Name, Description and Instructions, then click Create skill.
Check the new skill appears in your own list, and that the empty-state text 'No skills of your own yet.' is gone.

labels.text: No skills of your own yet.

items.note: Creating a skill is shown only when the account has the skill-create capability; the page ownership rule itself is server-side and not visible here.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > [skill name]

Click any skill name in the list.

Check the Enable skill switch and the Try in chat button are visible.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > Browse

items.where: Chat message box > type / (slash), or Settings > Customize > Skills > [skill name] > Try in chat

Click Create skill (or Save changes when editing) and check the text is kept.

items.note: The editor dialog title is New skill for create mode; an edit entry point for an existing own skill was not confirmed in the code.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > [skill name] > Skill files

Look in the chat for a code run or tool result that the skill's script produced.
items.needs: a skill with a script file and code execution allowed

Open a task and click Open source chat; compare the title shown there with the row title.
