items.note: No rename control was found on the Tasks page; the row title is the source chat's conversation title (runTitle in TasksPage.tsx), so changing it is done in the source chat, which I did not verify.

items.where: Command palette (Cmd+K) > Work history > open a task > Goal section
steps: Press Cmd+K and choose Work history.
Click a task row.
Read the Goal block at the top of the task details.
Compare the goal text with what you typed when starting the task.
items.needs: a task that was started with a goal

items.where: Composer > Add attachments and tools (+) > Add scope (optional) > Deliverable
steps: In a Work composer, click the + button labelled Add attachments and tools.
Click Add scope (optional).
Type in the Deliverable field, for example a report or a file.
Send the goal and open the task; check that the deliverable appears in the task details.
items.needs: a paid account, a project selected
items.note: The Deliverable value is sent with the goal; the task detail panel does not show it as its own labelled field, so check it in the Goal text.

items.where: Composer > Add attachments and tools (+) > Work tools palette > Connected apps, Folders, Skills, Plugins
steps: In a Work composer, click Add attachments and tools (+).
Read the Work tools palette.
Look at the sections Connected apps, Folders, Skills and Plugins and tick the ones the task may use.
Compare the ticked sources with the sources shown in the task after it starts.
items.needs: a paid account, connected apps or folders for the sections to fill

items.where: Composer > Add attachments and tools (+) > Add scope (optional) > Tools this task may use
steps: In a Work composer, click Add attachments and tools (+) and then Add scope (optional).
Read the Tools this task may use group.
Tick or untick Web search and browsing and Code execution.
Send the goal and check the task only uses the ticked tools.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: Only two tool choices have translated labels in the en file; the source code may list more.

items.where: Composer footer > model button (aria label Change model)
steps: In a Chat or Work composer, look at the composer footer.
Click the model name button (its accessible name ends with Change model).
Pick another model and close the list.
Send a Work goal and open the task; check the model is shown on the task row.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: The footer model selector is hidden in image and video modes.

items.where: Composer footer > Reasoning effort button > Reasoning effort slider
steps: In the composer footer, click the button titled Reasoning effort.
Move the Reasoning effort slider to another level.
Send the goal.
Check the level on the task after it starts; compare with Expected.
items.needs: a model that supports reasoning effort
items.note: The effort control only appears when the selected model has an effort setting.

items.where: Work chat > send a goal > Review the plan card (Start work or Cancel)
steps: Send a Work goal in a project chat.
Wait for the Review the plan card to appear.
Edit a step text, or click Add a step or Remove this step.
Click Start work, or Cancel, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account, a project selected, the agent must produce a plan

items.where: Command palette (Cmd+K) > Work history > click a task > Task plan section
steps: Open Work history and click a task.
Find the Task plan section, headed Plan with the step count.
Read the steps and the coloured dot next to each one.
Compare each dot with the step result after the run finishes.
items.needs: a task with a plan
items.note: Step status is shown only by coloured dots, with no status word, so a tester can see it only by colour.

items.where: Command palette (Cmd+K) > Work history > click a running task > Task plan section
steps: Open Work history and click a task that is still running.
Look at the Task plan section.
Find the step with the filled dot in the running colour.
Wait and check that the marked step moves forward as the run continues.
items.needs: a task that is running
items.note: The running step has no text label; only its dot colour marks it.

items.where: Work chat > tool activity list > group labelled parallel
steps: Start a Work task that runs several tools at once.
Open the tool activity list in the chat while the task runs.
Look for a group marked with the word parallel and a branch icon.
Compare the grouped tools with what ran at the same time.
items.needs: a Work task that runs tools in parallel
items.note: Whether the agent runs tools in parallel depends on the task; the group only appears when two or more tools share a parallel group.

items.where: Work chat > clarifying question card (Send answers)
steps: Send a short, vague Work request.
If the agent asks a question, read the card with its options.
Pick an option or type in Something else…, then click Send answers.
Check the agent continues the task with your answer.
items.needs: a paid account, a project selected
items.note: The card appears only when the agent decides to ask; the tester cannot force it.

items.where: Tasks (Work history) > Needs you filter > task card: Waiting for your approval > Approve or Deny
steps: Open Work history and choose the Needs you filter.
Find a task with the card Waiting for your approval.
Read the tool call shown on the card.
Click Approve or Deny, then check the task resumes or stops.
items.needs: a task that needs approval

items.where: Work history > open a running task > Message the agent box > Send
steps: Open Work history and click a running task.
Click into the box Message the agent to add instructions or change course.
Type new guidance and click Send.
Check the queued message appears and the task changes course without restarting.
items.needs: a task that is still running

labels.text: Message the agent to add instructions or change course

items.where: Work history > List or Board > task > Pause
steps: Open Work history on a running task.
Click Pause on the task row (List) or card (Board).
Watch the badge change to Pausing and then Paused.
Check that the task keeps its completed steps when it stops.
items.needs: a running task
items.note: The step-boundary timing of the pause is not visible in the UI.

items.where: Work history > Active filter > paused task > Resume
steps: Open Work history and choose the Active filter.
Find a task with the badge Paused.
Click Resume on the row or card.
Check the task continues from its last completed step.
items.needs: a paused or stopped task

items.where: Work history > Board > task card > Stop
steps: Open Work history and click the Board layout.
Find a running task card.
Click Stop on the card.
Check the task ends as Stopped and the run stops on the server.
items.needs: a running task
items.note: Stop was found on the Board layout only; the List layout was not verified.

items.where: Work chat > plan review card > Retry from this step
steps: Run a Work task until a step fails.
Find the plan review card for that run.
Click Retry from this step on the step that failed.
Check the task continues from that step.
items.needs: a Work task with a failed step
items.note: Whether the button appears for every failed step was not verified; a failed run is needed to test it.

items.where: Work history > click a finished task > Re-run this task
steps: Open Work history and click a finished task (not a live one).
Find the Goal block and click Re-run this task.
A new Work chat opens with the goal, constraints and deliverable filled in.
Send it and compare the new run with the old one.
items.needs: a finished task
items.note: No separate Restart control was found; Re-run this task is the closest match.

items.needs: a finished task
items.note: No Duplicate label was found in the tasks UI (searched TasksPage.tsx, TaskDetailPanel.tsx and the tasks folder). The nearest control is Re-run this task (TaskDetailPanel.tsx), which loads the goal into a new Work chat; desktop DesktopTasks.tsx was not opened.

items.where: Work history > click a finished task > Result section
steps: Open Work history and click a completed task.
Find the section labelled Result.
Read the result text.
Compare it with what the task produced.
items.needs: a completed task

items.where: Work history > click a task > Outputs section > Download and open
steps: Open Work history and click a task that produced files.
Open the Outputs section.
Click Download and open on a file.
Check the file opens or downloads and matches the name and size shown.
items.needs: a task that produced files
items.note: Without files the section says No generated files are recorded for this task.

items.where: Work history > Archived or All filter > task with state Partially completed > Task plan section
steps: Open Work history and choose the All filter.
Click a task whose state is Partially completed.
Read the line Done X of Y steps before it stopped.
Read the Remaining: list and compare with what was done.
items.needs: a task that stopped short

items.where: Command palette (Cmd+K) > Work history, or sidebar Chats and tasks > Tasks filter; then Work history filters Active, Needs you, All, Archived
steps: Press Cmd+K and choose Work history.
Click each filter: Active, Needs you, All, Archived.
Switch between List and Board.
Click Show more if it appears, then open any task and compare its state with the badge.
items.needs: none (more tasks make it easier to test)

items.where: Work history (route /tasks, also reached from the command palette action or the "Work history" link on the home screen) > open a finished task in the list > open the details panel > expand the details disclosure > Share task
steps: Sign in and open Work history from the home screen link "Work history" or the command palette.
Click a task that has a source chat and is not live (a finished one), so its details open on the right.
Expand the details section of the task panel.
Click the button "Share task" (it only appears when the task has a source chat and is not running).

Look for the share dialog on the source chat (the app opens /chat/<id>?share=true, which opens the chat's share dialog) and compare with Expected: the task's plan, steps and results should be shareable. Note: the handler shares the source conversation, not a separate task record.
items.needs: a Free or paid account with at least one finished work task that has a source chat
items.note: The share button sends the user to the source chat's share dialog (apps/web/features/tasks/components/TasksPage.tsx:40 uses ?share=true, handled in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:1686), so it shares the conversation, not a separate task view. Whether the plan, steps and results are all included in that share was not verified. The exact dialog title was not confirmed as a task-specific label. Confirmed the dialog exists at apps/web/features/chat/components/share/ShareConversationDialog.tsx.

items.where: Work history (route /tasks) > open a task from the list, or open a link with ?run=<id>; the list is loaded from the server, so the same account on another device shows the same tasks
steps: On device A, start a work task and note its title in Work history.
On device B (same account, signed in), open Work history.
Find the same task in the list (the list filter defaults to "active") and click it.
On device B, try a running control such as "Pause", "Cancel", or a pending approval ("Approve" or "Deny").

Compare with Expected: device B should show the same task state as device A and be able to act on it. A message such as "Another device already resumed this task." or "Another device already answered this approval." means the action was refused because device A acted first.
items.needs: a paid account (signed in on two devices) and a running task; a Free account may not have work tasks

labels.text: Another device already resumed this task.
Another device already answered this approval.

items.note: The run list comes from the server (getClient().listRuns in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/tasks/TasksPage.tsx:247), so the cross-device behaviour depends on the server side. The Expected behaviour was not judged. The web page's list fetch (apps/web/features/tasks/components/TasksPage.tsx) and the list route apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/runs/route.ts were not read beyond the lines named in the plan.

items.where: Settings > Notifications > Manage tasks (opens Work history, the /tasks page). The page title is Work history; the default filter is Active and the default layout is List. Home > Work history appears only when there are more than 5 active runs.
steps: Sign in and open Settings, then open the Notifications section.
Find the row titled Scheduled task finished and click Manage tasks.
On the Work history page, keep the filter on Active and the layout on List.
Look at the list: each running session should appear as its own row with its state label, and several rows can show running states at the same time.
Click Board in the Task layout control and compare the same sessions in the board view.
items.needs: An account with two or more Cloud work sessions running or active at the same time.
items.note: The Settings entry point from the account menu was not traced. Work history is not in the left rail (apps/web/shared/components/layout/app-nav-items.test.ts says no Tasks entry). Live refresh of the other sessions was not traced; only the selected session auto-refreshes.

items.where: Work history > filter Needs you (also: the Active list puts sessions that need input first).
steps: Open Work history as in S62.09.
Keep the filter on Active and look at the top rows of the list.
Sessions that are waiting for you (awaiting input, awaiting approval or paused) should be listed above the others.
Click Needs you in the filter control and check that only those waiting sessions are shown.
Compare with Expected: waiting sessions come first and can be filtered alone.
items.needs: At least one session that is waiting for input or approval, and one that is running, if possible.
items.note: The ordering is applied in code (orderedRuns in TasksPage.tsx) to the loaded list only; no label says it is a priority sort.

items.where: Work history > click a session row (View details for <title>) > Approve or Deny in the Waiting for your approval card. A paused session shows a Resume button in the same panel.
steps: Open Work history and click a session that is waiting for approval.
In the details panel, read the Waiting for your approval card and the listed tool calls.
Optionally type in the box Tell the agent what to change when it resumes (optional) or Add guidance to steer this run (optional).
Click Approve (or Deny) and watch the card show a spinner, then leave the card.
Check that the page stayed on Work history and the session state changed. For a paused session, click Resume.
items.needs: A Cloud work session that is waiting for a tool approval, or is paused.
items.note: The Approve and Deny buttons also appear on board cards as icon buttons with aria-labels; the Resume button is shown for paused sessions. Whether a session that is only waiting for input (not approval) can be answered inline was not confirmed.

items.where: Work history > click a session row > Open source chat, in the details panel.
steps: Open Work history and click a session row to open its details panel.
Read the panel sections: Task goal, Task plan and Latest output or Result.
Find the button Open source chat (it shows only when the session has a source chat).
Click Open source chat.
Compare with Expected: the chat opens on its full conversation at /chat/<id>, showing the messages of that task.
items.needs: A Cloud work session that was started from a chat (so it has a source chat).
items.note: The details panel itself shows a summary (goal, plan, output or result), not a message-by-message transcript; the full transcript is reached through the source chat. Without a source chat the panel shows no button.

items.where: Chat > open an existing chat > move the pointer over an assistant reply and click the Branch conversation from here icon (tooltip Branch conversation: this chat stays unchanged). User messages have the same action in More message actions.
steps: Open an existing chat with at least one reply from the assistant.
Move the pointer over the reply (on touch, tap it) to show its action buttons.
Click the branch icon, with the tooltip Branch conversation: this chat stays unchanged.
Wait for the toast Conversation branch created and the new chat page to open.
Type a new message in the new chat and compare with Expected: the original chat stays unchanged and the new chat continues from that point.
items.needs: A Free or paid account with a chat that has at least one reply.

labels.text: Branch conversation: this chat stays unchanged

items.note: The toast text Conversation branch created is in apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-conversation-branches.ts. Hover visibility of the assistant action bar was read from class names, not confirmed in a browser. The branch badge in the message row (BranchNavigator) appears only after a branch exists.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > More ways to create a task (chevron beside New task) > Start from a template
steps: Click Scheduled in the sidebar.
Click the chevron beside New task (its label is More ways to create a task).
Click Start from a template.
Look for the Start from a template panel with a grid labelled Schedule templates, and check you can browse several templates.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan (the create controls are hidden otherwise) and at least one existing routine, because the gallery panel only shows when the list is not empty
items.note: The gallery panel is rendered only when galleryOpen is true and the routine list is not empty; with no routines the empty state shows Create Your First Schedule instead. Whether the gallery can be reopened at any time was not confirmed.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch, then fill Task Instructions and click Create Schedule
steps: Click Scheduled in the sidebar.
Click New task, or choose Create from scratch from the chevron menu.
In the Create Schedule dialog, type your instructions in Task Instructions and enter a Schedule Name.
Click Create Schedule and check that the new routine appears in the list with its name and prompt.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan; a Free account sees Scheduled tasks are available on Basic and higher plans.
items.note: The earlier in-app check was blocked by plan (E054), so creation was not exercised.

items.where: Chat > an assistant reply's more-actions menu > Run this on a schedule
steps: Open a chat and wait for an assistant reply to finish.
Open the more-actions menu on that reply (its trigger label was not confirmed in code).
Click Run this on a schedule.
Check that the Create Schedule dialog opens pre-filled from that reply, then save it and look for the new routine under Scheduled.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and a finished chat reply
items.note: The menu's trigger button text was not confirmed; only the menu item label was found.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch (Schedule Name and Description fields); to edit later, Scheduled > Edit <routine name>
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task, then Create from scratch.
Type a value in Schedule Name and an optional value in Description.
Click Create Schedule.
Click the edit (pencil) button on the routine, change Schedule Name or Description, click Save Changes, and check the card shows the new values.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch (Task Instructions box); edit later with Scheduled > Edit <routine name>
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task, then Create from scratch.
Type several lines in Task Instructions, including a line break.
Click Create Schedule, then open the routine's edit (pencil) button.
Check that the Task Instructions text is shown and editable, and that Save Changes stores the change.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch > Sources
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task, then Create from scratch.
Find the Sources group in the form.
Tick and untick the source options offered.
Click Create Schedule and open Edit on the routine to check the same sources are still ticked.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan; a project may be needed for project-file sources (the code passes a hasProject flag)
items.note: Which source options appear depends on whether a project is selected; the exact option labels were not extracted.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch > Connectors
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task, then Create from scratch.
Find the Connectors group in the form; wait for Reading your connectors… to finish.
Tick the connectors the run may use and untick others.
Click Create Schedule and reopen Edit to check the selection is kept.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and at least one connected connector account to see options

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch > Run as agent
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task, then Create from scratch.
Open the Run as agent dropdown.
Choose an agent and read the description that appears under it.
Click Create Schedule, then check the routine card or Edit dialog shows the chosen agent.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and at least one custom agent; the field appears only when agents exist
items.note: The field is hidden when no agent options exist.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch > Frequency > One Time, then Run At
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task, then Create from scratch.
Set Frequency to One Time.
Set Run At to a future date and time.
Click Create Schedule and check the card's Next Run shows that time.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan
items.note: The earlier in-app check was blocked by plan (E054).

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch > Frequency > Daily (or Weekly, Monthly, Interval)
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task, then Create from scratch.
Set Frequency to Daily, Weekly or Monthly, and set Repeat Every where shown.
Click Create Schedule and read the Next Run value on the card.
Wait for a due time, or use Run now, then check Last Run and the run history update.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan; a long wait is needed to see a scheduled fire
items.note: The firing itself is a server cron route (apps/web/app/api/cron/run-schedules/route.ts) with no screen; the tester sees it through Next Run and Last Run.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch > Time Zone
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task, then Create from scratch.
Click Time Zone and type a city or region such as the zone you want.
Pick a zone from the suggestions, set a time, and click Create Schedule.
Open the routine card and compare the Time Zone and Next Run values with the zone you chose.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan
items.note: Suggestions come from a datalist; the helper text says daylight saving follows the chosen zone.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch > Frequency > Custom Cron, Recurrence Rule or Interval; Only Run During is under When It May Run, And What Happens If It Fails
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task, then Create from scratch.
Open Frequency and choose Custom Cron, then type a value in Cron Expression.
Try Recurrence Rule, then Interval with Repeat Every.
Open When It May Run, And What Happens If It Fails and set Only Run During; then check each saved routine's Next Run and Timing.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan
items.note: The Recurrence Rule field was located but its inner behaviour was not read; run windows are the Only Run During setting.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > routine card > History button (title Run History) > Triggers for <routine name> > Add trigger
steps: Click Scheduled and open a routine with the History button (title Run History).
Scroll to the Triggers for section and click Add trigger.
Choose a source such as Gmail, GitHub, Slack or Google Calendar, then fill its fields and click Add trigger to save.
Send or simulate an event from that source and check the routine appears in its run history.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan, the matching connector account for the source, and an outside account for the event source
items.note: A trigger is added from the routine card, not from the create form; the Frequency option When An Event Happens is the form-side choice.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > routine card > History button > Triggers for <routine name> > Add trigger > Only when and Event types
steps: Open a routine's History (title Run History) and click Add trigger.
Set Event types and the Ignore repeats for (seconds) value.
Under Only when, add a condition: pick a field, a comparison and a value.
Save the trigger, then send an event that matches and one that does not, and check only the matching one starts a run.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and an event source connected to send events

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > routine card > History button > Triggers for <routine name> > Add trigger > Anything else (signed webhook)
steps: Open a routine's History (title Run History), click Add trigger.
Choose Anything else (signed webhook) and click Add trigger to save.
Copy the URL and signing secret shown after saving (the exact display text was not extracted).
Send a signed POST to the URL and check a run starts; then click Regenerate secret and check the old secret is rejected.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan, a command-line tool or script that can sign a POST (the panel shows an openssl example)
items.note: The secret is shown in the panel after creation; its exact on-screen text was not found.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > More actions for <routine name> > Run now
steps: Click Scheduled and open the More actions menu on a routine card.
Click Run now.
Wait for the run to finish, then open the History button (title Run History).
Check the newest run in the list shows a status and open View Output to see the result.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan
items.note: Run now is disabled when canRun is false; the conditions were not traced.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > each routine card (Next Run row)
steps: Click Scheduled and find a routine card.
Read the Next Run row and the Timing row.
Compare the next-run time with the routine's Time Zone row.
Use Edit to change the timing, save, and check Next Run changes.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and a routine that has a future run

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > each routine card (Last Run row)
steps: Click Scheduled and find a routine that has run.
Read the Last Run row.
Open History (title Run History) and check the latest run's status badge.
Compare the failed status shown there with Last Run.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and a routine that has run at least once, ideally one that failed
items.note: Whether the card row itself shows a failure, or only the history does, was not confirmed.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > History button (title Run History) on a routine card
steps: Click Scheduled and click the History button on a routine (its aria label is View History for <name>).
Read the Run History heading and the list of runs.
Check each row's status badge and time.
Click Load more if it appears and check older runs load.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and a routine with past runs

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > History button > a run row > View Output
steps: Open a routine's History (title Run History).
Click a run row's View Output disclosure.
Read the output text under it.
Compare the text with the run's status and time shown on the row.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and a run that produced output
items.note: View Output appears only when the run has result text; latest result also opens from a separate card control.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > the switch on a routine card (pause or resume)
steps: Click Scheduled and find a routine card.
Click its switch to pause, which turns the card to Paused.
Read the message that appears (Schedule paused.).
Click the switch again to resume and check the card no longer shows Paused and the message is Schedule resumed.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan
items.note: The switch has no visible text; its accessible name is Pause <name> or Resume <name>.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > Edit <routine name> (pencil button, title Edit Schedule)
steps: Click Scheduled and click the Edit button on a routine card.
In the Edit Schedule dialog, change Schedule Name, a timing field or Task Instructions.
Click Save Changes.
Check the dialog closes, the message Schedule updated. appears and the card shows the new values.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and an existing routine

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > More actions for <routine name> > Delete
steps: Click Scheduled and open the More actions menu on a routine card.
Click Delete.
Read the Delete Schedule? confirmation and click the confirm button.
Check the routine disappears from the list and no longer shows a next run.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and an existing routine
items.note: The confirm button's exact text was not extracted.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > More actions for <routine name> > Share
steps: Click Scheduled and open the More actions menu on a routine card.
Click Share.
In the Share dialog, create the share link and copy it.
Open the link in a private window or as a second account and check a preview of the routine is shown (its copy action was not found).
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and a second account or private window to view the shared link
items.note: The share dialog title is built from the routine name; the copy button label and how a recipient makes their own copy were not found in the read files.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch > Execution Limits > Credit Cap (or Maximum Runs)
steps: Click Scheduled, then New task, then Create from scratch.
Open the Execution Limits section and enter a value in Credit Cap or Maximum Runs.
Click Create Schedule and open Edit on the routine to check the value is kept.
Run the routine until the cap is reached and check it pauses once runs use the credits.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan and enough credits to reach the cap
items.note: The cap pauses the routine after current credits are used; a run already started finishes (helper text in the form).

items.where: Scheduled > (open a schedule's card) > Run History (the clock icon, title "Run History") > run row showing "Waiting for your approval" > Approve
steps: Sign in and click "Scheduled" in the sidebar.
Find a schedule whose run needs a tool approval. Its card may show a paused note: "Paused: a run needed your approval. Approve or deny it in Run History".
Click the Run History icon on that schedule's card (title "Run History").
In the run list, find the run with the "Waiting for your approval" card and read the tool name listed under it.
Click "Approve" (or "Deny") on that card.
Check that the run continues and the status changes from waiting to a finished state, and that a message says "Approved." appeared.
items.needs: a schedule whose run needs a tool approval (for example one that uses a tool requiring approval)
items.note: The approval card and Approve/Deny buttons are in code, and the resume path is in apps/web/features/schedules/components/SchedulesPage.tsx; the approval pause itself is server-side (scheduled-agent-executor.ts), so whether a real run pauses and resumes was not checked. The card title and Approve label are confirmed in code; the "Approved." message is built from SchedulesPage.tsx and the outcome text varies.

items.where: Scheduled > (open a schedule's card) > Run History (the clock icon, title "Run History") > run row with the "skipped" status and a note above it
steps: Sign in and click "Scheduled" in the sidebar.
Find a schedule that has a run marked as missed or skipped. A schedule with missed runs set to skip shows these.
Click the Run History icon on that schedule's card (title "Run History").
Find the run row. Its status word is "skipped" when the run was skipped.
Read the grey note under the run row. It says the run was skipped, the scheduled time, and how late it was.
Compare the note and status with Expected: the history should say that a run was missed or skipped and why.
items.needs: a schedule that has a missed or skipped run (for example a schedule set to skip missed runs whose run was late)
items.note: The note text is built in packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/schedules.ts (for example "Skipped the run scheduled for ...: it was missed by ... and this schedule skips missed runs." and "Ran late: scheduled for ..."), so the exact note is dynamic and not a fixed label; the missed-run detection is in apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.ts. Whether a real run is marked missed was not checked.

items.where: Sidebar > Your computer (Code page). Offline shows as "offline" next to the computer name, and once connected a lost link shows "Your computer went offline. This page reconnects when it is back."
steps: Sign in on the web app and open the sidebar item "Your computer".
Look at the "Computers on your account" list. Each computer shows its state after a dot: "online", "asleep" or "offline".
Connect a paired computer, then quit Desktop on that computer or turn it off.
Wait for the page to update. Look for the message "Your computer went offline. This page reconnects when it is back." and compare with Expected (the product says it is offline and waits).
items.needs: a Free or paid account with Desktop paired on a Mac, and the ability to quit Desktop on that Mac

labels.text: Your computer went offline. This page reconnects when it is back.

items.note: The wait-then-continue copy ("Waiting for <device> to come online" and "Continuing without <device>") is in apps/web/lib/device-steps/device-clearance-step.ts, a server step for Cloud runs. I did not find which screen shows that text, so it is not part of the steps above. The wait budget is one hour, from apps/web/lib/workflows/cloud-agent-workflow.ts.

items.where: On the Mac, Desktop > Settings > Capabilities > Remote Control > Pair a phone > Copy link for a browser. Then in the browser, sidebar > Your computer > Pairing link > Connect > Task box > Send to computer.
steps: On the Mac, open Desktop and go to Settings, Capabilities, Remote Control, Pair a phone, and copy the link for a browser.
In a different browser or device, sign in and open the sidebar item "Your computer".
Paste the link into the field "Paste the link copied on your computer" and click "Connect". Wait until the page shows "Connected to" the computer name.
Type a task in the box "Describe what AGI should do on your computer" and click "Send to computer".
Look at the Tasks list: the new task should appear with a status label (for example queued or running) and the computer should begin work, as Expected says.
items.needs: a paid account (Remote Control comes with paid plans), Desktop on a Mac with Remote Control on, and a second device or browser signed in to the same account

labels.text: Remote Control comes with paid plans.

items.note: Several quoted lines in the Code audit are no longer in the files (RemoteComputerPage.tsx lines 219 and 367, remote-dispatch-client.ts line 155, CodeRail.tsx line 277), so I used the current text. The desktop menu words "Copy link for a browser" and "Pair a phone" come from the instruction text in RemoteComputerPage.tsx and the Desktop capabilities copy in packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/vscode.json, and I did not verify them on the Desktop screen. Owner notes say Remote Control may be hidden in v1, which I did not check in code.

items.where: Code > new session composer > "Select repository" chip > "Repository URL" or the list, then "Use this repository"
steps: Sign in and open Code (the /code page).
In the new-session composer, click the "Select repository" chip.
Pick a repository from the list, or click "Use a repository URL instead" and type an owner/repository URL.
Click "Use this repository".
Look for the chosen repository name on the composer chip and compare with Expected (the repository is chosen before the session starts).
items.needs: a GitHub App installation or a public GitHub repository URL; a cloud sandbox may not start until the deployment gate in the plan is switched on
items.note: The picker only lists repositories when a GitHub App is configured; otherwise only a public URL works (copy in code-surface.ts). Whether a session then runs is not judged here.

items.where: Code > new session composer > "Select repository" > "Branch" field, or "Change the branch" > "Use this branch"
steps: Open Code and choose a repository as in S66.01.
Read the "Branch" field, or click the branch chip and choose a branch from the "Branches" list.
Type a branch name in "Search or type a branch name" if needed, then click "Use this branch".
Compare the branch shown on the chip with Expected (the session starts from that git branch).
items.needs: a repository already chosen (see S66.01)
items.note: A cloud branch field is shown with the repository; the desktop local folder shows branch names through its own chip. Branch switching copy says the branch is checked out in place.

items.where: Code > new session composer > environment chip > "Local" or "Cloud"
steps: Open Code and look at the new-session composer.
Click the environment chip (it shows "Cloud" or "Local" with the network mode).
In the menu, choose "Local" (runs in a chosen folder on this computer) or "Cloud" (runs in an isolated cloud sandbox).
Check that the chip now shows the choice, and compare with Expected (chosen before the session starts).
items.needs: a Desktop folder for the Local option; a signed-in account for Cloud
items.note: The Local option appears in the desktop composer menu (CodeComposer.tsx) only; the web Cloud path is the default. Environment labels are in code-surface.ts.

items.where: Code > left list "Cloud sessions" (sessions group) > click a session title
steps: Open Code.
Look at the session list on the left under "Cloud sessions".
Use the "Filter sessions" menu or "Search sessions" to narrow the list if needed.
Click a session title to open it.
Compare the list and the opened session with Expected (a list of the user's sessions that can be opened).
items.needs: at least one earlier cloud session (empty state shows "No cloud sessions yet.")
items.note: On the desktop app a second list, "On this device", shows local sessions (LOCAL_CODE_COPY in apps/web/features/code/local-code.ts).

items.where: Code > open a session > "Session actions" icon menu > "Rename" > type title > "Rename the session"
steps: Open a cloud session from the session list.
Click the session actions button at the top of the session (it has no visible text; its accessible name is "Session actions").
Click "Rename".
Type a new title in the "Session title" field and click "Rename the session" (or "Keep the current title" to cancel).
Compare the title shown in the list and header with Expected (a readable title that can be renamed).
items.needs: a cloud session you can open
items.note: The "Session actions" button is icon-only, so testers must find it by position at the top of the session. Desktop renaming is a separate title control (LocalSessionTitleInput.tsx).

items.where: Code > left list ("Cloud sessions") > group headings "Running", "Ready", "Idle", and the "Open" badge; closed sessions show the banner "This session is closed."
steps: Open Code and look at the session list.
Find sessions under the group heading "Ready" or "Idle", and any running dot labelled "Running".
Open a session and read its status line or banner.
Compare with Expected (running, waiting for approval, idle, failed or closed).
items.needs: sessions in different states (a running one is hard to set up on demand)
items.note: Only part of the status set is shown: Running, Ready and Idle groups and the closed banner. Failed sessions are grouped as Idle, and no separate "Waiting for approval" session label was found in code-surface.ts.

items.where: Code > open a cloud session > "Changes" panel > "Terminal" section > "Command" field > "Run"
steps: Open a cloud session.
Open the "Changes" panel.
Scroll to the "Terminal" section.
Type a short command (for example ls) in the "Command" field and click "Run".
Compare the output that appears in the Terminal with Expected (the command output is shown in the session).
items.needs: a cloud session with its environment running
items.note: The cloud Terminal is in CodeChangesPanel.tsx. The desktop version is a bottom panel with terminal tabs (LocalTerminal.tsx). The "Changes" button that opens this panel in cloud sessions was not traced to its trigger.

items.where: Code > open a cloud session > "Changes" panel > "Terminal" section (list of commands) and the "Show exit codes" toggle
steps: Open a cloud session that has run a command (the Terminal section says "No commands have run in this session." when empty).
Open the "Changes" panel and go to "Terminal".
Turn on "Show exit codes" if you want exit status shown.
Compare the commands, their output and the exit status with Expected.
items.needs: a session where commands have already run

labels.text: No commands have run in this session.

items.note: The desktop equivalent is the "Running in this folder" block (LocalRunningCommands.tsx), which lists running commands rather than full history.

items.where: Code > open a cloud session > "Changes" panel > click a changed file
steps: Open a cloud session that has changed files.
Open the "Changes" panel and click a file in the list.
Read the line-by-line diff shown for that file (added and removed lines).
Compare with Expected (a line-level diff of the agent's changes).
items.needs: a session where the agent changed files

labels.text: The diff is too large to show in full.

items.note: The diff body is rendered by DiffBody in CodeDiffFile (imported in LocalChangesPanel.tsx). Whether a click expands the diff in place was not confirmed from the code.

items.where: Code > open a cloud session > "Changes" panel (heading "Changes", count "N added, M removed", then a row per file with its state)
steps: Open a cloud session that has changed files.
Open the "Changes" panel.
Read the count line "N added, M removed" and the state word on each file row (Added, Modified, Deleted, Renamed, Untracked or Conflicted).
Compare which files are shown and their state with Expected (created, modified or deleted files).
items.needs: a session where files were created, modified and deleted
items.note: Labels come from CHANGE_STATE_LABELS in code-surface.ts; the file rows are rendered in LocalChangesPanel.tsx and CodeChangesPanel.tsx.

items.where: Code > new session or open session > composer "Mode" control (the approval control, labelled "Approval mode") > choose one of "Ask before every action", "Run read-only actions without asking", "Skip approvals" or "Plan"
steps: Open Code and look at the composer below the message box.
Click the approval/mode control (accessible name "Approval mode"; it shows "Plan" or the short label Ask, Auto or Skip).
Under the heading "Mode", read the options and their hints.
Pick one, then compare the choice and its hint with Expected (agent may act on its own, or asks first).
items.needs: none for reading the options; a running session is needed to see the effect
items.note: There is no option called "edit mode" or "agent mode"; the closest control is this approval-policy menu plus the Plan option. Options and labels come from TOOL_APPROVAL_POLICY_OPTIONS.

items.where: Code > composer "Approval mode" control > "Ask before every action" / "Run read-only actions without asking" / "Skip approvals"; network choice "Isolated", "Trusted hosts", "Full internet" in the environment settings
steps: Open the composer approval control and pick one option, for example "Ask before every action".
Start a task that needs a tool or a write, and see whether the agent waits for an approval card.
Change the option to "Skip approvals" and start another task.
Compare what the agent does with Expected (the chosen mode is honoured while the session runs).
items.needs: a running cloud or local session; a task that uses tools
items.note: Enforcement of the chosen mode at runtime was not verified from the code, only the choice labels. Network labels come from the networkAccess list in code-surface.ts.

items.where: Code > composer > the small usage ring (button named "Usage") > popover "Context window"
steps: Open a session in Code and type in the composer.
Look for the small ring icon near the composer (its accessible name is "Usage").
Click it and read the "Context window" value.
Compare the used amount with Expected (how much of the model context is used).
items.needs: a session with some messages so a context figure exists
items.note: The ring is UsageRing in CodeComposer.tsx (rendered near line 2162). Whether it shows before any message was not confirmed.

items.where: Code > composer "Usage" button > popover "Plan usage limits" ("Five hour limit", "Weekly, all models", "Weekly, top model"); also the Usage settings page
steps: Open Code and find the "Usage" button in the composer.
Click it to open the popover.
Read "Plan usage limits" and the "Five hour limit" and "Weekly, all models" figures.
Click "See detailed breakdown" if you want more detail.
Compare the figures with Expected (plan usage or money spent is shown).
items.needs: a signed-in account on a paid plan (the popover hides plan usage heading for free plans)
items.note: Marked done in the audit. The popover is in CodeComposer.tsx (around lines 1562 and 1620), backed by useManagedUsageSummary.

items.where: Code > open a cloud session > "Changes" panel > "Create pull request"; then the pull-request area shows status
steps: Open a session that has a repository and a working branch.
Open the "Changes" panel and click "Create pull request".
Wait for "Opening the pull request" to finish, then look for the pull request state (Merged, Closed without merging, Checks passing, Checks failing, Checks running).
Compare the number, link and state with Expected (session's pull request is shown).
items.needs: a repository, a working branch and a GitHub connection; the feature is gated by the deployment (see the plan's switch-on note)
items.note: On the desktop, the pull request form is in LocalPullRequest.tsx with "Push and open a pull request" and "Create branch and open pull request" (local-code.ts). The pull request number/link display was not fully traced.

items.where: Code > open a cloud session > "Session actions" icon menu > "Share" > dialog "Share session" > "Who can open this session" (Private, Team, Public) > "Done"
steps: Open a cloud session.
Click the session actions button (accessible name "Session actions"), then click "Share".
In the "Share session" dialog, pick "Team" or "Public" under "Who can open this session".
Copy the link from the "Session link" field (copy button under the link).
Open the link in a private window signed in as another account and check that the session opens (the shared page is at /code/shared/[token]).
Compare with Expected (the other person can open it).
items.needs: a second account in the same workspace for Team, or any second signed-in account for Public
items.note: The share dialog is CodeShareDialog.tsx and the shared view is SharedCodeSessionPage.tsx; the shared-page route is apps/web/app/code/shared/[token]/page.tsx. Shared viewers see a snapshot, as copy in code-surface.ts says.

items.where: Model name button in the composer footer > All models, then look at row tags and the "Leaving" note
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer, then click All models.
Look at each row's tags for Preview, Experimental, Beta or Alpha, and for Coming soon.
Look for grey text "Leaving <date>" under a row name. It appears only within 30 days before retirement.
Try to pick a "Coming soon" model and check it does not start, as Expected says pickers exclude or label such models.
items.needs: none (a model in its last 30 days before retirement may not exist)
items.note: Models past their retirement date are dropped from the picker. The code comment at apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFooter.tsx (around line 312) says so.

items.where: Open the /operator page (platform admin account only), then click the tab labelled Routes (the tab text is lowercase "routes" and is shown capitalised). The heading on the panel reads Routes.
steps: Sign in with a platform admin account and go to /operator.
Click the Routes tab.
Read the heading Routes and the line below it, which says every route the registry declares is listed with what it costs.
Click a route row to expand it.
Look for the detail labels Cache class and Data retention on the expanded row, and compare with Expected (cache class and data retention per provider route).
items.needs: a platform admin account (not a normal Free or paid account)
items.note: The registry data is shown only in the admin Routes panel; the per-route price is described in the panel intro text but I did not confirm a price column. The routing ranking part of Expected (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1099 zero-retention filter and :1169 cache-affinity ranking) has no visible control and is inner behaviour, so a tester cannot see it from the UI. Composer catalogue at ComposerFooter.tsx:1571 is a model picker, not a route display, and was not used.

items.where: Settings > Skills: a plan that is denied Skills shows the notice there
steps: Open Settings and click Skills.
If the account's plan does not include Skills, read the notice title and text.
Compare with Expected: one decision drives the Skills and Plugins panes and the notice explains the denial.
items.needs: a Free account (if the plan blocks Skills)
items.note: The resolver itself is packages/contracts/types/src/capability-handshake/evaluator.ts and packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/Capabilities.tsx; whether Skills is blocked for Free was not verified.

items.where: Composer bottom bar: model name button > Models, then pick a different model
steps: Open a new chat.
Look at the bottom bar of the composer and note whether a Reasoning effort button is there.
Click the model name button and choose a different model from the Models list.
Look at the bottom bar again: the Reasoning effort button should appear, change or disappear according to Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: In code only the effort control changes with the model; the + menu attachment rows do not.

items.where: Composer: + button (Add attachments and tools) > Add photos & files, then the model name button > a model that cannot read the file
steps: Click the + button (Add attachments and tools) and choose Add photos & files; add a PDF or a photo.
Click the model name button and choose a model that cannot read that file type.
Look above the composer for the alert.
Compare with Expected: the alert names the file kind the selected model cannot read.
items.needs: a file to upload (PDF or image) and a model that cannot read it

labels.text: The selected model can't read the attached document.

items.note: The file picker accept list is the same for every model (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/chat-attachments.ts, chatAttachmentAcceptAttribute); the model-dependent part is the alert.

items.where: Composer bottom bar: Reasoning effort button
steps: Choose a model and click the Reasoning effort button.
Read the levels offered in the panel.
Choose another model, open the panel again and check that only its levels are offered.
On a model where Off is not supported, read the note under the panel.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Off is not supported by this model

items.note: Removing unsupported levels before sending happens on the server (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts) and is not visible on screen.

items.where: Composer: + button (Add attachments and tools) > Create video, then the video setting buttons in the composer
steps: Use a paid account (Free has no video row).
Click the + button (Add attachments and tools) and choose Create video.
Click the length, quality (Select video quality) and aspect ratio buttons and note the options.
Switch to another video model and compare which buttons and options appear, per Expected.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: Each video setting button shows only when the model has more than one option for it (ChatComposerNew.tsx); the accessible names are shown, the buttons display the current value.

items.where: Composer bottom bar: model name button > Models list, locked rows
steps: Sign in with a Free account and open the model picker.
Look for rows with a lock badge: a plan name followed by and above, or Upgrade to use.
Click a locked row and check that it does not switch to that model.
Compare with Expected: plan checks apply to the model here and again on the server.
items.needs: a Free account (a paid plan sees fewer locks)
items.note: The server check per route was not exercised from the UI; only the picker's visible lock is covered here.

items.where: Settings > Usage
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Read the This month card and the Plan usage limits card (on Free it reads Upgrade for higher capacity).
Read the remaining figures, which show as a percentage left or None left.
Send a chat message, click Refresh usage data (if shown), and check that the figure moved.
items.needs: a paid or Free account (Free shows only the upgrade card)

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Policy
steps: Open Settings and click Workspace.
Click Workspace administration.
Click Policy in the console menu.
Read the Workspace policy card. An owner or admin sees editable controls; a member reads Only an owner or admin can change these. You are a (role).
Compare with Expected: the rules (for example Zero data retention only) apply to member chats.
items.needs: a member of a workspace (an owner or admin account to edit)
items.note: Enforcement on chat and other surfaces is server-side (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts) and not visible as a control.

items.where: Settings > Workspace
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin of a workspace and open Settings > Workspace; note the Invite teammate card and the Change role and Remove member actions.
Sign out and sign in as a plain member of the same workspace.
Open Settings > Workspace again.
Compare with Expected: those admin controls are missing for the member, and the server refuses such requests.
items.needs: two accounts in the same workspace: an owner or admin, and a plain member
items.note: The SSO panel is also admin-only (TeamSection.tsx); the server refusal is in apps/web/app/api/settings/team/route.ts.

items.where: Settings > Privacy > Only use AI providers based in the US
steps: Open Settings and click Privacy.
Find the switch Only use AI providers based in the US and turn it on.
Read the line Only US-based providers serve your chats. Models without one are unavailable.
Open the model picker in a new chat and check which models are unavailable, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: an account for which the switch is enabled (eligibility was not verified)

labels.text: Only use AI providers based in the US

items.note: Which accounts can use the switch was not confirmed.

items.where: Sign-up (new account) or sign-in to an account with no age decision > Confirm your age step
steps: Create a new account, or sign in to an account that has no age decision yet.
On Confirm your age, type an age under 18 in Your age and press Continue.
Read the screen This account can't be used with the text You must be at least 18 years old to continue.
Type 18 or more on another try and compare with Expected: adults continue.
items.needs: a new account or one without an age decision; a test age under 18
items.note: The quoted lines in RecordTermsAcceptance.tsx and identity/client.ts no longer hold the age check; it now lives in AgeConfirmationStep.tsx.

items.where: Plugins catalogue (/plugins) > open a plugin > Required connectors
steps: Sign in and open /plugins.
Open a plugin that lists required connectors.
Read the Required connectors list: connected rows show Connected, others show Connect.
Compare with Expected: a missing connection is named and marked with Connect.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one required connector not connected
items.note: If connections cannot be read, the page shows a notice saying it shows what the pack needs instead.

items.where: Code (sidebar) > More > Work with local code; a cloud session row menu > Open in > Desktop app
steps: Click Code in the app and click More in the rail.
Read Work with local code: with a paired desktop it names the desktop; without one it links to the download page.
Hover the item to read the status (for example is online, is asleep, is offline).
Compare with Expected: the status shows before you rely on the desktop.
items.needs: none to see the no-desktop case; a paired desktop app to see its status
items.note: The status text appears as a tooltip and screen-reader text, not as a visible label; the status wording comes from apps/web/features/desktop-host/hooks/use-paired-desktop.ts.

items.where: Code (sidebar) > the cloud session area: notice above the composer
steps: Click Code in the app.
With a Free plan, read the notice Your plan does not include managed environments. and the Upgrade button.
If the deployment has managed environments off, the notice reads Managed environments are not enabled on this deployment.
Compare with Expected: the feature is gated and the create action is not offered.
items.needs: a Free account (to see the plan notice)

labels.text: Your plan does not include managed environments.

items.note: Whether the create action is disabled was read from CloudCodePage.tsx (canCreate), not clicked.

items.where: Composer bottom bar: model name button > Models > All models
steps: Open the model picker and click All models.
Look for rows marked Temporarily unavailable.
Look for rows marked Not available in this app.
Compare with Expected: the two states read differently; a row can only show one.
items.needs: none (to see the unavailable state, a model that is temporarily down is needed)
items.note: Whether a model is temporarily down at a given time cannot be predicted from code.

items.where: Composer bottom bar: model name button, then compare two models
steps: Choose a model and look at the bottom bar for a Reasoning effort button.
Choose a model without that control and check the button is gone, not greyed out.
Open the + menu (Add attachments and tools) and check Create image appears only if your plan allows it.
Compare with Expected: irrelevant controls are hidden.
items.needs: none (to see a model without the effort control, try a few models)
items.note: Which models lack the effort control is not listed in code; the tester has to find one.

items.where: Composer: + button (Add attachments and tools) > Deep Research (dimmed); model picker rows with badges
steps: With a Free account, click the + button (Add attachments and tools).
Check that the Deep Research row is dimmed.
Hover the Deep Research row and read the reason.
Open the model picker and compare the dimmed rows and badges (Coming soon, Beta) with Expected.
items.needs: a Free account

items.where: Composer: + button (Add attachments and tools) > Deep Research, and the model picker's locked rows
steps: With a Free account, click the + button (Add attachments and tools).
Hover Deep Research and read Upgrade to use Deep Research.
Open the model picker and read the locked row badge, which names the plan (and above).
Compare with Expected: the text names which plan unlocks it and how to upgrade.
items.needs: a Free account

labels.text: Upgrade your plan to use it.

items.note: The Not on your plan wording shows in a settings panel (Skills or Plugins) when that pane is denied, not in the composer.

items.where: Plugins catalogue (/plugins) > open a plugin > Required connectors > Connect
steps: Open a plugin that lists required connectors while signed in.
Find a connector that shows Connect.
Click Connect (it links to the connectors page) and connect it.
Return to the plugin page and check the row now shows Connected.
items.needs: a signed-in account and an outside account for that connector (the connector's own sign-in)
items.note: The row names the connector only; whether it names the account to connect was not confirmed.

items.needs: a microphone
items.note: Searched apps/web for microphone and permission copy (use-dictation.ts, VoiceSection.tsx, rg across features, lib and app); found only The microphone could not be started. Try again. and Settings > Voice > Dictation text Speak into the composer with the microphone button. No explanation before the browser prompt was found; the Tool approvals menu in ComposerPlusMenu.tsx was not read for it.

items.where: Composer: add a file, then model name button > a model that cannot read it; alert above the composer
steps: Add a PDF or photo with + (Add photos & files).
Choose a model that cannot read that file from the model name button.
Read the alert: it names the file kind and says to switch to Auto or choose a model that can read it.
Click Choose a compatible model to see the models that can read it, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: a file to upload and a model that cannot read it

labels.text: The selected model can't read the attached document.

items.where: Code (sidebar) > More > Work with local code; a cloud session row menu > Open in > Desktop app
steps: Click Code in the app and click More.
Click Work with local code: with a paired desktop it opens the desktop; without one it goes to the download page.
Open a cloud session's menu, go to Open in, and click Desktop app.
Compare with Expected: the work continues on the other device or app.
items.needs: a paired desktop app to see the continue action (without one, the download page)
items.note: The device bridge contract is packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/host-bridge.ts (no screen of its own).

items.where: Composer: add a file, then model name button > a model that cannot read it; alert offers Remove attachments and Choose a compatible model
steps: Add a file with + (Add photos & files).
Switch to a model that cannot read it.
In the alert, click Choose a compatible model and pick a model that can read the file (this keeps the file).
Or click Remove attachments (this removes it). Compare with Expected: the user chooses to keep or remove.
items.needs: a file to upload and a model that cannot read it
items.note: If no model on the plan can read the file, the list says so and may offer a plan upgrade.

items.where: Composer bottom bar: Reasoning effort button > panel
steps: Choose a model with a reasoning control and click Reasoning effort.
Try to turn thinking off on a model that does not support Off.
Read the note Off is not supported by this model. Using (the level it will use).
Send a message and check that the chat still works, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: none (a model where Off is unsupported is needed)

labels.text: Off is not supported by this model

items.note: Removing unsupported parameters before sending is server-side (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts) and not visible.

items.where: Settings > Billing (change plan), then return to the chat tab; check the model picker and + menu
steps: Note the locked model rows and the Deep Research row in the composer.
Change the plan in Settings > Billing (Checkout or the billing portal).
Return to the app tab without reloading or restarting.
Reopen the model picker and the + menu and compare the locks and Deep Research row with Expected.
items.needs: a test account that can change plan
items.note: Billing data refetches on window focus (apps/web/features/billing/hooks/use-billing-queries.ts); the refresh path for the capability decisions was not traced.

items.where: Composer model button (the selected model name, e.g. under the message box) > top row "Auto"
steps: Sign in with a paid account.
Click the model name button at the bottom of the message box (its accessible name ends in "Change model").
Find the row labelled "Auto" with the text "Picks the best model for each message" and click it.
Send a short message and an image-free question, then look at the answer: it should come from a model chosen by Auto, not a fixed one.
items.needs: a paid account (Free accounts see "Auto (free) · community models, capacity varies" instead)

labels.text: Picks the best model for each message

items.note: Auto row is shown only on paid plans; the choice is visible only as the answer's model, no per-answer model name was found.

items.where: Composer model button > model rows below "Auto" (under "Recommended" or the model list)
steps: Sign in with a paid account.
Click the model name button at the bottom of the message box.
Click any model row other than "Auto", for example one listed under "Recommended".
Send a message and check that the model name shown in the composer button is the one you picked.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: Model names are read from the catalogue at runtime, so no fixed model name is written in the code.

items.where: Projects > open a project > the More (···) button > project settings, then the "Default model" field
steps: Open Projects from the left sidebar and open a project.
Click the More (···) button at the top of the project and open its settings.
Find the "Default model" field and pick a model from the dropdown.
Save, open a new chat in that project and check the composer shows the chosen model.
items.needs: a paid account, a project

labels.text: No default, use the model you last picked

items.note: The exact name of the settings item in the More menu was not confirmed in the code.

items.where: Composer model button > "Auto" row, then the profile rows "Instant", "Best", "Economy" below it
steps: Sign in with a paid account.
Click the model name button at the bottom of the message box.
Click "Instant", "Best" or "Economy" under the "Auto" row.
Send a question about coding or reasoning and compare the answer's model with what the row said.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: No visible row mentions coding or reasoning; the Expected example (premium for coding) is not stated on screen.

items.where: Composer model button > "Instant" row (under "Auto")
steps: Sign in with a paid account.
Click the model name button at the bottom of the message box.
Click the row "Instant" with the text "Answers fastest, on the quickest models your plan includes."
Send a short question and check the answer arrives quickly and the composer shows a fast model.
items.needs: a paid account

labels.text: Answers fastest, on the quickest models your plan includes.

items.where: Composer model button > "Best" row (under "Auto")
steps: Sign in with a paid account.
Click the model name button at the bottom of the message box.
Click the row "Best" with the text "The most capable model your plan includes, for harder work."
Send a hard question and check the composer shows the most capable model for your plan.
items.needs: a paid account

labels.text: The most capable model your plan includes, for harder work.

items.where: Composer model button > "Economy" row (under "Auto")
steps: Sign in with a paid account.
Click the model name button at the bottom of the message box.
Click the row "Economy" with the text "The lowest-cost model that can handle the task."
Send a simple question and check the composer shows a low-cost model.
items.needs: a paid account

labels.text: The lowest-cost model that can handle the task.

items.where: Settings > Workspace policy > "Zero data retention only"
steps: Open Settings and go to Workspace policy (organization admin access is needed to change it).
Find the row "Zero data retention only".
Turn on the toggle and save.
Send a request and check that it is refused rather than sent to a provider without zero data retention.
items.needs: an organization admin account
items.note: The Settings menu item that opens this section was not confirmed; there is no visible privacy-first routing profile, only this policy toggle.

items.needs: none
items.note: Tool needs are classified on the server (request-processor.ts) with no control of its own.

items.needs: none
items.note: Attached-media routing is internal; the only visible result is the "Choose a compatible model" offer (see S79.21).

items.needs: none
items.note: Complexity classification is internal (packages/ai/routing/src/task-family.ts) with no visible control.

items.needs: none
items.note: Freshness detection is server-side with no visible control; the effect shows only in the answer.

items.needs: none
items.note: Candidate filtering is a server rule; its effect is visible only as which models appear in the picker.

items.needs: none
items.note: Provider route choice is server-side ranking with no control of its own.

items.note: A server rule. Visible sign: a model picked by hand is not replaced; the "Moved to" line (S79.26) appears only for Auto moves.

items.needs: none
items.note: Quota-aware routing is server-side with no control of its own.

items.needs: none
