items.where: Message box > attach a file or image that the selected model cannot read > "Choose a compatible model"
steps: Select a model that cannot read images.
Attach an image to the message box.
Read the warning and click "Choose a compatible model".
Pick a model from the list and check the composer switches to it and the attachment is kept.
items.needs: a file to upload, a model that cannot read it
items.note: This is an offer to switch on a conflict; a switch offer for a better answer (not for attachments) was not found.

items.where: Models (catalogue) > the Compare button (scale icon) on two or more model cards > Compare answers page
steps: Open the models catalogue.
Click the scale icon on two models (its accessible name is "Compare <model name>").
Open the compare answers view and type one prompt in the box "Ask every model the same thing".
Press send and check each model returns its own answer side by side.
items.needs: a paid account (at least two models your plan includes)

labels.text: Ask every model the same thing

items.note: The button that opens the compare page was not confirmed; the scale icon has no visible text.

items.where: A chat answer > the small line "Moved to <model>: <reason>" under the answer (appears only when Auto switched models)
steps: Start a chat with Auto and keep sending messages until Auto moves to another model (it is not forced).
Look at the answer where the model changed.
Read the line under the answer that starts with "Moved to".
Check the reason text matches the reasons listed in the contracts file.
items.needs: a paid account, a long chat or a case where Auto moves

labels.text: the model this chat was already using

items.note: The line appears only after an Auto move, so a tester cannot force it.

items.needs: none
items.note: Only the "Moved to" receipt (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx) was found, and it shows only after a move; no per-answer model name was found.

items.needs: none
items.note: Searched apps/web and packages/ui for routing policy version text: none found; trace code is in packages/ai/routing/src/routing-trace.ts and a service in apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/.

items.needs: none
items.note: Fallback on ambiguous classification is server-side; the visible result is a normal answer.

items.where: Shows only as prices: compare Settings > Billing with the pricing table
steps: Sign in and open Settings > Billing (or the account menu's Upgrade > Compare plans)
Note the plan name and price shown for the current plan
Compare them with the prices in Compare plans
The catalog version number and the version recorded on a subscription are not shown in the UI; mark that part as not visible
items.needs: a paid account, to see a subscription's plan and price
items.note: The version number is not visible in the code paths I read, so only the prices can be checked from the UI.

items.where: Account menu > Upgrade > Compare plans
steps: Open the account menu in the sidebar footer and click Upgrade
Find the Compare plans heading in the dialog
Read the Free column: capabilities and limits listed for Free
Compare the Free column with Expected: the plan's bundle is shown and matches the limits enforced
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: Upgrade opens UpgradePlanDialog, which shows Compare plans. The server-side enforcement of the Free bundle is not visible in the UI.

items.where: Account menu > Upgrade > Compare plans
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Find the Basic column in Compare plans and read its price and limits
Check the Get Basic button is shown with the Basic price
Compare with Expected: priced bundle shown on pricing and in-app
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: The Basic column is built from the billing catalog; I did not find the literal word Basic as a label in the pricing copy I read.

items.where: Account menu > Upgrade > Compare plans
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Find the Pro column in Compare plans
Read its price, limits and feature rows
Compare with Expected: priced bundle shown in pricing and in-app
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: The Pro bundle comes from the billing catalog; I did not find a literal Pro label in the copy I read.

items.where: Account menu > Upgrade > Compare plans
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Find the Max column in Compare plans
Read the price, usage multiplier line and limits
Compare with Expected: priced bundle shown in pricing and in-app
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: The Max 5x name is set in code by the plan tier, and I did not find its exact visible label in the copy I read.

items.where: Account menu > Upgrade > Compare plans
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Find the Max 15x column in Compare plans
Read the price, limits and the Get Max 15x style button
Compare with Expected: priced bundle shown in pricing and in-app
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: The button text is a template filled with the plan name; the exact label is not confirmed.

items.where: Account menu > Upgrade > Compare plans
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Read the usage line under the Max plans: it reads like a multiple of a baseline plan
Find the baseline plan named in that line
Compare with Expected: pricing states what 1x means and its concrete allowance
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: The copy is a template filled at runtime, and I did not confirm the concrete allowance number is shown beside it.

items.where: Settings > Usage
steps: Open Settings and click Usage
Read the bars: the 5-hour and weekly limit bars and the reset line
Find the sentence about 5-hour and weekly limits
Compare with Expected: the copy names which allowance a multiplier scales
items.needs: a paid account, to see plan-scaled limits

labels.text: A reset brings your 5-hour and weekly limits back to full.

items.note: The multiplier copy in Compare plans names the baseline, but I did not confirm that the Usage screen names which allowance a multiplier scales.

items.where: Account menu > Upgrade > Compare plans
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Scroll the Compare plans table through its feature rows
Compare a Free column cell with a Pro column cell for a feature such as Cloud API access
Compare with Expected: plans differ in feature access and the rows are listed
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: The gate is enforced on the server; the UI only shows the table.

items.where: Account menu > Upgrade > Compare plans (storage line), then Projects > a project's knowledge files
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Read the storage wording in the plan columns (for example the phrase of storage)
Go to a project and try to add a knowledge file
Compare with Expected: each plan's storage limit is stated and enforced when files are added
items.needs: a Free account and a Pro or higher account to compare
items.note: The Projects path to add a knowledge file is not confirmed from the files I read; the storage limit wording is in the pricing copy.

items.where: Account menu > Upgrade > Compare plans (context row)
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Find the context row in Compare plans
Read the line Up to a number of tokens for each plan
Compare with Expected: each plan states its own context limit
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: The per-request enforcement is not visible in the UI.

items.where: Account menu > Upgrade > Compare plans (concurrency line)
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Find the line about chats at once in the Max 15x copy
Compare the number of simultaneous chats per plan
Compare with Expected: each plan states its own simultaneous-response limit
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: The concurrency rows in the pricing page are built in code; I did not confirm a visible row for every plan.

items.where: Composer footer > Reasoning (effort chips in the model menu)
steps: Sign in and open a new chat
In the composer footer, open the model or Reasoning control
Look at the effort marks offered for the chosen model
Click a gated effort mark and look for the Upgrade label, then compare with Expected
items.needs: a Free account and a paid account to compare
items.note: The exact flyout and the manual model choice control were not confirmed from the lines I read; the server clamp is not visible.

items.where: Settings > Usage (flagship weekly bar)
steps: Open Settings and click Usage
Find the separate weekly bar for the most capable models
Read its percent and reset time
Compare with Expected: a model-class cap is shown to the user
items.needs: a paid account, since the flagship bar shows only when the plan has one

labels.text: On {{baseline}} and higher plans, the most capable models can use up to {{percent}}% of each week's credits.

items.note: The bar label comes from a bucket helper and I did not confirm its visible words.

items.needs: a Team account, with a second member in the same workspace
items.note: I did not find any visible word saying whether usage is pooled or dedicated. The owner decision is recorded as open in the plan file, so it may not be shown.

items.where: Account menu > Upgrade > Compare plans, then the Monthly and Annual toggle (Team section)
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Find the Monthly and Annual buttons for the Team billing cadence
Click Annual and read the saving and billed-yearly text
Click Monthly and compare the price change with Expected
items.needs: a Free account to see the toggle; checkout needs a plan that offers both cadences
items.note: The toggle I found is for the Team cadence. I did not locate a separate individual monthly or annual toggle, and I did not confirm the checkout cadence.

items.where: Settings > Billing (plan row shows Free trial and Trial ends on)
steps: Sign in with an account that has a granted trial and open Settings > Billing
Read the plan status: Free trial
Read the date row labelled Trial ends on
Compare with Expected: the trial is shown as a trial and the end date is visible
items.needs: a trial account granted by the owner
items.note: What happens when the trial ends (revert or bill) is handled on the server and not visible on this screen.

items.where: Account menu > Upgrade > pick a plan > promotion code field > Apply
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Pick a plan so the checkout panel opens
Type a promotion code into the promotion field and click Apply
Read the applied discount line and compare with Expected
items.needs: a Free account and a valid promotion code
items.note: The button text on the promotion field is not confirmed from the file that holds it; bonus credits and invite grants are not visible from this path.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Buy credits
steps: Open Settings and click Usage
Click Buy credits
Choose a credit pack or enter an amount, and read the quote before paying
Compare with Expected: purchased credits appear as a separate balance from the plan allowance
items.needs: a paid account, because the top-up flow may be limited by plan
items.note: The Free plan top-up prompt shows Compare plans instead, so gating may apply; do not complete a real purchase without the owner.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Keep going after a usage limit (switch)
steps: Open Settings and click Billing
Scroll to the section Keep going after a usage limit
Confirm the switch is off by default and read the sentence Spend your credits when a usage limit stops you
Turn the switch on and check the available credits line, then compare with Expected
items.needs: a paid account with purchased credits

labels.text: Keep going after a usage limit

items.note: The switch appears only under some conditions I did not confirm; accounting in separate plan windows is not visible.

items.where: Settings > Billing shows the plan and price a subscriber bought
steps: Sign in with an account on a retired plan, if one exists
Open Settings > Billing and read the plan and price
Compare with the current price on Compare plans, and confirm the old price stays
items.needs: an account on a retired plan or price, which a new QA account will not have
items.note: The grandfather rule is applied on the server; there is no screen that names it.

items.where: Account menu > Upgrade > pick a paid plan > Upgrade (confirm dialog)
steps: Open the account menu, click Upgrade and pick a paid plan
Click the Upgrade button to open the confirm dialog
Read the first charge or Renews line and the price before confirming
Stop before any final confirm button, and compare with Expected: the time it takes effect and the renewal date are shown
items.needs: a Free account; do not finish the purchase without the owner
items.note: The phrase immediately was not found in the confirm dialog text I read.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Switch to a smaller plan
steps: Sign in with a paid account and open Settings > Billing
Start a plan change to a smaller plan
Read the dialog title Switch to a smaller plan or Switch to a plan name
Read the sentence that says the new plan starts at the end of the current billing period and nothing is charged today; compare with Expected
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: The button that opens this dialog was not confirmed from BillingSection; I found only the dialog title and copy.

items.where: Settings > Billing (notice shown after a failed renewal)
steps: Use a paid account whose renewal payment failed (needs the owner's test setup)
Open Settings > Billing and read the notice that says the last payment did not go through
Read the line about grace and the Update payment method button
Compare with Expected: the grace rule and the access that remains are stated
items.needs: a paid account with a failed renewal, which needs the owner's test setup
items.note: The code states there is no grace period: paid features stop at the first failed renewal. Expected says a grace rule applies, so the wording differs.

items.where: Account menu > Upgrade > Compare plans (Cloud API access row)
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Find the row Cloud API access in Compare plans
Read which plans show it as included and which show it as not included
Compare with Expected: API use is a plan capability and API calls are gated by it
items.needs: a Free account and a Pro account to compare
items.note: The gate on API calls is enforced server-side and is not visible in the UI.

items.where: No control of its own. Sign in to the same account on the web app and on another signed-in surface, then open Settings > Billing on each and compare the plan name.
steps: Sign in to the AGI web app with an account that has a paid plan.
Open Settings > Billing and note the plan name shown in the plan line.
Sign in to the same account on another surface (for example the desktop app or the mobile app).
Open the same Billing screen on that surface and compare the plan name and the features it allows with the web app. Expected: the same plan on both.
items.needs: a paid account, plus a second signed-in surface for the same account
items.note: The entitlement is resolved server-side in apps/web/lib/services/entitlement-resolution.ts and the per-surface policy is in apps/web/lib/free-chat-surface-policy.ts; both are inner logic. The line numbers cited in the plan (BillingSection.tsx:671) are stale: the quoted text is not in the file now. The Billing label is shown on the Settings screen in both apps, so the check uses the Billing screen only as a visible comparison point; I did not confirm that the desktop and mobile apps expose the same Billing label.

items.where: Account menu > Upgrade (opens /upgrade, which shows each plan with a "What changes" list). Settings > Billing also has "Compare plans" and "Upgrade plan" (or "Adjust plan" for a paid plan) buttons that lead to the same plan pages.
steps: Sign in with a Free account and open the account menu.
Click Upgrade.
On the upgrade page, read the plan card marked Recommended and its "What changes" list. Each item should say what that plan adds over the current plan.
Click the Continue with button on a plan card and check that its page explains that plan's own features. Expected: each plan explains what it adds and what blocked features need it.
items.needs: a Free account (a paid account would see Adjust plan instead of Upgrade plan)
items.note: Cited line numbers are stale: quoted text is not found at apps/web/app/pricing/page.tsx:1170, apps/web/features/billing/lib/plan-display.ts:36 or apps/web/app/api/media/image/generate/route.ts:223. The blocked-feature reason text ("That capability is not included in your current plan.") is defined in packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:920, but I did not confirm which screen shows it to a person. The public /pricing page exists (apps/web/app/pricing/page.tsx) and may also explain plans; I did not verify its visible labels. The Upgrade label is a translation key (common:navUpgrade) and the account-menu trigger that opens it was not confirmed.

items.where: Settings > Billing (top plan card)
steps: Sign in and click the Settings command: open the command palette and choose Settings, or use the Settings entry in the app menu.
In the settings list, click Billing.
Look at the plan card at the top: it shows Free plan, or the plan name followed by the word plan.
Compare the name with the plan on the Usage page and the account you expect.
items.needs: none (works on a Free account)
items.note: The settings entry point was not traced beyond the command palette item Settings.

items.where: Settings > Billing (plan card and rows below it)
steps: Open Settings and click Billing.
Look for a row labelled Renews on, Ends on, Current period ends or Trial ends on.
Read the date shown beside that row.
Compare the date with the renewal or end date you expect.
items.needs: a paid account (the row shows only when a subscription has a period end)
items.note: On a Free account no period row is expected; this was read from the code, not run.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Plan usage limits (bars)
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled Plan usage limits.
Look at the bars: Current session, This week, Most capable models (when shown) and This billing period.
Compare the bar fill and the percent with what you expect from the plan allowance.
items.needs: a paid account (a Free account sees only Upgrade for higher capacity)
items.note: The overall meter is the This billing period bar; the Free account shows a waitlist/upgrade card instead.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went > By model
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to the card titled Where your usage went.
Look at the table captioned By model.
Compare the per-model rows with the usage you made in each model.
items.needs: a paid account (the history card is hidden on Free)
items.note: The flagship cap is the Most capable models bar in Plan usage limits; per-model spend is the By model table.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went > By product area
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to Where your usage went and find the table captioned By product area.
Read the rows labelled Chat, AGI Work, Deep Research, AGI Code and Browser.
Compare the amounts with the activity you did in each area.
items.needs: a paid account with some settled usage
items.note: The history shows settled usage only; recent requests appear after they settle.

items.where: Settings > Usage > This month (row Voice) and Plan usage limits (row Voice)
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled This month and look for the row labelled Voice.
Read the minutes used and any monthly cap text beside it.
Also find the Voice line in Plan usage limits and compare the estimate of minutes left.
items.needs: a paid account with voice use
items.note: The Voice row appears only when the plan has a voice allowance.

items.where: Settings > Usage > This month (row Images)
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled This month.
Look for the row labelled Images, which shows the image count and credits.
Compare the count with the images you generated.
items.needs: a paid account that has made at least one image request
items.note: The Images row appears only after the account has an image request.

items.where: Settings > Usage > This month (row Video)
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled This month.
Look for the row labelled Video, which shows seconds used.
Compare the seconds with the video you generated.
items.needs: a paid account with a video allowance and some video use
items.note: Whether the Video row always appears was not confirmed from the code path.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went > By product area (row Deep Research)
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to Where your usage went and open the By product area table.
Find the row labelled Deep Research.
Compare its credits and requests with the Deep Research runs you made.
items.needs: a paid account that has run Deep Research
items.note: Research is a product-area row, not a separate chart.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went > By product area (rows AGI Code and AGI Work)
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to Where your usage went and open the By product area table.
Find the rows labelled AGI Code and AGI Work.
Compare them with the coding and agent work you did.
items.needs: a paid account that has used AGI Code or AGI Work
items.note: Coding and agentic work are split into two product-area rows; the task cost view is a separate item.

items.where: Sidebar > Library (heading line)
steps: Click Library in the sidebar.
Read the line under the Library heading.
It shows the file storage used against the storage limit, or the used amount alone when no limit is known.
Compare the numbers with the files you uploaded.
items.needs: a file to upload (to see storage move)
items.note: The storage line appears only after the storage numbers load.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Plan usage limits (row Responses running now)
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled Plan usage limits.
Look for the row labelled Responses running now.
Start a long response in chat and refresh the Usage page to see the count change.
items.needs: a paid account; a running response helps show a non-zero count
items.note: The row reads active of limit at a time; the counter is only refreshed on reload.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Credit balances and Plan usage limits
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled Credit balances and read the rows Bonus credits and Purchased credits.
Find the card titled Plan usage limits and read the bars.
Compare the remaining amounts with the balance you expect.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: The Credit balances card is hidden for Free and contract-priced accounts.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Credit balances (rows Purchased credits and Bonus credits)
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled Credit balances.
Read the row Purchased credits (bought credits) and the row Bonus credits (promotional or referral credits).
Compare the included monthly allowance in Plan usage limits with these two rows.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: The plan allowance is shown as a plan line and bars, not as its own row.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Credit balances (row Bonus credits)
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled Credit balances.
Read the row Bonus credits: the amount remaining and the line Next expiry with the date.
Compare the amount and date with the promotional or referral credit you were given.
items.needs: an account that has a promotional or referral credit
items.note: When there is no bonus balance the row shows None with a note about referrals and promotions.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Credit balances (Next expiry and Purchased credits don't expire) and the reset lines
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
In Credit balances, read Next expiry under Bonus credits.
Read the note under Purchased credits.
In Plan usage limits, read the Resets in and reset date text on each bar.
items.needs: a paid account, and a bonus credit to see an expiry date
items.note: Plan allowance reset and bonus lapse dates appear on their own rows; the purchased balance note is fixed text.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Plan usage limits (reset text on each bar)
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled Plan usage limits.
Read the reset text on a bar, such as Resets in followed by minutes or hours and a date.
Wait a minute and check that the countdown moved.
items.needs: a paid account with a bar that is not full
items.note: The countdown is refreshed about every minute by the page.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went (Days, Weeks, Months)
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to Where your usage went.
Open the period choice and pick Days, Weeks or Months.
Compare the rows with the period you picked and the UTC note under the heading.
items.needs: a paid account with settled usage
items.note: History is grouped in UTC, as the note under the heading says.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went > By project
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to Where your usage went.
Find the table captioned By project.
Compare each project row with the work you did in that project.
items.needs: a paid account with settled usage in a project
items.note: A row with no project name reads Project not in this workspace.

items.where: Work history (page title Work history, from the command palette)
steps: Open the command palette and choose Work history.
Pick an agent task from the list.
Look at each row: a cost appears after the time when the run has a cost.
Compare the cost with the Cost and usage section of the task.
items.needs: an account that has run at least one agent task
items.note: The command palette entry is Work history in apps/web/shared/components/CommandPalette/CommandPalette.tsx; the palette shortcut and any other link to the page were not traced.

items.where: Chat composer > + menu > Deep Research (estimate appears in the research activity)
steps: Open a new chat and click the + button in the composer.
Choose Deep Research.
Send a research question and look at the research activity for the text up to ~ with a credit amount.
Compare that estimate with the actual cost in Work history.
items.needs: a paid account (estimate shown for Deep Research); for video, switch to video mode to see the video cost estimate
items.note: Whether the estimate shows before the first step was not verified in the code path; the video estimate is a separate component.

items.where: Work history > open a task > Cost and usage
steps: Open the command palette and choose Work history.
Click a finished task.
Find the section titled Cost and usage.
Read the cost and the token and model call line, and compare with what you expect.
items.needs: an account with a finished agent task
items.note: On a free trial run the section says the run was metered against the free trial allowance instead of charged.

items.where: Sidebar footer usage bar (above the mode pill)
steps: Look at the bottom of the sidebar for the thin usage bar.
Hover it to see the title text, for example 80% of token budget used.
Check the bar colour: it changes at 80% and 95%.
Compare the percent with the Usage page bars.
items.needs: a paid account near a limit (the widget is hidden on Free)
items.note: The composer banner for warnings was not traced to its visible wording; only the sidebar text was confirmed.

items.where: Chat composer, the banner above the text box after a limit is reached
steps: Open a chat and send messages until a limit is reached, or use an account already at its limit.
Try to send a new message.
Look at the warning banner above the composer: it names the limit and the reset time.
Check that Notify me when it resets and the Upgrade or Use action are shown.
items.needs: an account at a usage or free limit

labels.text: Free usage limit reached. Upgrade to continue.

items.note: The composer banner for plan limits is data-driven; the exact limit text comes from the account response.

items.where: Chat composer banner at a limit > Switch to (or Use) an eligible model
steps: Reach the blocked state described in the item above.
Look for a button in the banner or the inline paywall card that names another model, such as Switch to.
Click it and confirm the model in the chat header or composer changes.
Send a message and check that it is answered.
items.needs: an account at a limit where another eligible model exists
items.note: The composer action uses the Use name wording from apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx; only Switch to was confirmed as visible text.

items.where: In chat, send a message after a free-plan capacity limit is hit, so the limit card appears. The card's "Try again" button stays disabled with a countdown ("Try again in ...") until the retry time passes. The reset line under the card's text shows when the limit resets.
steps: Reach a free-plan capacity limit in chat (or wait for a "No free capacity right now" card).
Look at the card's main button: it reads "Try again" and is disabled with a countdown.
Read the reset sentence under the card text, if one is shown.
Look at the second button "Try later" and the "Upgrade to ..." button, and compare with the Expected: waiting for the reset is offered as an alternative to paying.
items.needs: a Free account that can reach a limit, or a limit-state test account
items.note: The countdown button applies to free-capacity cards only; the rolling-window and billing-period limit cards show a reset-time line and "Try later" or "Not now" instead. The plan's old code line 345 is now line 345 for the countdown and 362 for "Try later".

items.where: Chat: at a limit, the limit card shows a "Buy credits" button when the account is a paid self-serve plan billed through Stripe, Apple or Google. Also Settings > Billing > "Buy credits" panel (the "Buy $..." button starts checkout).
steps: Sign in to a paid self-serve account and reach a usage limit in chat (or open Settings > Billing).
In the limit card, look for the "Buy credits" button.
Or open Settings > Billing and find the "Buy credits" section, pick an amount, and read the "Buy $..." button.
Compare with Expected: the user can buy extra usage from where they hit the limit. Stop before paying.
items.needs: a paid account billed through Stripe, Apple or Google; a Free account sees only the upgrade paths
items.note: The "Buy credits" button on the limit card appears only when the server recovery action is top_up; otherwise the card shows "Upgrade to ..." instead.

items.where: Settings > Billing, then scroll to the "Auto-reload" section below the "Buy credits" panel.
steps: Open Settings, then the "Billing" tab.
Scroll to the "Auto-reload" heading.
Turn on the switch next to it (a confirm dialog asks "Turn on auto-reload?").
Set "When my balance falls below" and "Reload with", then press "Save auto-reload" and compare with Expected: you can turn on and configure automatic credit reload.
items.needs: a paid account billed through Stripe with a saved card (the panel shows "Add a payment method" if no card is on file)
items.note: The panel is shown only when the account can buy top-ups and the billing source is Stripe; the "Billing" tab label comes from packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/settings.json (nav.billing).

items.where: Workspace console > "Usage" (sidebar item under the workspace console, page title "Usage"), then the "Monthly spend limit" block at the top of the analytics.
steps: Sign in as a workspace owner and open the workspace console.
Click "Usage" in the console sidebar.
Find the "Monthly spend limit" block.
Set "Alert at" and the action ("Notify" or "Block"), then press "Set limit" (or "Update limit" if one exists).
Compare with Expected: managed usage stops at the cap for "Block"; "Remove limit" removes the cap after a confirm dialog.
items.needs: a workspace owner account
items.note: The console group heading above "Usage" was not checked; the sidebar label "Usage" is at WorkspaceConsoleNav.tsx line 132. The workspace owner-only access rule was not verified in the page code.

items.where: Settings > Usage, then the "Download CSV" link under the usage history.
steps: Open Settings, then the "Usage" tab.
Wait until the usage history has loaded.
Click "Download CSV" below the history.
Open the downloaded file and compare with Expected: a usage report file is saved.
items.needs: a paid account with usage history (the Free account QA run showed only paid-plan waitlist text on Usage)
items.note: The "Download CSV" link only renders once the history is shown (the shown && guard); the link points to /api/usage/export with a granularity parameter.

items.where: Settings > Usage, then the "Report a billing problem" button under the usage history.
steps: Open Settings, then the "Usage" tab.
Wait until the usage history has loaded.
Click "Report a billing problem".
Choose the period in the form, optionally add a note, and press "File report".
Compare with Expected: a confirmation reads "Report filed as ..." with the usage record attached.
items.needs: a paid account with usage history (the Free account QA run showed only paid-plan waitlist text on Usage)
items.note: The form uses the period dropdown option "Everything shown" by default; no alternative period label was checked beyond the code.

items.where: Pricing > Compare plans
steps: Open the Pricing page (/pricing), or the plans page reached from Settings > Billing.
Scroll to the section headed "Compare plans".
Read the columns "Plan", "Price", "Billing" and "Usage capacity" and the rows for usage, models, admin and data.
Compare the plans shown with what the Expected line asks for: price, usage and features before choosing.
items.needs: none
items.note: The comparison is a section of the page, not a dialog; the file has no S83.19 or S83.25, so 25 items are listed.

items.where: Pricing > Team & Enterprise > Monthly / Annual
steps: Open the Pricing page (/pricing).
Select the "Team & Enterprise" tab.
Click "Annual", then "Monthly" in the toggle beside the seat price.
Look at the price text and the billing line ("billed yearly" or "billed monthly") and compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The toggle appears only on the Team & Enterprise panel, and only when yearly team checkout is available; it is not on the Individual tab.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Upgrade plan
steps: Sign in with a Free account, press ⌘, and choose "Billing".
Click "Upgrade plan".
Choose a paid plan on the "Upgrade" page and read the "Upgrade to" dialog.
Click the confirm button and complete the Stripe checkout page.
Return to Billing and check the plan name and status shown under the Billing heading against Expected.
items.needs: a Free account and a card for the Stripe checkout
items.note: The plan says the owner decision on this item is still open.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Switch to a smaller plan
steps: Press ⌘, and choose "Billing" with a paid Stripe-billed account.
Click "Switch to a smaller plan".
In the dialog, read the "Price", "Usage" and "Limits" sections.
Read the switch date line and the button "Switch on" or "Switch to" and compare with Expected before confirming.
items.needs: a paid account billed through Stripe

items.where: Settings > Billing > Upgrade plan > choose a paid plan
steps: Start from a Free account: press ⌘, and choose "Billing", then click "Upgrade plan".
Read the sentence about starting a new billing period and credit for unused time.
Choose a paid plan and open the confirmation dialog.
Read "Total due today" and the "Renews" line and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Free account

labels.text: Upgrading starts a new billing period today, with credit for unused time on your plan.

items.note: The proration amounts appear only when a paid Stripe charge exists to credit.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Upgrade plan > choose a paid plan
steps: Open "Upgrade plan" from Settings > Billing.
Choose a paid plan and read the order panel.
Look for the "Tax" line and the "Total due today" line.
If the panel says "Tax is calculated at checkout.", note that tax is only added on the Stripe page, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Free account

items.where: Settings > Billing > Upgrade plan > choose a paid plan > Add a promotion code
steps: Open "Upgrade plan" from Settings > Billing and choose a paid plan.
In the confirmation dialog, find the "Promotion code" field.
Click "Add a promotion code" and type a code.
Check the discount line shown below the code, such as "% off", and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Free account and a valid promotion code
items.note: No valid promotion code was found in the code, so the tester needs one from the owner.

items.where: Settings > Billing (status row "Trial ends on" or badge "Free trial")
steps: Open Settings > Billing with an account on a trial.
Read the "Free trial" badge and the "Trial ends on" row.
Read the text under the plan name about the trial end date.
Open "Upgrade plan" and choose a plan with a trial, then read "Your free trial ends on" and the charge after it, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: an account on a trial (or a plan offered with a trial)
items.note: Trial terms appear only when a trial is offered; the code does not show when that happens.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Payment > Add payment method
steps: Press ⌘, and choose "Billing".
Find the "Payment" heading.
If no card is saved, click "Add payment method".
Complete the card form that opens and compare the new card with Expected.
items.needs: a Free or paid account with no saved card
items.note: The button opens the Stripe billing portal, not an in-app card form.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Payment
steps: Press ⌘, and choose "Billing".
Under "Payment", read each saved card line with its "Default" badge and "Expires" date.
Click "Manage cards" to change or remove a card in the billing portal.
Compare the default card, update and remove options with Expected.
items.needs: a saved card on a paid or Stripe-billed account
items.note: Removing or changing a card happens in the billing portal; no remove control was found in the app code.

items.needs: a paid checkout or a Stripe billing portal session
items.note: The billing address form is collected on the Stripe checkout page (tax-policy.ts sets billing_address_collection to 'required'); I found no in-app billing address field, and searched apps/web for 'billing address'.

items.needs: a business buyer account and a paid checkout
items.note: Tax identifier collection is enabled on Stripe checkout (apps/web/lib/billing/tax-policy.ts); I found no in-app tax ID field, and searched apps/web for 'Tax ID' and 'VAT'.

items.where: Finish a paid checkout > Billing > You're all set.
steps: Complete a paid upgrade on the Stripe checkout page.
Return to the app; it opens Billing with success in the address.
Wait for the page to update the plan.
Read the heading "You're all set." and the plan name beside it, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Free account and a completed paid checkout
items.note: The heading in the code is written with an HTML entity for the apostrophe.

items.where: Settings > Billing (past-due notice)
steps: Use an account whose renewal failed, press ⌘, and choose "Billing".
Read the red notice at the top of the page.
Read the text "Your last ... payment didn't go through" and the status "past due" or "unpaid".
Check that the notice shows how to fix it with the buttons "Pay" and "Update payment method", and compare with Expected.

labels.text: Your last {planLabel} payment didn’t go through

items.note: The notice is shown only for past-due or unpaid Stripe-billed plans.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Update payment method
steps: Use an account with a failed payment and open Settings > Billing.
In the red notice, click "Update payment method" (or the "Pay" link for the open invoice).
Complete the payment in the billing portal or on the invoice page.
Return to Billing and check that the notice is gone and the status is active, as Expected says.
items.needs: a paid account with a failed payment
items.note: The payment-failure page button "Open billing" leads to /settings/billing.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Invoices (and Settings > Billing > Credit history)
steps: Press ⌘, and choose "Billing".
Scroll to the "Invoices" heading and read the table.
Scroll to the "Credit history" heading and read its rows.
Compare the lists with Expected: past bills and credit purchases.
items.needs: a paid account with invoices and credit purchases
items.note: A Free account shows only empty-state text; the invoice list is also at /billing/invoices.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Invoices > Pay / View
steps: Open Settings > Billing and scroll to "Invoices".
Find an invoice row with a link labelled "Pay" or "View".
Click the link; it opens the hosted invoice in a new tab.
On /billing/invoices, check the "PDF" link in the "Invoice" column and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account with an issued invoice
items.note: The Settings link opens the hosted invoice page; the PDF file link is on the invoices page.

items.where: Settings > Billing (payment history table, column "Receipt")
steps: Open Settings > Billing with an account that has bought credits or paid a top-up.
Find the payment history table and its "Receipt" column.
Click the receipt link for a payment.
Check that a receipt exists for each payment, including credit purchases, and compare with Expected.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Resume button in the scheduled-cancellation notice

Check that the notice disappears and the plan continues, and compare with Expected.

items.where: Settings > Billing (notice "Your ... plan ends on ...")

Read the notice that starts "Your ... plan ends on" and the date after it.
Check the "Price" and status rows below the notice, and compare with Expected.

items.where: Settings > Billing (notice "You keep ... features and credits until then")

Check the sentence "You keep ... features and credits until then" and what it says happens after: the account moves to Free and chats, projects and files stay.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Manage in the App Store / Manage on Google Play
steps: Use an account whose subscription was bought in the App Store or Google Play.
Open Settings > Billing.
Read the text about the store billing the plan and the button "Manage in the App Store" or "Manage on Google Play".

items.where: Settings > Billing > Upgrade plan > choose a paid plan (warning appears when checkout is refused)

Open "Upgrade plan" from Settings > Billing and choose a paid plan.

items.where: Workspace > Members (seat counts appear on Workspace > Billing under "Plan and seats")

Click "Members" to see the people list, roles and invitations.
Click "Billing" in the same Workspace area and read the "Plan and seats" section.
Compare the "Seats used" row (for example "N of M") with the members list and the seat assignment controls.

items.where: Workspace > Billing, then the "Enterprise contract" section and its "Contacts" part
steps: Sign in as an enterprise organization admin and open Workspace, then Billing.

Read the "Contacts" part.
Compare "Billing contact" and "Procurement contact" with the names on record; a missing one shows the not-on-record text.

steps: Sign in as an enterprise organization admin and open Workspace, then Billing.
In the "Enterprise contract" section, read the "Payment terms" and "Purchase order" rows.
Scroll to the "Invoices" section and read the recent invoices, newest first.
Compare the purchase order number and payment terms with the order form on record.

Scroll to the "Credit history" section.
Find rows labelled "Top-up purchase" for credit purchases.
Compare each purchase row with the credits bought and the date.

items.where: Settings > General > Preferences > Display Language

steps: Open Settings > Appearance.
Find the Accent colour row of colour circles.

items.needs: none

items.where: Settings > General > Preferences > Default model
