Click Delete Key on the test key, read the warning, and confirm. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The UI calls revoking a key Delete Key, and the code does not show a masked key value; this was not confirmed in code.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > open a connector > Tool Permissions (Always run without asking, Needs approval each time, Never run this tool; Reset all to default)
steps: Open Settings and click Connectors.
Open a connected connector and click Tool Permissions.
Look at each tool's current level, and change one to Always run without asking or Never run this tool.
Click Reset all to default and confirm the reset. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a connected connector with tools
items.note: The phrase Saved approvals appears only in the VS Code extension locale (packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/vscode.json), not in the web app.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Default approval for tool actions
steps: Open Settings and click Capabilities.
Find Default approval for tool actions and pick Ask before every action, Run read-only actions without asking, or Skip approvals.
Read the Saved and Synced to your account status after each change.
Start a chat that runs a tool and check whether it asks. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account (Skip approvals is blocked when the workspace does not allow it)
items.note: The option labels are Ask before every action, Run read-only actions without asking and Skip approvals, not the names in Expected; enforcement is in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-approval-policy.ts.

items.where: Settings > Security > Advanced Account Security > Turn on Advanced Account Security
steps: Open Settings, click Security, and find the Advanced Account Security card.
Read its description: for accounts at higher risk, sign-in needs a passkey or security key.
Click Turn on Advanced Account Security after entering the code from the email, and read the result.
Check that password and email-code sign-in stop working, then click Turn off Advanced Account Security to undo it if the test allows. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a passkey or security key, and access to the account email
items.note: The hardened mode is the Advanced Account Security card, and the support article and recovery files are not UI.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Overview
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin of a Team or Enterprise workspace.
Open Settings, then the Workspace tab, then click Workspace administration.
The page opens on Overview. Read the workspace name shown as the large heading.
Read the line under it that gives the time of the live read and the count of items needing attention.
Scroll the signal cards: Identity, Provisioning, Access (Members, Pending invitations, Seats), AI controls, Data, Residency and keys, Audit, Usage and spend.
Compare with Expected: name, members/seats and security posture should match the live workspace.
items.needs: an owner or admin account on a Team or Enterprise workspace
items.note: The plan name is in the posture data but the overview does not show it as a line; check Billing for the plan. The Settings opener from the main screen was not confirmed (the command palette has a Settings entry at packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:96).

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Members
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin.
Open Settings > Workspace, then click Workspace administration.
Click Members in the left menu.
Find the card titled Members and read each row: the name, the email under it, and the role.
Compare with Expected: every workspace member should appear with name, email and role.
items.needs: an owner or admin account on a Team or Enterprise workspace

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Members > Invite teammate
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, open Members, and find the Invite teammate card.
Type an email in Email address, pick a role in Role, then click Create invitation.
Check that a private invitation link appears and the seat count goes down.
Find Pending invitations. Click New link to renew one, or Revoke to cancel one, and confirm the dialog.
Open the invitation link as the invitee (the Accept invitation button) and check the invitee joins with the chosen role.
items.needs: an owner or admin account, and a second account with the invited email address
items.note: The invitee screen is at the invite page (apps/web/app/invite/page.tsx).

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Roles > Groups
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Roles in Workspace administration.
Scroll to the Groups card and read each group name and its member count.
To create one, type a name in New group name and click Create group.
Tick roles for a group and click Save group.
Compare with Expected: groups show members, and roles on a group are saved. A synced group says it is managed by its source and is read-only for its name and members.
items.needs: an owner or admin account; a directory-synced group for the synced case
items.note: Group creation and role saving are in WorkspaceRoles.tsx; the sync itself is run from the Identity page (Directory sync).

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Roles
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Roles.
Read the Roles card: each role and its permissions.
Read the Additional roles card to see which extra roles each member holds.
Go to Members, open a member's role select, choose another role, then click Change role in the confirm dialog.
Compare with Expected: the member's role changes. Then sign in as that member and check that the server now allows or refuses the matching actions.
items.needs: an owner or admin account and a second member account

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Roles > New role
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Roles.
Click New role, type a name, tick permissions, then click Create role.
Click Edit on the role to change it, or Delete and confirm Delete role to remove it.
In Additional roles, tick the custom role for a member, then click Save roles.
Compare with Expected: the role appears with its permissions. Sign in as the member and check the permission takes effect.
items.needs: an owner or admin account and a second member account

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Members > Seats & billing
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Members.
In the Seats & billing card read Licensed, In use and Available.
Invite a member or remove one and see whether In use goes up or down.
Click Change seats (or Review contract for contract-priced workspaces) to see how seats are added.
Compare with Expected: the three numbers match the seats and members, and seats change as members come and go.
items.needs: an owner or admin account on a paid Team or Enterprise workspace
items.note: Change seats opens the public pricing page, which is outside the console.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Members > Workspace ownership
steps: Sign in as the current owner and open Members.
In the Workspace ownership card, choose a member in Member to receive ownership.
Click Transfer ownership, then read the Transfer ownership? dialog and confirm.
Read the Ownership transferred message that follows.
Compare with Expected: the new owner holds the owner role and the old owner gets the chosen role. Check the change from the other account.
items.needs: the owner account and a second member account
items.note: The exact condition that shows this card was not fully traced; it is rendered inside the Members page.

items.where: Workspace administration > Identity > Single sign-on (SAML / OIDC) > Email domain
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, open Identity in Workspace administration.
In Single sign-on (SAML / OIDC), type a company domain in Email domain and click Add connection.
Copy the TXT record shown (Record type, Record name, Record value) and publish it in the domain's DNS.
Click Verify domain.
Compare with Expected: the status changes from Domain not verified to Domain verified, and only then is sign-in routed for that domain.
items.needs: an owner or admin account, a company domain they control, and access to its DNS
items.note: The status label Domain verified is in the same file (line 40).

items.where: Workspace administration > Identity > Single sign-on (SAML / OIDC) > Add connection
steps: Sign in as the workspace owner, open Identity, and find Single sign-on (SAML / OIDC).
After the domain is verified, choose a Protocol: SAML 2.0 or OIDC.
Fill the provider fields (IdP metadata URL for SAML; OIDC discovery URL, client ID and client secret for OIDC), then click Add connection.
Check the connection appears with its provider type and domain.
Sign in as a member on that domain through the identity provider and check it works.
items.needs: an owner account, a verified domain, and a test SAML or OIDC identity provider
items.note: Whether sign-in through the provider works is checked at sign-in, not on this console page.

items.where: Workspace administration > Identity > Directory sync (SCIM 2.0)
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, open Identity, and find Directory sync (SCIM 2.0).
Under Connections, fill the form and click Add connection.
Under SCIM tokens, choose a Connection, type a Token name and click Mint token. Copy the token shown.
Set up the identity provider with the token; create, change and remove a test user there.
Compare with Expected: the member is created, updated and removed (deprovisioned) in the workspace, and Recent IdP activity lists the events.
items.needs: an owner or admin account and a test identity provider that supports SCIM 2.0

items.where: Workspace administration > Identity > Service principals (disable); Workspace administration > Audit > Workspace API keys (keys)
steps: Open Identity and find the Service principals card; read each name, its permissions and its created date.
Click Disable on a principal, then confirm Disable principal. Check that the button now says Enable.
Open Audit, find Workspace API keys, and click Create key with scopes and an expiry (the No expiry option is there).
Click Revoke on a key and confirm Revoke key.
Compare with Expected: a disabled principal and a revoked key stop working for automations, and keys keep working after their creator leaves.
items.needs: an owner or admin account; an automation or test client that uses a key
items.note: A service principal is created with the first workspace API key, so creating one goes through Create key.

items.where: Workspace administration > Models
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Models.
In Providers, click Block on a provider (or Approve on one to allow it).
In Models, use Filter models, click Approve or Block on a model, then click Save model policy.
Sign in as a member, open chat, and try to pick the blocked model.
Compare with Expected: the blocked model is refused; the page says Auto never reaches a blocked model.
items.needs: an owner or admin account and a member account
items.note: The refusal message seen by a member was not traced in this pass; watch the chat when testing.

items.where: Workspace administration > Policy > Allow (feature) switches > Save features and defaults
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Policy.
Find the Allow switches (for example Allow Skills or Allow Plugins) and turn one off.
Click Save features and defaults.
Under Exceptions, add an exception for a person or group and click Save exception if needed.
Compare with Expected: the switched-off feature is refused for members in the product (for example in chat or the desktop app).
items.needs: an owner or admin account and a member account
items.note: The refusal is checked in the feature itself (chat, Code, desktop), not on this page.

items.where: Workspace administration > Connectors > Catalog connectors
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Connectors.
Under Catalog connectors, open a connector and set Read-only tools and Write tools to Always allow, Needs approval or Blocked.
Click Save policy.
Sign in as a member and use that connector's read and write tools in chat.
Compare with Expected: an allowed tool runs, a tool set to Needs approval asks first, and a blocked tool is refused.
items.needs: an owner or admin account, a member account, and a connected connector

items.where: Workspace administration > Connectors > Catalog connectors > Block
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Connectors.
Under Catalog connectors, click Block on a connector, then click Save policy.
Sign in as a member and look for that connector in the connectors list.
Try to connect it.
Compare with Expected: the blocked connector is not offered and cannot be connected. Repeat for Custom connectors (Allow custom connectors switch).
items.needs: an owner or admin account and a member account

items.where: Workspace administration > Connectors > Plugins > Approve
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Connectors.
In the Plugins card, type a plugin name and click Approve (or Block), then click Save policy.
Optionally, on Policy, turn the Skills or Plugins switch off and click Save features and defaults.
Sign in as a member and look at the plugins and skills they can install or use.
Compare with Expected: an approved plugin can be used, a blocked one cannot, and a switched-off feature is refused.
items.needs: an owner or admin account and a member account
items.note: Per-item control exists for plugins only on this page; skills are switched as a whole on Policy.

items.where: Workspace administration > Plugins > Publish a plugin or a skill
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Plugins.
In Publish a plugin or a skill, click Upload a plugin or skill and choose a plugin .zip (or a skill .zip with SKILL.md).
Wait for the scan to finish; accept any findings if asked, then check the plugin is listed in Workspace plugins.
Sign in as a member and look for the plugin under Plugins.
Compare with Expected: the member can browse and install the workspace's own plugin; Retire for everyone removes it.
items.needs: an owner or admin account, a member account, and a plugin or skill .zip file

labels.text: Publish a plugin or a skill

items.note: Separation from the public directory was not checked in this pass.

items.where: Workspace administration > Sharing > Shared projects
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Sharing.
Under Shared projects, read each shared project and who has access.
Open the project's sharing controls to see each member's access: Can view, Can edit or No access.
Click Stop sharing on a project and confirm it.
Compare with Expected: the project leaves Shared projects, and the members lose access to it.
items.needs: an owner or admin account, a shared project, and a member account
items.note: The per-member access controls live in the project sharing component; how to open them from this console page was not fully traced.

items.where: Workspace administration > Policy > Public sharing
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Policy.
In the Public sharing card, turn Allow public sharing off, then click Save policy.
Sign in as a member and try to create a new public share link for a chat.
Compare with Expected: the share is refused and no new external link is created while the switch is off.
items.needs: an owner or admin account and a member account
items.note: No separate external-sharing switch was found; the Public sharing card is the closest control. Confirm the mapping with the owner.

items.where: Workspace administration > Policy > Public sharing
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Policy.
In the Public sharing card, turn Allow public sharing off, then click Save policy.
Sign in as a member and try to publish a chat or an artifact publicly.
Compare with Expected: publishing is refused while the switch is off.
items.needs: an owner or admin account and a member account with a chat or artifact
items.note: This is the same card as S87.20.

items.where: Workspace administration > Policy > Memory
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Policy.
In the Memory card, turn Allow memory off, then click Save policy.
Sign in as a member and open Settings > Memory.
Compare with Expected: the member sees memory turned off and no memory is used in chats.
items.needs: an owner or admin account and a member account

items.where: Workspace administration > Policy > Retention window
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Policy.
In Retention window, set the days in Retention window in days.
Turn on Enforce the retention window (in the Enforce retention card) and confirm if asked.
Read the card text: chats idle for that many days are deleted each night, except under legal hold.
Check the Data page sweeps table (Retention by data type) after a run.
Compare with Expected: the setting is saved and the nightly sweep follows it. Deletion is permanent, so use only test data.
items.needs: an owner or admin account and test conversations older than the window
items.note: The Data page also has Retention by data type with its own Save button; the code sits on the Policy page for this item.

items.where: Workspace administration > Data > Data region
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Data.
In Data region, read the line Stored in <region>.
Choose a region in Move to, then click Request move and confirm.
Check the line that says a move was requested and that data stays in the current region until the move completes.
Compare with Expected: the request is recorded; a Cancel the move button is shown while it is pending.
items.needs: an Enterprise workspace (choosing a region needs an active Enterprise plan) and an owner or admin account
items.note: Partly built: the audit says the EU region infrastructure is not yet set up and the owner decision is open, so an EU move may not complete.

items.where: Workspace administration > Data > Encryption key
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Data.
In Encryption key, choose a provider (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS or Azure Key Vault), paste the key identifier and click Connect key.
Click Rotate and confirm Rotate key, then check Last rotated changes.
Click Revoke, enter a reason, then confirm Revoke key.
Compare with Expected: rotation and revocation are recorded and the status text changes; a refused state shows the server message instead of the controls.
items.needs: an owner or admin account and a customer-managed key in AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS or Azure Key Vault
items.note: Where this is offered (plan or region gating) was not traced; the page shows the server's refusal message when it is not offered.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Controls > Policy, then the row IP allow list
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin. Open Settings, then the Workspace pane, then click Workspace administration.
Under Controls, click Policy.

Scroll to the row IP allow list. Click the field Add an IP address or CIDR block, type a test range you can reach (for example 203.0.113.0/24) and press Enter. A range that leaves out your own address can lock you out.
Look at the text under IP allow list: it should say Members may only sign in to this workspace from one of these addresses or blocks.
Compare with Expected. A sign-in from an address outside the list should be refused, which needs a second network to check.
items.needs: an owner or admin account (the console is limited to owners and admins); a second network to test a refused sign-in
items.note: The refusal rule runs on the server (apps/web/lib/ip-allow-list-gate.ts), so the screen only shows the list; how the first screen opens Settings was not traced.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Records > Audit, then the card Audit trail
steps: Open Records > Audit. Find the card titled Audit trail.
Open the All actions list and pick one action.
Open the Outcome and severity filters and pick a value in each.
Look at the table columns When, Actor, Action, Resource, Surface and Outcome. Only matching rows should stay and the count line should change.
Compare with Expected: filters should work on live data.
items.needs: an owner or admin account; some audit events already in the workspace
items.note: No time-range filter was found in WorkspaceAuditSection.tsx, so the time-range part of Expected is not visible on this card.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Records > Audit, button Export JSONL (switch: Controls > Policy, row Audit export)
steps: Open Controls > Policy and find the row Audit export. Check that the switch Allow audit export is on.
Open Records > Audit. Set filters if you want a smaller export.
Click Export JSONL. The browser downloads a file.
Open the file. Each line should be one audit event.
Compare with Expected: the export should be recorded. Check the Audit trail for a new event. The SIEM streaming card on the same page needs an HTTPS endpoint to test.
items.needs: an owner or admin account; a browser that saves downloads
items.note: The card text says exporting is recorded in the trail; whether the export event actually appears was not traced in code.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Records > Usage
steps: Open Records > Usage. Click 7 days, 30 days or 90 days at the top to change the period.
Read the card Managed cloud usage: Credits used, Active members, Turns, Tokens in and Tokens out.
Scroll to the tables By member, By product area, By model and By provider. Check that each lists rows.
Click Export daily CSV and open the downloaded file.
Compare with Expected. The page says only settled Cloud usage is counted; Local and BYOK activity is not included.
items.needs: an owner or admin account; some Cloud usage in the chosen period
items.note: The export is a daily CSV only; no export by model, provider or product area was found.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Records > Usage, then scroll to the card Monthly spend limit
steps: Open Records > Usage and scroll to the bottom card Monthly spend limit.
Type a monthly amount in credits in the cap field and set the percent next to Alert at.
Pick a value in Spend limit enforcement (Off, Notify or Block) and read the line under it.
Click Set limit (or Update limit if a limit exists).
Compare with Expected: the limit should show against spend. With Block, a managed turn past the cap should be refused, which needs spend close to the cap to test.
items.needs: an owner or admin account; managed usage near the cap to see a refusal
items.note: Controls > Policy also has a row named Monthly spend cap (apps/web/features/settings/sections/WorkspacePolicySection.tsx); how the two relate was not traced.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Records > Billing
steps: Open Records > Billing.
Read the card Plan and seats: the plan, the Seats used count and the seat note.
Read the card Manage billing. It says payment, invoices and plan changes are in billing settings. Click Billing settings to go there.
Compare with Expected. The page shows plan and seats, and a contract panel for contract-priced plans; payment, invoices and plan changes are not made on this page.
items.needs: an owner or admin account; a contract-priced plan to see the contract panel
items.note: Expected says the console manages payment method, invoices and contract terms. The code shows a summary with a link to billing settings, plus WorkspaceEnterpriseContract.tsx, whose visible text was not read.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Records > Data, then the card Legal holds, then Export records on a hold row
steps: Open Records > Data and find the card Legal holds.
Pick a hold in the list. If none exists, create one first with Place a hold (see S87.37).
Click Export records on that hold. The browser downloads the records held for it.
Open the file and check it holds conversations, messages, files or artifacts in a machine-readable format.
Compare with Expected. Export is offered per legal hold only; a whole-workspace export was not found.
items.needs: an owner or admin account; an existing legal hold
items.note: Expected asks for a full workspace export of conversations, messages, files and artifacts. The only export found is HoldExportLink in WorkspaceDataControls.tsx; the file types it includes were not traced.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Records > Data, then the card Legal holds
steps: Open Records > Data and find the card Legal holds.
Click Place a hold. Pick a scope in Legal hold scope (whole workspace or one member), type a name and reason, then click Place hold.
Check that the new row shows Placed with a date and either Whole workspace or Member.
Click Release hold, read the confirmation, then choose Keep hold to cancel or Release hold to confirm.
Compare with Expected: a released hold shows Released. Look at the Retention sweeps card to check that held records were not deleted while the hold was active.
items.needs: an owner or admin account (placing and releasing is limited to owners and admins); a member account for the member scope
items.note: The protection of held data from the sweep is enforced on the server; the screen shows only the sweep record.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Controls > Policy, then scroll to Explain a member’s policy
steps: Open Controls > Policy and scroll past the policy sections to Explain a member’s policy.
Pick a member.
Pick a request in the request list, or keep No request, show the policy only. For a country check, type a two-letter code such as US in the country field.
Click Explain.
Compare with Expected. The result starts with Allowed. or Refused. and lists the allowed countries and surfaces, with the reason when refused.
items.needs: an owner or admin account; a member with at least one restriction to see a refusal

labels.text: No request, show the policy only

items.note: The file writes the heading with the entity ’, which shows as a curly apostrophe.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Records > Audit, then the card Workspace API keys
steps: Open Records > Audit and scroll to Workspace API keys.
Type a name in the key name field, pick an expiry (30 days, 90 days, 1 year or No expiry), and tick at least one scope.
Click Create key. Copy the key shown under Copy the key now.
Find the key in the list. It shows its scopes, Last used and Expires.
Click Revoke, read the confirmation, and confirm. Compare with Expected: the key should show scopes and an expiry, and after Revoke it should show Revoked.
items.needs: an owner or admin account; an integration to try the key (optional)
items.note: Scope names come from the server list (grantableScopes) and are not written in this file. No documented API page was found, and the item was not checked against a live key.

items.where: Settings > Memory > "How memory works" link
steps: Open Settings and go to the Memory section.
Find the link "How memory works" under the memory description.
Click "How memory works".
Check that a help article about memory opens and matches the Memory screen.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The Memory section name in the settings menu was not checked; the link itself is in the code.

items.where: Settings > Help > "Help center"
steps: Open Settings and go to Help.
Click "Help center" (it opens in a new tab).
Type a word into the search box on the Help center page and press Enter.
Check that matching articles appear with snippets and links, then click one and check it opens.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Search every help article, or browse the help centre by collection.

items.note: The search box placeholder text was not found as a literal in the files read.

items.where: Settings > Help > "Contact support"
steps: Open Settings and go to Help.
Look at the support tickets panel at the top of the Help section.
Click "Contact support" (opens in a new tab).
Check that the support page opens where you can describe a problem; check that replies to a ticket appear with a "Send reply" form.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Only the path to the form was checked; the form itself was not traced.

items.where: Settings > Help > "Report a bug"
steps: Open Settings and go to Help.
Click "Report a bug" (opens in a new tab at the support page, bugs section).
Describe a problem in the bug part of the support page.
Check that the page mentions build and platform details being sent with the report.
items.needs: none
items.note: The exact wording of the bug form fields was not found; diagnostics collection is in apps/web/lib/support/diagnostics/collect.ts.

items.where: Feedback > Feedback type > "Send feedback" (in the chat composer)
steps: Open a chat.
Click the "Feedback" button near the composer.
Leave the Feedback type on the general option and type a note.
Click "Send feedback" and check that a confirmation appears.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Where the general Feedback button sits was not traced exactly. The plan marks this item as unfinished on mount.

items.where: Feedback > Feedback type > "Feature request" > "Send feedback" (in the chat composer)
steps: Open a chat.
Click the "Feedback" button near the composer.
Under "Feedback type", choose "Feature request".
Type a request and click "Send feedback"; check that a confirmation appears.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Same trigger as S88.05; the plan marks this item as unfinished on mount.

items.where: Settings > Help > "Review diagnostics" > "Download diagnostics"
steps: Open Settings and go to Help.
Keep the box "Attach diagnostics: your build, platform and the last few errors this browser recorded." ticked, or untick it.
Click "Review diagnostics" and read the summary in the box labelled "Diagnostics that would be attached".
Click "Download diagnostics" and check the file contents match the summary.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Sharing with support is done through the ticket form in the same panel; the send control was not traced.

items.where: Chat > a reply that fails > the error notice under the reply
steps: Open a chat and send a message in a way that makes the reply fail (for example with the network turned off).
Read the error notice under the reply.
Look for the reference id in the notice text.
Compare it with the reference shown in the message details.
items.needs: a way to make a reply fail
items.note: The reference wording is built by withTurnErrorReference in apps/web/features/chat/lib/turn-error-notice.ts; its exact visible text was not found as a literal.

items.where: Settings > Help > "System status"
steps: Open Settings and go to Help.
Click "System status" (opens the status page in a new tab).
Read the page title "Status: hosted dependency and route checks" and the current status rows.
Compare the rows with what the app shows in the composer footer.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Status: hosted dependency and route checks

items.note: The composer footer status feed (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFooter.tsx) has no visible wording that was checked.

items.where: A notice card near the top of the app while an incident is active
steps: Sign in while an incident notice is active and look at the top of the app.
Check that the notice card shows the problem and its status.
items.needs: an active incident notice (set by the team)
items.note: Notices come from the service notices feed (apps/web/lib/server/service-notices.ts); the visible wording comes from data, not fixed text.

items.where: A notice card in the app before and during planned maintenance
steps: Sign in while a maintenance notice is scheduled and look at the top of the app.
Check that the maintenance notice shows the planned time.
items.needs: a scheduled maintenance notice (set by the team)
items.note: Maintenance notices use a clock icon (apps/web/shared/components/ServiceNotices.tsx); the wording comes from data.

items.where: A banner at the top of the app that starts with "What's new:" after an update
steps: Sign in after a new release is published, or clear the saved last-seen release value in the browser to test again.
Read the banner "What's new:" followed by the headline.
Click the banner link and check it opens the release notes for that release.
Click the dismiss control and check the banner goes away.
items.needs: a new release in the release feed
items.note: The banner shows only when a release has not been seen in this browser.

items.where: Composer footer > model picker: a row that reads "Leaving" a model, or a notice that says "is no longer available"
steps: Open a chat that uses a model marked as retiring.
Look at the model picker in the composer footer for the row that reads "Leaving" the model name.
Look at the notice that says the model "is no longer available" and says which model replaces it.
Click the dismiss control on the notice and check it closes.
items.needs: a model marked as retiring or retired in the catalogue
items.note: The model picker row wording is built from data ("Leaving" plus the model short name), so it depends on the catalogue state.

items.where: Settings > Memory > import dialog (choose a source, pick a file, then preview)
steps: Open Settings and go to Memory.
Open the memory import dialog.
Choose a source such as "ChatGPT", then choose a .txt or .json file.
Check the preview step lists what will be imported before you confirm the import.
items.needs: a .txt or .json file to upload
items.note: The button that opens the import dialog was not found as a literal; the dialog itself is in apps/web/features/settings/components/ImportMemoryDialog.tsx.

items.where: Settings > Privacy > rights-request link > "Exercise your rights." page
steps: Open Settings and go to Privacy.
Find the link to rights requests and click it.
On the "Exercise your rights." page, read the "Your requests" list if you have any.
Check each listed request shows its reference, type (Access, Correction or Erasure) and status.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The link text on the Privacy page was not found; the request form was not traced.

items.where: "Cookie preferences" (cookie preference centre, opened from the cookies page or the cookie banner)
steps: Open "Cookie preferences" from the cookies page or the cookie banner.
Turn analytics off and keep necessary cookies on, then save.
Reload the page and open "Cookie preferences" again.
Check analytics is still off and necessary is still locked on, and no banner returns.
items.needs: none
items.note: The save button's visible text was not found; network-level enforcement is not checked here.

items.where: Under a chat reply: "Report this response"
steps: Open a chat with a reply.
Find "Report this response" on the reply.
Click it and check the message "Reported. Thank you: our trust and safety team will review it." appears.
Check the report button shows it was sent and cannot be sent again.
items.needs: a chat reply
items.note: The success text is in the same file as the code, around line 1189.

items.where: Browser address bar: /copyright/report (copyright report form)
steps: Open /copyright/report in a browser.
Read the legend "What you are reporting" and choose the type of report.
Fill in the reporter fields and submit.
Check the result shows "recorded" with a reference number.
items.needs: none (a link to the form was not found in the app)
items.note: No in-app link to the copyright form was found; the form is reached by its address only.

items.where: Under a refused chat reply: "Report issue" > "Submit report"
steps: Get a chat reply that the provider refuses for safety reasons.
Find the notice under the refused reply and click "Report issue".
Describe the refusal and click "Submit report".
Check a confirmation appears.
items.needs: a refused reply (needs a safety refusal from the provider)
items.note: The refusal notice text was not found as a literal; it is shown from ChatMessageList.tsx when a refusal finishes.

items.where: Sign-in screen for a suspended account: "Submit appeal" (or "Why should the suspension be lifted?")
steps: Sign in to a suspended account, or open the appeal page at /appeal.
Read the account access notice that explains the suspension.
Type a reason under "Why should the suspension be lifted?" and click "Submit appeal".
Check the appeal thread shows your appeal and the note "A person reviews every appeal."
items.needs: a suspended account (or the appeal page)

labels.text: Why should the suspension be lifted?

items.note: Only the appeal path was traced; the suspension reason text is not a fixed literal.

items.where: Browser address bar: /security (section "Reporting a vulnerability.")
steps: Open /security in a browser.
Scroll to the section "Reporting a vulnerability.".
Read the reporting instructions and the contact the page names.
Check /.well-known/security.txt also opens and lists a contact.
items.needs: none
items.note: The security.txt route is in apps/web/app/.well-known/security.txt/route.ts; no in-app link was checked.

steps: Open /accessibility in a browser.
Scroll to the section "Report a barrier.".
Read how to report an accessibility barrier and the channel it names.
Check the channel can be used without a mouse (keyboard and screen reader).

items.note: No in-app link to the accessibility page was found; the support panel has accessibility text at SupportTicketsPanel.tsx line 583 that was not traced.

steps: Open Settings and go to Help.
Click "Legal" (it opens the legal page in a new tab).
Open a policy and find the "Previous versions" link under its date.
Click it and check earlier dated versions of the policy and what changed are listed.
items.needs: none
items.note: The version history page is apps/web/app/legal/archive/[policy]/page.tsx.

steps: Open /subprocessors in a browser.
Read the page title "Subprocessors." and the "Last updated:" line.
Read the list of subprocessors.
Check the change log link (to /changelog) is present.

items.note: No in-app link to the subprocessors page was found in the Help section.

steps: Open /trust in a browser.
Read the heading and the section "Audit reports".
Read the "SOC 2" and "ISO 27001" rows, which say no report is held.
Compare with Expected: the page states no reports or certificates are published yet.

items.where: Settings > Help > Legal > India: DPDP notice (the EU representative page is reached the same way through the Legal page, or from the footer Legal list)
steps: Sign in, open Settings, and choose the Help tab.
Click the Legal item (it opens the /legal page).
Find and click the India: DPDP notice link. Check that the page titled Notice to Data Principals in India. loads and shows the DPDP Act, 2023 notice.

Go back to Legal and click EU representative. Check that the page says no representative is currently appointed under Article 27 GDPR, with the date-stamped status text and where to send privacy requests.
items.needs: none
items.note: Expected says notices appear automatically for users in a jurisdiction; the code has no location check. The India and EU pages are fixed pages reached by link, and the plan's Where line 'not written yet' is out of date. I did not trace the route from the first screen into Settings, and I found no region-block notice in the code.

items.where: Type /developers in the address bar after signing in (no menu link to it was found), then the "Projects" card > "Create project"
steps: After signing in, type /developers in the address bar and press Return.
Find the card with the "Projects" heading and the name field.
Type a project name. Optionally fill "Monthly limit in credits".
Click "Create project".
Look for the new project in the card's list and compare with Expected (a project that scopes keys, usage and limits). No control to create an organization was found on this page.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The Developer console has no link in the account menu or primary rail; it was found only at /developers. No organization-creation control was found, only projects.

items.where: Type /developers in the address bar, then the "API Keys" card > "New Key"
steps: Type /developers in the address bar and press Return.
In the "API Keys" card, click "New Key".
Enter a "Key Name", pick "Scopes", optionally a "Project" and an "Expires" choice, then submit.
Read the new key once in the dialog, then close it.

In the key list, check the masked key, the "Created" date and "Last used" date, then click the trash button labelled "Delete <key name>" and confirm "Delete Key". Compare with Expected (scoped key, expiry, masked, last used, revoke).
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The UI says Delete, not Revoke. The removal confirm text is "Delete Key" and its aria-label is "Delete <name>".

items.where: Workspace console > Records > Audit > "Create key" (creates a service principal with the first workspace API key); list and disable under Workspace console > Identity > "Service principals"
steps: Sign in as a workspace admin and open the workspace console (Settings > Workspace > "Workspace administration").
Open Records > Audit and find the "Workspace API keys" card.
Enter a name, choose scopes, then click "Create key"; copy the key shown once.
Open Identity and find the "Service principals" list; check the new principal and its permissions.
Click "Disable" on a principal, confirm in the dialog, then check the button changes to "Enable" and the row shows "Disabled". Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a workspace admin account on a workspace that allows workspace API keys (Team or Enterprise)
items.note: No separate create-principal control was found; principals are created implicitly by the first workspace API key. Identity is in the console nav, which I did not confirm as a grouped heading.

items.where: Type /developers in the address bar, then the "Reference" card > "Models"
steps: Type /developers in the address bar and press Return.
Scroll to the "Reference" card and click "Models".
On the Models page read the model cards: each shows "Context" and capability chips.
Use the "Capabilities" filter buttons and check the list narrows.
Compare with Expected (models your key can call, with capabilities and context size).
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The page description says every model the plan can reach; I did not confirm it filters by the key's scopes.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > General > "Custom commands" > "New command"
steps: Open the account menu and choose "Settings", then the "General" pane.
Scroll to "Custom commands" and click "New command".
Fill "Name", "Description" and the "Template" field (it takes one user-text placeholder).
Click "Create command".
In a chat, type / and look for the new command in the slash menu; check that the placeholder is filled with the text you typed.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The template takes a single user-text token, not named arguments. The Prompts card on /developers ("Prompts and evaluations") is a separate feature.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > "Usage" (settings pane)
steps: Open the account menu, choose "Settings", then "Usage".
Read "Where your usage went" and the "Group usage history by" control; choose "Days", "Weeks" or "Months".
Read the "By model" table for the period.
Compare the figures across periods with Expected (usage and cost over time, broken down by model).
items.needs: a signed-in account with some usage
items.note: The pane reports credits, not a currency cost; the "By model" table appears only when history exists.

items.where: Type /developers in the address bar, then the "Rate limits" card
steps: Type /developers in the address bar and press Return.
Scroll to the "Rate limits" card.
Read each row in "Request limits by endpoint": endpoint, requests per window, and whether it counts per account or per IP.
Compare with Expected (see the limits and how close the account is to them).
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The panel lists the limits only; I did not find a used-versus-limit figure, so "how close" may not be shown.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > "Workspace administration" > Usage > "Monthly spend limit"
steps: Open Settings, choose the "Workspace" pane and click "Workspace administration".
Open Records > Usage and scroll to "Monthly spend limit".
Enter a cap, choose "Notify" or "Block" under "Spend limit enforcement", then click "Set limit".
Read the usage meter ("% of the monthly limit used") and check the cap shows.
Optionally click "Remove limit" and confirm, then check the message says spending is no longer capped. Compare with Expected (an owner's spend cap the API enforces).
items.needs: a workspace owner account on a workspace
items.note: Enforcement by the API is not visible from the UI. The owner-only check was not confirmed in this component. A personal "Monthly spend limit" also exists in Settings > Usage (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx).

items.where: Type /developers in the address bar, then the "Webhooks" card > "Add endpoint"
steps: Type /developers in the address bar and press Return.
In the "Webhooks" card, click "Add endpoint".
Enter the "Endpoint URL" and an optional "Description", tick the events under "Events", then click "Add endpoint" in the dialog.
Copy the signing secret from the "Copy the signing secret now" dialog and close it.
Check the endpoint appears in the "Webhook endpoints" list with its events. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account and an HTTPS URL you control

items.where: Type /developers in the address bar, then the "Webhooks" card > an endpoint > "Recent deliveries" > "Resend"
steps: Type /developers in the address bar and press Return.
In the "Webhooks" card, pick an endpoint from "Webhook endpoints" (or use "Send test event").
Read the "Recent deliveries" list: each row shows its status.
Click "Resend" on one delivery.
Check a new row appears with ", resent" after its details. Compare with Expected (delivery history with status and redeliver).
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one webhook endpoint
items.note: The redeliver control is labelled "Resend", not "Redeliver". How an endpoint is picked in the list was not fully traced.

items.where: Type /developers in the address bar, then the "Reference" card > "API docs" > scroll to "SDKs."
steps: Type /developers in the address bar and press Return.
In the "Reference" card, click "API docs".
Scroll to the "SDKs." heading and read the Python and TypeScript tabs.
Compare with Expected (documentation for official client SDKs).

items.note: The page says there is no AGI SDK; it documents OpenAI's official Python and TypeScript libraries pointed at the AGI base URL. Differs from Expected's wording.

Scroll to the "Reference." heading and follow its link to the bundle.
Click "OpenAPI bundle" on the /developers Reference card and check it lists endpoints. Compare with Expected (every public endpoint, credential and scope).

items.where: Type /developers in the address bar, then the "Reference" card > "API docs" > "Quick start" tabs "curl", "Python", "TypeScript"

Find the "Quick start" section.
Click the "curl" tab, then "Python", then "TypeScript".
Check each tab shows a copyable example. Compare with Expected (curl, Python and TypeScript examples).

items.where: Type /developers in the address bar, then the "Reference" card > "Migration guides"
steps: Type /developers in the address bar and press Return.
In the "Reference" card, click "Migration guides".
Read the headings "From the OpenAI API", "From the Anthropic API" and "Between models".
Compare with Expected (migration guides for API and model changes and from other providers).

items.where: Type /developers in the address bar, then the "Reference" card > "Deprecations"
steps: Type /developers in the address bar and press Return.
In the "Reference" card, click "Deprecations".
Read the "Deprecations." section, which says models are announced before they go and points to deprecation_date in GET /models.
Compare with Expected (developers told ahead of time). The dated list is not on this page itself.

items.note: The page gives the rule and points to the models list for dates; the dated list itself was not found on this page.

items.where: Settings > Help > "Raise ticket" (also the /support page's "Raise a ticket" button)
steps: Open the account menu, choose "Settings", then "Help".
Find the support ticket form and fill it in.
Click "Raise ticket".
Check the ticket appears in the list with replies. Compare with Expected (a support channel reachable from the product).
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Ticket creation is from the Help pane; the account menu's "Email support" is a mail link.

items.where: Settings > "Plugins" > "Upload plugin" (or "Create a plugin")
steps: Open the account menu, choose "Settings", then "Plugins".
Click the "Upload plugin" action in the list toolbar.
Choose a plugin archive file and submit (the "Upload" button).
Read the result and check the plugin appears in your list without being published. Compare with Expected (load an unpublished plugin into your own account).
items.needs: a plugin archive file on disk
items.note: The upload route is wired on the web adapter; I did not verify that an uploaded plugin stays private to the account.

items.where: Settings > "Plugins" > open your plugin > "Submit to the directory"
steps: Open the account menu, choose "Settings", then "Plugins".
Open one of your plugins from the list.
Click "Submit to the directory" and confirm "Submit for review".
Check the status shows a pending submission, with "Withdraw" available.
Use "Switch version" to choose an installed version. Compare with Expected (submit for review and publish versions).
items.needs: a plugin you own
items.note: Submit-for-review is traced. Publishing a new version to users was not clearly found; "Switch version" changes an installed version, and review is by moderators.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Slack app > Slack workspaces you added > Add to Slack, then message AGI in Slack
steps: Open Settings and choose Slack app under Customize.
In the card Slack workspaces you added, click Add to Slack, and finish the install on Slack's own page.
In Slack, open a direct message with the AGI app and send a message such as hello.
Look at the DM: the assistant's reply should appear in that same DM, and compare it with Expected.
items.needs: a Slack workspace where you can add apps, the Slack app set up by the owner first (see the code note)
items.note: The Slack reply happens inside Slack, not in the AGI screens; the code marks this item unfinished until the owner creates the Slack app and applies migration 0333; the way into Settings from the first screen was not located in the code.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Slack app > Slack workspaces you added (read the text there), then in Slack use /invite in a channel
steps: Open Settings, choose Slack app under Customize, and read the card Slack workspaces you added: it says to add the app, then /invite it to channels.
In Slack, type /invite and the app name in a channel to add the app to that channel.
Post a normal message in that channel and wait for the agent to act.
Check the channel for the agent's reply, and check Settings > Customize > Slack app > Waiting for your approval for any request, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Slack workspace where you can add apps and invite them to a channel, the Slack app set up by the owner first
items.note: The channel reply and action happen in Slack; the owner must create the Slack app and apply migration 0333 first, and the code is marked partial.

items.where: In Slack, @mention the app in a channel message; then in AGI open Settings > Customize > Slack app > Waiting for your approval
steps: In a Slack channel where the app is invited, write a message that mentions the app with a request.
In AGI, open Settings > Customize > Slack app and look at the card Waiting for your approval.
Find the item that says A task from a channel mention, and click View task if it appears.
Compare with Expected: the channel message should now be a task the agent runs.
items.needs: a Slack channel where the app is invited, the Slack app set up by the owner first

labels.text: A task from a channel mention

items.note: The task is listed in that card only when the run needs approval; the link View task appears only when a task path exists, and where the task shows otherwise was not confirmed in the code.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Slack app > Your Slack accounts; the agent's own name is seen in Slack
steps: Open Settings, choose Slack app under Customize, and read the card Your Slack accounts: it says accounts AGI answers as you.
In Slack, mention the app in a channel with a short request.
Read the reply in Slack and compare its sender name with your own name.
Compare with Expected: the agent should answer under its own app identity, not as you.
items.needs: a Slack workspace where the app is installed and a Slack account of your own, the Slack app set up by the owner first
items.note: The bot identity is shown by Slack, and the code that sets it was not checked against Slack's display; the item is marked partial in the code.

items.where: Scheduled page (route /chat/schedules, page title Scheduled) > schedule card > Run History button
steps: Open the Scheduled page.
On a schedule card, click the history icon button (its tooltip says Run History).
Read the section Run History that opens under the card.
Compare with Expected: work started from a channel or host should be listed there for review.
items.needs: a paid account with at least one schedule that has run
items.note: The sidebar label for the Scheduled page was not found in the code; whether channel runs appear in this list was not confirmed by reading the code.

items.where: Open the sitemap page (apps/web route /sitemap-page) > Gallery. Public routes /gallery and /plugins also exist.
steps: Sign out, then open the sitemap page at /sitemap-page in the browser.
Click Gallery under its list of links.
Check that the curated examples page opens without signing in.
Check the example cards and directory content are set by the product team, not by users, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The cited GalleryClient.tsx line numbers no longer hold the quoted code; no visible nav button labelled Gallery was found in the marketing nav, so the sitemap page is the only visible path I could confirm. Plugins page heading is 'Workflow packs, not loose parts.'

items.where: Open a shared link (/share/<token>) > Open in AGI
steps: Sign in, then open a public shared conversation link (/share/<token>).
Click Open in AGI in the top right of the header.
Wait for the page /chat/from-share/<token> to create your own conversation.
Send a new message in your own conversation and check it continues with the copied messages, compare with Expected.

items.note: The copy step runs in apps/web/app/chat/from-share/[token]/ContinueSharedSession.tsx; I did not find its visible wording in the render, so the exact on-screen text while copying is unknown.

items.where: Gallery > choose a category card > fill in the creation wizard > send (prompt opens in /chat)
steps: Open the gallery page at /gallery.
Click an example card or category, then fill in the wizard that opens.
Submit the wizard, which opens /chat with the prompt added as starterPrompt.
Check the prompt sits in the composer ready to send, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The exact button label that sends the wizard prompt was not found; the link from a public example to the wizard is in GalleryClient.tsx, and the template page is apps/web/app/gallery/[templateId]/page.tsx.

items.where: Open a shared link (/share/<token>) > the line under the title that starts with Shared by
steps: Open a public shared conversation link (/share/<token>) while signed out.
Look under the title for the line Shared by and the model badge.
Check the message count and Expires line also appear.
Compare with Expected: publisher and source shown, and check for copied-from or version information.
items.needs: none
items.note: The viewer shows Shared by and the model only; I did not find copied-from, author or version wording in this viewer. The line is shown only when the share has a shared_by value.

items.where: A public share page (/share/<token>) > Report infringement or impersonation. For an AI answer: the answer's menu > Report this response.
steps: Open a public shared conversation link (/share/<token>) and scroll to the bottom.
Click Report infringement or impersonation and check the notice form opens.
In a chat, open the menu on an AI answer and click Report this response.
Check for the toast Reported. Thank you: our trust and safety team will review it., and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account for the AI answer report
items.note: The menu that opens Report this response was not confirmed; the AI-answer report goes to /api/content-report and the share-page link goes to the copyright notice form, which feeds a different queue.

items.where: Plugins > open a plugin's detail > Submit to the directory
steps: Open a plugin you created, then its detail view.
Look for the button Submit to the directory under the plugin details.
Click it and confirm in the dialog that opens.
Check the plugin shows as submitted and is named, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a plugin you created in the account

labels.text: List a plugin in the directory

items.note: The panel that holds the directory list was not confirmed by its visible label; the public partners page at /partners describes the submission path. I did not check that the publisher name is shown.

steps: Sign in.
Type /chat/finance in the browser address bar and press Enter.
Look for the heading Finances, then the Accounts section.
Compare the accounts and the total under Spending with the Expected line: accounts, balances and spending in one view.

steps: Open /code in the address bar.
Start a new session and choose Code Interpreter.
Click Add cell, type a short Python line, then click Run all.
Run all again and compare the output with Expected (same result on re-run).

items.note: The /code route is not in the sidebar; the exact control for choosing the template was not confirmed. The environment is not version-pinned in the UI code read.

items.where: Sidebar > Study
steps: Click Study in the sidebar.
Type a topic in the box, choose the level and mode, then click Start studying.
Look for guided, one-idea-at-a-time study in the session.
Compare with Expected: a teacher or learner workspace with classes and assignments.
items.needs: none
items.note: No classes or assignments screen was found; Study is topic-based. The CODE line target apps/web/features/study/lib/study-session.ts was not re-read.

items.where: Sidebar > Study, then Start studying
steps: Click Study in the sidebar.
Type a subject and choose a level, then click Start studying.
Look for a study plan generated for the topic.
Compare with Expected: objectives, activities and materials.
items.needs: none
items.note: A study plan request exists in the code; the objectives, activities and materials structure was not confirmed in the UI code read.

items.where: Chat > type / in the message box > Skills group > pipeline-review
steps: Click Chat in the sidebar.
Type / in the message box and find the Skills group.
Choose pipeline-review (or deal-review) and send a request about your pipeline.
Compare the answer with Expected: looking up and updating contacts, deals and pipelines.
items.needs: a CRM connector connected in Settings
items.note: The CRM connection step was not located; updates to contacts were not confirmed in code read.

items.where: Chat > type / in the message box > Skills group > ticket-triage
steps: Click Chat in the sidebar.
Type / in the message box and find the Skills group.
Choose ticket-triage, paste a ticket, and send.
Compare the answer with Expected: triage, reply drafting and ticket updates (draft-response and customer-escalation are in the same group).
items.needs: a support ticket text to paste; a support connector for updates
items.note: Ticket updates through a support system were not confirmed in the code read.

items.where: Chat > type / in the message box > Skills group > recruiting-pipeline
steps: Click Chat in the sidebar.
Type / in the message box and find the Skills group.
Choose recruiting-pipeline or interview-prep and send a request.
Compare the answer with Expected: job posts, candidate pipeline and interview plans.
items.needs: none
items.note: Job posting publication was not found in the code read.

items.where: Chat > type / in the message box > Skills group > marketing-plan
steps: Click Chat in the sidebar.
Type / in the message box and find the Skills group.
Choose marketing-plan (also seo-audit, social, analytics are in .agents/skills) and send a request.
Compare the answer with Expected: audiences, campaigns, assets and analytics.
items.needs: none; analytics connectors for live data
items.note: Cited vendor-directory lines and skills-lock entries were not all re-read; live analytics connection not confirmed.

items.where: Chat: ask the assistant to compare products in the message box
steps: Click Chat in the sidebar.
Type a request to compare two or three products by specs and price, and send.
Look for a product comparison card with specs, prices and merchants.
Click View product on a row and compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: No comparison button exists; the card appears when the assistant chooses the comparison tool.

items.where: Chat: ask the assistant to plan a trip in the message box
steps: Click Chat in the sidebar.
Type a trip request (places and a route) and send.
Look for an itinerary card with stops and a map.
Open a directions link (for example Walking directions in Google Maps) and compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: Reservations are not made by the itinerary tool; the code says booking needs a travel or booking connector (apps/web/lib/places/itinerary-tool.ts), not confirmed in UI.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Slack app > "Add to Slack" (then message AGI in Slack)
steps: Sign in to the web app and open Settings.
Under Customize, click "Slack app".
In the "Slack workspaces you added" card, click "Add to Slack". Slack's install page opens in the browser.
Approve the app in Slack. Come back to Settings and look for the message "AGI was added to Slack. Send it a message there to start."

In Slack, send AGI a direct message or mention it in a channel after /invite-ing it. Click the link it sends to connect your Slack account, then check that "Your Slack accounts" in Settings lists your account and that AGI answers in the thread.
items.needs: a Slack workspace where you can add apps, and a Slack account; the app must be configured by the owner first (see note)
items.note: Partly built: the Slack routes exist (apps/web/app/api/webhooks/slack/route.ts, apps/web/lib/slack/slack-config.ts) but the owner still has to create the Slack app and set SLACK_APP_CLIENT_ID, SLACK_APP_CLIENT_SECRET and SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET, and migration 0333 must be applied. Teams, WhatsApp and Telegram have no chat-with-AGI path in the code: they appear only as connectors (Settings > Customize > Connectors, apps/web/features/connectors/data/connectors.ts), which send and read messages but do not answer a person there. The step that opens the Settings modal from the first screen was not confirmed in code; the modal title "Settings" is in packages/ui/ui/src/settings-modal/SettingsModal.tsx.

items.where: Open a chat answer that holds a document > open the document as an artifact > Edit document
steps: Ask the assistant in chat to write a document, for example a short memo, and wait for it to finish.
Open the document artifact from the chat.
Click the Edit button (aria-label "Edit document").
Change some text in the document.
Click the save control (title "Save as a new version").
Look for the new version in the artifact's version controls and compare with Expected: the edit is saved back as a new version.
items.needs: none
items.note: The Edit and save controls were found; the version list label was not confirmed.

items.needs: a document
items.note: Searched apps/web/features and apps/web/lib for presentation, slide, deck and convert labels. Only a prompt-based 'Slide deck' starter in apps/web/features/projects/components/ProjectStudio.tsx was found, with no control that converts an existing document into a presentation.

items.needs: a spreadsheet file to upload
items.note: Found apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts, which gates on AGI_E2B_EXECUTION and E2B_API_KEY. No visible chart or report control was found for this flow, so the path is unknown.

items.needs: a finished research report
items.note: Checked apps/web/features/chat/lib/visual-intent.ts and apps/web/features/chat/utils/research-plan.ts. No visible control for converting a report to an interactive page was found. The Publish button exists in apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx, but it is not confirmed as this feature.

items.needs: a microphone and a Free or paid account
items.note: Found the voice tool files under apps/web/lib/voice/ (live-voice-tools.ts). No visible voice control that creates a tracked work task was found, so the path is unknown.

items.needs: a microphone
items.note: Found apps/web/lib/voice/live-voice-tools.ts and apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceModeSurface.tsx. No visible label tying a voice request to a generated document was found.

items.needs: an outside account (Google) with Gmail connected
items.note: Found a Gmail trigger labelled 'Gmail' in apps/web/features/schedules/components/ScheduleTriggersPanel.tsx (line 75), which runs for each new email. The path from the app to that panel and the thread-to-task step were not confirmed.

items.needs: a team with a repository and the coding feature enabled
items.note: Searched apps/web/features/code and apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts. The feature depends on AGI_E2B_EXECUTION and E2B_API_KEY. No visible label for a team mention flow was found.

items.needs: a design file and a repository
items.note: Searched apps/web/features/code and apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts. The feature depends on AGI_E2B_EXECUTION and E2B_API_KEY. No visible label for a design-to-implementation flow was found.

items.where: Chat > the answer's More message actions menu > Save as skill
steps: Finish a task in chat so the answer is complete.
Click the More message actions button on that answer.
Click Save as skill.
Look at the plugin draft card and confirm the skill is saved.
Open the skills list in settings and check that the skill appears, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a finished task
items.note: The draft card label 'Save as a skill' is in apps/web/features/chat/components/PluginDraftCard.tsx. The settings path to the skills list was not confirmed.

items.where: Web chat sidebar and the phone app's conversation list
steps: Start a chat in the web app and send a message.
Open the same conversation on the phone app and check that the full history is there.
Send a follow-up from the phone.
Reload the web app and check that the reply appears in the same conversation.
items.needs: a signed-in account on web and the phone app
items.note: The effect is in the sync and persistence routes (apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts and persist-message.ts), not a control of its own.

items.needs: a finished cloud coding session
items.note: Found apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts. The feature depends on AGI_E2B_EXECUTION and E2B_API_KEY. No visible label for bringing a cloud result into a local checkout was found.

items.where: Chat > composer > Project or folder > pick the project
steps: Open the main chat.
Click the Project or folder control in the composer.
Search for or pick an existing project.
Ask a question that the project's sources should answer.
Check that the answer uses the project's sources, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a project with sources
items.note: A chat is scoped to a project or a local folder, never both, per the comment in WebChatPage.

items.where: Chat > an answer's More message actions > Save to project > pick the project
steps: Open a chat with a finished answer.
Click the More message actions button on the answer.
Click Save to project.
Pick the project name from the list.
Open that project and check that the answer is listed as a source, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a project
items.note: Artifacts also have a 'Save to project' group in apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx. The project list in the project was not confirmed.

items.where: Chat > send a message after the usage limit is reached > inline card
steps: Use up the account's usage, or use an account that is already out of usage.
Send a new message in chat.
Look at the inline card that appears under the message.
Click Switch to (the named model) to continue, or Buy credits.
Check that the reply continues, compared with Expected.
items.needs: an account that has run out of usage
items.note: The 'Switch to' label is a template string in the same file, and the exact trigger was not reproduced.

items.where: Settings > Published artifacts > History
steps: Publish an artifact with the Publish button in the artifact panel.
Edit the artifact and publish again to the same link.
Open Settings and find the Published artifacts section.
Click History on the artifact row.
Check that the new version is listed and can be restored, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a published artifact
items.note: The settings navigation label was not confirmed.

items.where: Shared artifact link > Save a copy to my chats
steps: Sign in with a second account.
Open a shared artifact link from the first account.
Click Save a copy to my chats.
Open the copy in your own chats.
Continue the copy and check that it is private to your account, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a second account and a shared artifact link

labels.text: Save a copy to my chats

items.note: The label comes from a translation key with this fallback text. The continue-chat page is apps/web/app/chat/from-share/[token]/page.tsx.

steps: Open the workspace console and click Sharing.

Pick an access level, such as Can view or Can edit.
Sign in as another member and open the shared resource.
Check the member can find and open it, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a second member in the same workspace
items.note: The route from the sidebar to the workspace console was not confirmed. Access labels Can view and Can edit are in apps/web/features/projects/components/ProjectSharingControls.tsx.
